4.s: etadvo 'bhihitaṃ sarvaṃ vidhānaṃ pāñcayajñikam dvijātimukhyavṛttīnāṃ vidhānaṃ śrūyatāmiti
4.d: एतद्वो ऽभिहितं सर्वं विधानं पाञ्चयज्ञिकम् द्विजातिमुख्यवृत्तीनां विधानं श्रूयतामिति

4.s: caturthamāyuṣo bhāgamuṣitvā 'dyaṃ gurau dvijāḥ dvitīyamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ kṛtadāro gṛhe vaset
4.d: चतुर्थमायुषो भागमुषित्वा ऽद्यं गुरौ द्विजाः द्वितीयमायुषो भागं कृतदारो गृहे वसेत्
4.e: Having dwelt, during the first quarter of his life, with the Teacher, the Brāhmaṇa shall, during the second quarter of his life, live in his house, after having taken a wife.

4.s: adroheṇaiva bhūtānāmalpadroheṇa vā punaḥ yā vṛttistāṃ samāsthāya vipro jīvedanāpadi
4.d: अद्रोहेणैव भूतानामल्पद्रोहेण वा पुनः या वृत्तिस्तां समास्थाय विप्रो जीवेदनापदि
4.e: [While living in the house], The Brāhmaṇa shall, in normal times, subsist by taking to that means of livelihood which involves no trouble—or very little trouble—to living beings.

4.s: yātrāmātraprasiddhiarthaṃ svaiḥ karmabhiragarhitaiḥ akleśena śarīrasya kurvīta dhanasañcayam
4.d: यात्रामात्रप्रसिद्धिअर्थं स्वैः कर्मभिरगर्हितैः अक्लेशेन शरीरस्य कुर्वीत धनसञ्चयम्
4.e: For the accomplishment of bare maintenance, one shall accumulate wealth by means of one’s own irreproachable occupations, without causing trouble to the body.

4.s: ṛtāmṛtābhyāṃ jīvet tu mṛtena pramṛtena vā satyānṛtābhyāmapi vā na śvavṛttyā kadā cana
4.d: ऋतामृताभ्यां जीवेत् तु मृतेन प्रमृतेन वा सत्यानृताभ्यामपि वा न श्ववृत्त्या कदा चन
4.e: He shall live in “Truth” and “Nectar,” or by “Death” and “Super-death;” or, even by “Truth and Falsehood;” but never by the “living of the dog.”

4.s: ṛtamuñchaśilaṃ jñeyamamṛtaṃ syādayācitam mṛtaṃ tu yācitaṃ bhaikṣaṃ pramṛtaṃ karṣaṇaṃ smṛtam
4.d: ऋतमुञ्छशिलं ज्ञेयममृतं स्यादयाचितम् मृतं तु याचितं भैक्षं प्रमृतं कर्षणं स्मृतम्
4.e: Gleaning and picking is to be known as “Truth;” and what is obtained unasked, “Nectar”; alms obtained by begging is “Death,” and cultivation is declared to be “Super- death.”

4.s: satyānṛtaṃ tu vāṇijyaṃ tena caivāpi jīvyate sevā śvavṛttirākhyātā tasmāt tāṃ parivarjayet
4.d: सत्यानृतं तु वाणिज्यं तेन चैवापि जीव्यते सेवा श्ववृत्तिराख्याता तस्मात् तां परिवर्जयेत्
4.e: Trade is “Truth and Falsehood;” even by that one may live. Service has been declared, to be the “living of dogs;” hence one should avoid it.

4.s: kusūladhānyako vā syāt kumbhīdhānyaka eva vā tryahehiko vā 'pi bhavedaśvastanika eva vā
4.d: कुसूलधान्यको वा स्यात् कुम्भीधान्यक एव वा त्र्यहेहिको वा ऽपि भवेदश्वस्तनिक एव वा
4.e: He shall be either one possessing a granary full of grains, or one possessing a jar full of grains; he may be one possessing what is wanted for three days, or one who does not possess enough for the morrow.

4.s: caturṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ dvijānāṃ gṛhamedhinām jyāyān paraḥ paro jñeyo dharmato lokajittamaḥ
4.d: चतुर्णामपि चैतेषां द्विजानां गृहमेधिनाम् ज्यायान् परः परो ज्ञेयो धर्मतो लोकजित्तमः
4.e: Among these four Brāhmaṇa-householders, each later should be regarded as superior, and a superior winner of worlds by virtue of his merit.

4.s: ṣaṭkarmaiko bhavatyeṣāṃ tribhiranyaḥ pravartate dvābhyāmekaścaturthastu brahmasattreṇa jīvati
4.d: षट्कर्मैको भवत्येषां त्रिभिरन्यः प्रवर्तते द्वाभ्यामेकश्चतुर्थस्तु ब्रह्मसत्त्रेण जीवति
4.e: From among these one follows the six occupations; another lives by three; one again with two; while the fourth lives by “Brahmasattra.’

4.s: vartayaṃśca śilauñchābhyāmagnihotraparāyaṇaḥ iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇāntīyāḥ kevalā nirvapet sadā
4.d: वर्तयंश्च शिलौञ्छाभ्यामग्निहोत्रपरायणः इष्टीः पार्वायणान्तीयाः केवला निर्वपेत् सदा
4.e: ‘Living by gleanings and pickings, intent upon the performance of Agnihotra, one should constantly offer only those Iṣṭi-sacrificer that pertain to the moonless and full-moon days and to the solstices.—(10);

4.s: na lokavṛttaṃ varteta vṛttihetoḥ kathaṃ cana ajihmāmaśathāṃ śuddhāṃ jīvedbrāhmaṇajīvikām
4.d: न लोकवृत्तं वर्तेत वृत्तिहेतोः कथं चन अजिह्मामशथां शुद्धां जीवेद्ब्राह्मणजीविकाम्
4.e: He shall never follow the worldly way, for the sake of subsistence; he shall live the straightforward, sincere and pure life of the Brāhmaṇa.

4.s: saṃtoṣaṃ paramāsthāya sukhārthī saṃyato bhavet saṃtoṣamūlaṃ hi sukhaṃ duḥkhamūlaṃ viparyayaḥ
4.d: संतोषं परमास्थाय सुखार्थी संयतो भवेत् संतोषमूलं हि सुखं दुःखमूलं विपर्ययः
4.e: He who wants happiness should adopt perfect contentment and remain self-controlled. Happiness has its root in contentment, and its opposite is the root of unhappiness.

4.s: ato 'nyatamayā vṛttyā jīvaṃstu snātako dvijaḥ svargāyuṣyayaśasyāni vratāṇīmāni dhārayet svargyāyuṣya
4.d: अतो ऽन्यतमया वृत्त्या जीवंस्तु स्नातको द्विजः स्वर्गायुष्ययशस्यानि व्रताणीमानि धारयेत् स्वर्ग्यायुष्य
4.e: The twice-born Accomplished Student, living by any one of these means of livelihood, should keep these (following) observances, which are conducive to heaven, longevity and fame.

4.s: vedauditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryādatandritaḥ taddhi kurvan yathāśakti prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
4.d: वेदौदितं स्वकं कर्म नित्यं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः तद्धि कुर्वन् यथाशक्ति प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम्
4.e: He shall, without sloth, always perform his own duty as prescribed in the Veda. Performing that, to the best of his ability, he attains the highest state.

4.s: naihetārthān prasaṅgena na viruddhena karmaṇā na vidyamāneṣvartheṣu nārtyāmapi yatastataḥ na kalpamāneṣvartheṣu
4.d: नैहेतार्थान् प्रसङ्गेन न विरुद्धेन कर्मणा न विद्यमानेष्वर्थेषु नार्त्यामपि यतस्ततः न कल्पमानेष्वर्थेषु
4.e: He shall not seek wealth by clinging pursuits, or by contrary acts; nor when wealth is already there; nor from here and there, even in times of distress.

4.s: indriyārtheṣu sarveṣu na prasajyeta kāmataḥ atiprasaktiṃ caiteṣāṃ manasā saṃnivartayet
4.d: इन्द्रियार्थेषु सर्वेषु न प्रसज्येत कामतः अतिप्रसक्तिं चैतेषां मनसा संनिवर्तयेत्
4.e: He shall not, through desires, become addicted to any sensual objects; excessive addiction to these, he shall avoid by mental reflection.

4.s: sarvān parityajedarthān svādhyāyasya virodhinaḥ yathā tathā 'dhyāpayaṃstu sā hyasya kṛtakṛtyatā
4.d: सर्वान् परित्यजेदर्थान् स्वाध्यायस्य विरोधिनः यथा तथा ऽध्यापयंस्तु सा ह्यस्य कृतकृत्यता
4.e: He shall relinquish all things impeding study, maintaining himself somehow. This is what constitutes the accomplish ment of his aims.

4.s: vayasaḥ karmaṇo 'rthasya śrutasyābhijanasya ca veṣavācbuddhisārūpyamācaran vicarediha
4.d: वयसः कर्मणो ऽर्थस्य श्रुतस्याभिजनस्य च वेषवाच्बुद्धिसारूप्यमाचरन् विचरेदिह
4.e: He should wander about in this world, keeping his dress, speech and thoughts in conformity with his age, occupation, wealth, learning and family.

4.s: buddhivṛddhikarāṇyāśu dhanyāni ca hitāni ca nityaṃ śāstrāṇyavekṣeta nigamāṃścaiva vaidikān
4.d: बुद्धिवृद्धिकराण्याशु धन्यानि च हितानि च नित्यं शास्त्राण्यवेक्षेत निगमांश्चैव वैदिकान्
4.e: He shall always pore over such treatises as quickly enliven the intelligence, are conducive to wealth and are beneficial,—as also over the Vedic Scriptures.

4.s: yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ śāstraṃ samadhigacchati tathā tathā vijānāti vijñānaṃ cāsya rocate
4.d: यथा यथा हि पुरुषः शास्त्रं समधिगच्छति तथा तथा विजानाति विज्ञानं चास्य रोचते
4.e: For, as the man goes on studying a science, so does he go on understanding, and then his knowledge shines forth.

4.s: ṛṣiyajñaṃ devayajñaṃ bhūtayajñaṃ ca sarvadā nṛyajñaṃ pitṛyajñaṃ ca yathāśakti na hāpayet
4.d: ऋषियज्ञं देवयज्ञं भूतयज्ञं च सर्वदा नृयज्ञं पितृयज्ञं च यथाशक्ति न हापयेत्
4.e: To the rest of his power, he shall never omit the sacrifice to the sages, the sacrifice to the gods, the sacrifice to elementals, the sacrifice to men and the sacrifice to the Pitṛs.

4.s: etāneke mahāyajñān yajñaśāstravido janāḥ anīhamānāḥ satatamindriyeṣveva juhvati
4.d: एतानेके महायज्ञान् यज्ञशास्त्रविदो जनाः अनीहमानाः सततमिन्द्रियेष्वेव जुह्वति
4.e: Some persons, conversant with the ordinances relating to sacrifices, who do not cherish ant desires, regularly offer these great sacrifices into the sense-organs.

4.s: vācyeke juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe vācaṃ ca sarvadā vāci prāṇe ca paśyanto yajñanirvṛttimakṣayām
4.d: वाच्येके जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणे वाचं च सर्वदा वाचि प्राणे च पश्यन्तो यज्ञनिर्वृत्तिमक्षयाम्
4.e: Some people constantly offer their life-breath into speech, and their speech into the life-breath,—knowing that in speech and in life-breath rests the imperishable fulfilment of sacrifices.

4.s: jñānenaivāpare viprā yajantyetairmakhaiḥ sadā yajante tairmakhaiḥ sadā jñānamūlāṃ kriyāmeṣāṃ paśyanto jñānacakṣuṣā
4.d: ज्ञानेनैवापरे विप्रा यजन्त्येतैर्मखैः सदा यजन्ते तैर्मखैः सदा ज्ञानमूलां क्रियामेषां पश्यन्तो ज्ञानचक्षुषा
4.e: Other Brāhmaṇas, looking, with the eye of knowledge, upon this act as having its root in knowledge, always sacrifice with these sacrifices, by means of knowledge.

4.s: agnihotraṃ ca juhuyādādiante dyuniśoḥ sadā darśena cārdhamāsānte paurṇāmāsena caiva hi
4.d: अग्निहोत्रं च जुहुयादादिअन्ते द्युनिशोः सदा दर्शेन चार्धमासान्ते पौर्णामासेन चैव हि
4.e: He shall always offer the Agnihotra, either at the beginning, or, at the end, of day and night, as also the “Darśa” and the “Paurṇamāsa” at the end of each half-month.

4.s: sasyānte navasasyaiṣṭyā tathāṛtuante dvijo 'dhvaraiḥ paśunā tvayanasyādau samānte saumikairmakhaiḥ 'yanānte tu samāṃte
4.d: सस्यान्ते नवसस्यैष्ट्या तथाऋतुअन्ते द्विजो ऽध्वरैः पशुना त्वयनस्यादौ समान्ते सौमिकैर्मखैः ऽयनान्ते तु समांते
4.e: At the end of the grains, the Brāhmaṇa shall perform the “New-Harvest sacrifice;” at the end of the seasons, the “Adhvara-sacrifices;” at the end of the solstices the “Animal-sacrifice;” and at the end of the year the “Soma-sacrifices.”

4.s: nāniṣṭvā navasasyaiṣṭyā paśunā cāgnimān dvijaḥ navānnamadyātmāṃsaṃ vā dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ
4.d: नानिष्ट्वा नवसस्यैष्ट्या पशुना चाग्निमान् द्विजः नवान्नमद्यात्मांसं वा दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः
4.e: Without having performed the New-Harvest sacrifice, and the animal Sacrifice, the Brāhmaṇa, who has set up the fire, shall not eat new grain or meat,—if he desires to live a long life.

4.s: navenānarcitā hyasya paśuhavyena cāgnayaḥ prāṇānevāttumicchanti navānnāmiṣagardhinaḥ
4.d: नवेनानर्चिता ह्यस्य पशुहव्येन चाग्नयः प्राणानेवात्तुमिच्छन्ति नवान्नामिषगर्धिनः
4.e: For his Fires, greedy or n ew grains and meat, seek to devour his very life, if they are not worshipped with new grains and with meat.

4.s: āsanāśanaśayyābhiradbhirmūlaphalena vā nāsya kaścidvasedgehe śaktito 'narcito 'tithiḥ
4.d: आसनाशनशय्याभिरद्भिर्मूलफलेन वा नास्य कश्चिद्वसेद्गेहे शक्तितो ऽनर्चितो ऽतिथिः
4.e: No guest shall dwell in his house without being honoured, to the best of his ability, with seat, food, bed, or with water, fruits and roots.

4.s: pāṣāṇḍino vikarmasthān baiḍālavratikāṃśaṭhān haitukān bakavṛttīṃśca vācmātreṇāpi nārcayet
4.d: पाषाण्डिनो विकर्मस्थान् बैडालव्रतिकांशठान् हैतुकान् बकवृत्तींश्च वाच्मात्रेणापि नार्चयेत्
4.e: He shall not honour, even with speech, impostors, those who follow improper occupations, those who are cat-like in their behaviour, hypocrites, logicians, and those who behave like herons.

4.s: vedavidyāvratasnātāṃśrotriyān gṛhamedhinaḥ pūjayeddhavyakavyena viparītāṃśca varjayet
4.d: वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातांश्रोत्रियान् गृहमेधिनः पूजयेद्धव्यकव्येन विपरीतांश्च वर्जयेत्
4.e: He shall honour with offerings to gods and to Pitṛs, those Vedic scholars, who have become accomplished in the Veda, in learning and in the observances, as also house-holders; He shall, however, avoid those who are otherwise.

4.s: śaktito 'pacamānebhyo dātavyaṃ gṛhamedhinā saṃvibhāgaśca bhūtebhyaḥ kartavyo 'nuparodhataḥ
4.d: शक्तितो ऽपचमानेभ्यो दातव्यं गृहमेधिना संविभागश्च भूतेभ्यः कर्तव्यो ऽनुपरोधतः
4.e: The Householder shall give as much as he can to those who do not cook their own food; and, for the sake of all living beings, he shall make apportionment, without detriment (to himself).

4.s: rājato dhanamanvicchet saṃsīdan snātakaḥ kṣudhā yājyāntevāsinorvā 'pi na tvanyata iti sthitiḥ
4.d: राजतो धनमन्विच्छेत् संसीदन् स्नातकः क्षुधा याज्यान्तेवासिनोर्वा ऽपि न त्वन्यत इति स्थितिः
4.e: Suffering from hunger, the accomplished student should seek for wealth from the king, or from one at whose sacrificial rites he officiates, or from his pupil; and not from others; such is the rule.

4.s: na sīdet snātako vipraḥ kṣudhā śaktaḥ kathaṃ cana na jīrṇamalavadvāsā bhavecca vibhave sati
4.d: न सीदेत् स्नातको विप्रः क्षुधा शक्तः कथं चन न जीर्णमलवद्वासा भवेच्च विभवे सति
4.e: The Accomplished Brāhmaṇa shall not, if he can, suffer from hunger; nor shall he wear torn or dirty clothes, so long as he has any property.

4.s: kḷptakeśanakhaśmaśrurdāntaḥ śuklāmbaraḥ śuciḥ svādhyāye caiva yuktaḥ syānnityamātmahiteṣu ca
4.d: कॢप्तकेशनखश्मश्रुर्दान्तः शुक्लाम्बरः शुचिः स्वाध्याये चैव युक्तः स्यान्नित्यमात्महितेषु च
4.e: Keeping his hair, nails and beard clipped, subdued, wearing white clothes, pure,—he shall always remain engaged in Vedic study, also in what may be conducive to his welfare.

4.s: vaiṇavīṃ dhārayedyaṣṭiṃ saudakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum yajñopavītaṃ vedaṃ ca śubhaṃ raukme ca kuṇḍale
4.d: वैणवीं धारयेद्यष्टिं सौदकं च कमण्डलुम् यज्ञोपवीतं वेदं च शुभं रौक्मे च कुण्डले
4.e: He shall hold a stick of bamboo, and also a water-pot full of water, the sacred thread, a handful of kuśa-grass and a pair of bright golden ear-rings.

4.s: naikṣetaudyantamādityaṃ nāstaṃ yāntaṃ kadā cana naupasṛṣṭaṃ na vāristhaṃ na madhyaṃ nabhaso gatam
4.d: नैक्षेतौद्यन्तमादित्यं नास्तं यान्तं कदा चन नौपसृष्टं न वारिस्थं न मध्यं नभसो गतम्
4.e: He shall not look at the Sun when rising, nor when setting, nor when it is eclipsed, nor when it is in water, nor when it has reached the middle of the sky.

4.s: na laṅghayedvatsatantrīṃ na pradhāvecca varṣati na caudake nirīkṣeta svarūpamiti dhāraṇā
4.d: न लङ्घयेद्वत्सतन्त्रीं न प्रधावेच्च वर्षति न चौदके निरीक्षेत स्वरूपमिति धारणा
4.e: He shall not step over the rope to which a calf is tied; he shall not run when it is raining; he shall not look at his own figure in water; such is the established rule.

4.s: mṛdaṃ gāṃ daivataṃ vipraṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu catuṣpatham pradakṣiṇāni kurvīta prajñātāṃśca vanaspatīn
4.d: मृदं गां दैवतं विप्रं घृतं मधु चतुष्पथम् प्रदक्षिणानि कुर्वीत प्रज्ञातांश्च वनस्पतीन्
4.e: By a mound of clay, a cow, a deity, a Brāhmaṇa, clarified butter, honey, a cross-way and the well-known trees—he shall pass in such a manner as to leave them on his right.

4.s: naupagacchet pramatto 'pi striyamārtavadarśane samānaśayane caiva na śayīta tayā saha
4.d: नौपगच्छेत् प्रमत्तो ऽपि स्त्रियमार्तवदर्शने समानशयने चैव न शयीत तया सह
4.e: Even though mad, he shall not approach a woman during her courses; nor shall he sleep on the same bed with her.

4.s: rajasā 'bhiplutāṃ nārīṃ narasya hyupagacchataḥ prajñā tejo balaṃ cakṣurāyuścaiva prahīyate
4.d: रजसा ऽभिप्लुतां नारीं नरस्य ह्युपगच्छतः प्रज्ञा तेजो बलं चक्षुरायुश्चैव प्रहीयते
4.e: Of the man who approaches a woman covered with impurity,—intelligence, vitality, strength, sight and longevity wear off.

4.s: tāṃ vivarjayatastasya rajasā samabhiplutām prajñā tejo balaṃ cakṣurāyuścaiva pravardhate
4.d: तां विवर्जयतस्तस्य रजसा समभिप्लुताम् प्रज्ञा तेजो बलं चक्षुरायुश्चैव प्रवर्धते
4.e: Of that same man, if he avoids the woman covered with impurity, intelligence, vitality, strength, sight and longevity flourish.

4.s: nāśnīyādbhāryayā sārdhaṃ naināmīkṣeta cāśnatīm kṣuvatīṃ jṛmbhamāṇāṃ vā na cāsīnāṃ yathāsukham
4.d: नाश्नीयाद्भार्यया सार्धं नैनामीक्षेत चाश्नतीम् क्षुवतीं जृम्भमाणां वा न चासीनां यथासुखम्
4.e: He shall not eat with his wife; nor shall he look at her while she is eating, or snoring, or yawning, or sitting at her ease.

4.s: nāñjayantīṃ svake netre na cābhyaktāmanāvṛtām na paśyet prasavantīṃ ca tejaskāmo dvijottamaḥ
4.d: नाञ्जयन्तीं स्वके नेत्रे न चाभ्यक्तामनावृताम् न पश्येत् प्रसवन्तीं च तेजस्कामो द्विजोत्तमः
4.e: The brāhmaṇa, desiring brightness, shall not look at a woman who is a pplying collyrium to her own eyes, or who has anointed herself, or who is uncovered, or is bringing forth a child.

4.s: nānnamadyādekavāsā na nagnaḥ snānamācaret na mūtraṃ pathi kurvīta na bhasmani na govraje
4.d: नान्नमद्यादेकवासा न नग्नः स्नानमाचरेत् न मूत्रं पथि कुर्वीत न भस्मनि न गोव्रजे
4.e: He shall not eat food with only one piece of cloth on him; he shall not bathe naked; he shall not pass urine on the road, nor on ashes, nor on the haunts of cows.

4.s: na phālakṛṣṭe na jale na cityāṃ na ca parvate na jīrṇadevāyatane na valmīke kadā cana
4.d: न फालकृष्टे न जले न चित्यां न च पर्वते न जीर्णदेवायतने न वल्मीके कदा चन
4.e: Nor on ploughed land, nor in water, nor on an oven, nor on a mountain, nor in a ruined temple, nor on an ant-hill.

4.s: na sasattveṣu garteṣu na gacchannapi na sthitaḥ na nadītīramāsādya na ca parvatamastake
4.d: न ससत्त्वेषु गर्तेषु न गच्छन्नपि न स्थितः न नदीतीरमासाद्य न च पर्वतमस्तके
4.e: Nor in holes inhabited by living creatures, nor walking, nor standing, nor on reaching the banks of a river, nor on the mountain-top.

4.s: vāyuagnivipramādityamapaḥ paśyaṃstathaiva gāḥ na kadā cana kurvīta viṣmūtrasya visarjanam
4.d: वायुअग्निविप्रमादित्यमपः पश्यंस्तथैव गाः न कदा चन कुर्वीत विष्मूत्रस्य विसर्जनम्
4.e: One should never pass faeces or urine, while looking at the wind or fire, or a Brāhmaṇa, or the sun, or water, or cows.

4.s: tiraskṛtyauccaret kāṣṭhaloṣṭhapatratṛṇādinā tṛṇādi ca niyamya prayato vācaṃ saṃvītāṅgo 'vaguṇṭhitaḥ
4.d: तिरस्कृत्यौच्चरेत् काष्ठलोष्ठपत्रतृणादिना तृणादि च नियम्य प्रयतो वाचं संवीताङ्गो ऽवगुण्ठितः

4.s: mūtrauccārasamutsargaṃ divā kuryādudalgmukhaḥ dakṣiṇā 'bhimukho rātrau saṃdhyāyośca yathā divā
4.d: मूत्रौच्चारसमुत्सर्गं दिवा कुर्यादुदल्ग्मुखः दक्षिणा ऽभिमुखो रात्रौ संध्यायोश्च यथा दिवा
4.e: He shall pass it after placing a stick, or a clod, or leaves, or grass, or some such thing, restraining his speech, clean, his b ody wrapped and covered.

4.s: chāyāyāmandhakāre vā rātrāvahani vā dvijaḥ yathāsukhamukhaḥ kuryāt prāṇabādhabhayeṣu ca
4.d: छायायामन्धकारे वा रात्रावहनि वा द्विजः यथासुखमुखः कुर्यात् प्राणबाधभयेषु च
4.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

4.s: pratiagniṃ pratisūryaṃ ca pratisomaudakadvijam pratigu prativātaṃ ca prajñā naśyati mehataḥ pratigāṃ prativātaṃ
4.d: प्रतिअग्निं प्रतिसूर्यं च प्रतिसोमौदकद्विजम् प्रतिगु प्रतिवातं च प्रज्ञा नश्यति मेहतः प्रतिगां प्रतिवातं
4.e: In the shade, or in darkness, the Brāhmaṇa may—during the day or the night—do it, with his face towards any direction he pleases; as also where there is danger to life, and when there is fear.’

4.s: nāgniṃ mukhenaupadhamennagnāṃ naikṣeta ca striyam nāmedhyaṃ prakṣipedagnau na ca pādau pratāpayet
4.d: नाग्निं मुखेनौपधमेन्नग्नां नैक्षेत च स्त्रियम् नामेध्यं प्रक्षिपेदग्नौ न च पादौ प्रतापयेत्
4.e: He shall not blow fire with the mouth; nor shall he look at a naked woman. He shall not throw an unclean thing into fire; nor shall he warm his feet at it.

4.s: adhastānnaupadadhyācca na cainamabhilaṅghayet na cainaṃ pādataḥ kuryānna prāṇābādhamācaret
4.d: अधस्तान्नौपदध्याच्च न चैनमभिलङ्घयेत् न चैनं पादतः कुर्यान्न प्राणाबाधमाचरेत्
4.e: He shall not place fire under himself; nor shall he step over it; he shall not place it under his feet. He shall not do anything dangerous to life.

4.s: nāśnīyāt saṃdhivelāyāṃ na gacchennāpi saṃviśet na caiva pralikhedbhūmiṃ nātmano 'paharet srajam
4.d: नाश्नीयात् संधिवेलायां न गच्छेन्नापि संविशेत् न चैव प्रलिखेद्भूमिं नात्मनो ऽपहरेत् स्रजम्
4.e: At junction-time, he shall not eat, nor travel, nor sleep. He shall not scratch the ground; and he shall not remove his own garland.

4.s: nāpsu mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā ṣṭhīvanaṃ vā samutsṛjet amedhyaliptamanyadvā lohitaṃ vā viṣāṇi vā
4.d: नाप्सु मूत्रं पुरीषं वा ष्ठीवनं वा समुत्सृजेत् अमेध्यलिप्तमन्यद्वा लोहितं वा विषाणि वा
4.e: He shall not throw into water urine, or faeces, or spittings, or anything else contaminated by unclean things, or blood or poisons.

4.s: naikaḥ supyātśūnyagehe na śreyāṃsaṃ prabodhayet [śūnyagṛhe svapyān naudakyayā 'bhibhāṣeta yajñaṃ gacchenna cāvṛtaḥ
4.d: नैकः सुप्यात्शून्यगेहे न श्रेयांसं प्रबोधयेत् [शून्यगृहे स्वप्यान् नौदक्यया ऽभिभाषेत यज्ञं गच्छेन्न चावृतः
4.e: Alone he shall not sleep in a deserted house. He shall not offer advice to his superior. He shall not converse with a woman in her courses. He shall not go to a sacrifice uninvited.

4.s: agnyagāre gavāṃ goṣṭhe brāhmaṇānāṃ ca saṃnidhau svādhyāye bhojane caiva dakṣinaṃ pāṇimuddharet
4.d: अग्न्यगारे गवां गोष्ठे ब्राह्मणानां च संनिधौ स्वाध्याये भोजने चैव दक्षिनं पाणिमुद्धरेत्
4.e: In the abode of fire, in the cow-pen, in the presence of Brāhmaṇas, during the reading of Vedas, at the time of eating, he shall uncover his right hand.

4.s: na vārayedgāṃ dhayantīṃ na cācakṣīta kasya cit na divīndrāyudhaṃ dṛṣṭvā kasya ciddarśayedbudhaḥ
4.d: न वारयेद्गां धयन्तीं न चाचक्षीत कस्य चित् न दिवीन्द्रायुधं दृष्ट्वा कस्य चिद्दर्शयेद्बुधः
4.e: He shall not prevent a heifer while she is drinking, nor shall he point her out to anybody. Having seen the rainbow in the sky, the wise man shall not show it to any person.

4.s: nādharmike vasedgrāme na vyādhibahule bhṛśam naikaḥ prapadyetādhvānaṃ na ciraṃ parvate vaset
4.d: नाधर्मिके वसेद्ग्रामे न व्याधिबहुले भृशम् नैकः प्रपद्येताध्वानं न चिरं पर्वते वसेत्
4.e: He shall not dwell long in an unrighteous village, nor in one abounding in sickness. Alone, he shall not undertake a journey; nor shall he reside for long on a mountain.

4.s: na śūdrarājye nivasennādhārmikajanāvṛte na pāṣaṇḍigaṇākrānte naupasṣṛṭe 'ntyajairnṛbhiḥ
4.d: न शूद्रराज्ये निवसेन्नाधार्मिकजनावृते न पाषण्डिगणाक्रान्ते नौपस्षृटे ऽन्त्यजैर्नृभिः
4.e: He shall not dwell in a country with a Śūdra King; nor in one surrounded by unrighteous persons; nor in one occupied by impostors;. nor in one frequented by men of the lowest castes.

4.s: na bhuñjītauddhṛtasnehaṃ nātisauhityamācaret nātiprage nātisāyaṃ na sāyaṃ prātarāśitaḥ
4.d: न भुञ्जीतौद्धृतस्नेहं नातिसौहित्यमाचरेत् नातिप्रगे नातिसायं न सायं प्रातराशितः
4.e: He shall not eat anything from which oil has been extract ed; he shall not commit gluttony; he shall not eat very early in the morning, nor very late in the evening; nor in the evening, if he has eaten in the morning.

4.s: na kurvīta vṛthāceṣṭāṃ na vāryañjalinā pibet nautsaṅge bhakṣayedbhakṣyānna jātu syāt kutūhalī
4.d: न कुर्वीत वृथाचेष्टां न वार्यञ्जलिना पिबेत् नौत्सङ्गे भक्षयेद्भक्ष्यान्न जातु स्यात् कुतूहली
4.e: He shall not put forth any exertion without a purpose. He shall not drink water with joined hands. He shall not eat articles of food in his lap. He shall never be too curious.

4.s: na nṛtyedatha vā gāyenna vāditrāṇi vādayet na nṛtyennaiva gāyecca na vāditrāṇi vādayet nāsphoṭayenna ca kṣveḍenna ca rakto virāvayet na ca rakto virodhayet
4.d: न नृत्येदथ वा गायेन्न वादित्राणि वादयेत् न नृत्येन्नैव गायेच्च न वादित्राणि वादयेत् नास्फोटयेन्न च क्ष्वेडेन्न च रक्तो विरावयेत् न च रक्तो विरोधयेत्
4.e: He shall not dance, nor sing, nor play upon musical instruments, nor clap, nor grind his teeth, nor, when satisfied, shall he create enmity.

4.s: na pādau dhāvayet kāṃsye kadā cidapi bhājane na bhinnabhāṇḍe bhuñjīta na bhāvapratidūṣite
4.d: न पादौ धावयेत् कांस्ये कदा चिदपि भाजने न भिन्नभाण्डे भुञ्जीत न भावप्रतिदूषिते
4.e: He shall never wash his feet in a vessel of white brass. He shall not eat out of a broken dish; nor out of one that is felt to be defiled.

4.s: upānahau ca vāsaśca dhṛtamanyairna dhārayet upavītamalaṅkāraṃ srajaṃ karakameva ca
4.d: उपानहौ च वासश्च धृतमन्यैर्न धारयेत् उपवीतमलङ्कारं स्रजं करकमेव च
4.e: He shall not use shoes, on clothes, or sacred thread, or ornament, or garland, or water-pot, which has been used by others.

4.s: nāvinītairbhajeddhuryairna ca kṣudhvyādhipīḍitaiḥ nāvinītairvrajed na bhinnaśṛṅgākṣikhurairna vāladhivirūpitaiḥ
4.d: नाविनीतैर्भजेद्धुर्यैर्न च क्षुध्व्याधिपीडितैः नाविनीतैर्व्रजेद् न भिन्नशृङ्गाक्षिखुरैर्न वालधिविरूपितैः
4.e: He shall not travel with untrained beasts of burden; nor with such as are suffering from hunger or disease; nor with those whose horns, eyes or hoofs are injured; nor with those that are disfigured by their tails.

4.s: vinītaistu vrajennityamāśugairlakṣaṇānvitaiḥ varṇarūpaupasaṃpannaiḥ pratodenātudan bhṛśam pratodenākṣipan
4.d: विनीतैस्तु व्रजेन्नित्यमाशुगैर्लक्षणान्वितैः वर्णरूपौपसंपन्नैः प्रतोदेनातुदन् भृशम् प्रतोदेनाक्षिपन्
4.e: He should always travel with beasts that are trained, fast, equipped with signs, well endowed with colour and figure,—without striking them much with the goad.

4.s: bālātapaḥ pretadhūmo varjyaṃ bhinnaṃ tathā 'sanam na chindyānnakharomāṇi dantairnautpāṭayennakhān na cchindyān
4.d: बालातपः प्रेतधूमो वर्ज्यं भिन्नं तथा ऽसनम् न छिन्द्यान्नखरोमाणि दन्तैर्नौत्पाटयेन्नखान् न च्छिन्द्यान्
4.e: The young sun and the smoke from the dead body, should be avoided, as also a broken seat. He shall not cut his nails and hair, nob shall he tear his nails with his teeth.

4.s: na mṛtloṣṭhaṃ ca mṛdnīyānna chindyāt karajaistṛṇam cchindyāt na karma niṣphalaṃ kuryānnāyatyāmasukhaudayam
4.d: न मृत्लोष्ठं च मृद्नीयान्न छिन्द्यात् करजैस्तृणम् च्छिन्द्यात् न कर्म निष्फलं कुर्यान्नायत्यामसुखौदयम्
4.e: He shall not crush clods of earth; nor shall he cut grass with hi s nails. He shall not do an aimless act, nor one that is likely to lead to disagreeable results.

4.s: loṣṭhamardī tṛṇacchedī nakhakhādī ca yo naraḥ sa vināśaṃ vrajatyāśu sūcakā 'śucireva ca sūcako 'śucireva ca
4.d: लोष्ठमर्दी तृणच्छेदी नखखादी च यो नरः स विनाशं व्रजत्याशु सूचका ऽशुचिरेव च सूचको ऽशुचिरेव च
4.e: A man who crushes clods, cuts grass or bites his nails, quickly goes to perdition; so also the back-biter and the unclean man.

4.s: na vigarhya kathāṃ kuryādbahirmālyaṃ na dhārayet na vigṛhya kathāṃ kuryād gavāṃ ca yānaṃ pṛṣṭhena sarvathaiva vigarhitam
4.d: न विगर्ह्य कथां कुर्याद्बहिर्माल्यं न धारयेत् न विगृह्य कथां कुर्याद् गवां च यानं पृष्ठेन सर्वथैव विगर्हितम्
4.e: He shall hot carry on a wrangling conversatioh. He shall not wear a garland outside. Riding on the back of cows and oxen is altogether deprecated.

4.s: advāreṇa ca nātīyādgrāmaṃ vā veśma vā 'vṛtam rātrau ca vṛkṣamūlāni dūrataḥ parivarjayet
4.d: अद्वारेण च नातीयाद्ग्रामं वा वेश्म वा ऽवृतम् रात्रौ च वृक्षमूलानि दूरतः परिवर्जयेत्
4.e: He shall hot enter a walled village or house, except through the gate. At night, he shalt, keep away, at a long distance, from the roots of trees.

4.s: nākṣairdīvyet kadā cit tu svayaṃ naupānahau haret śayanastho na bhuñjīta na pāṇisthaṃ na cāsane
4.d: नाक्षैर्दीव्येत् कदा चित् तु स्वयं नौपानहौ हरेत् शयनस्थो न भुञ्जीत न पाणिस्थं न चासने
4.e: He shall never gamble with dice; he shall not himself carry his shoes; he shall not eat, seated on a bed; nor what has been placed in his hand or on the seat.

4.s: sarvaṃ ca tilasaṃbaddhaṃ nādyādastamite ravau na ca nagnaḥ śayītaiha na caucchiṣṭaḥ kva cidvrajet
4.d: सर्वं च तिलसंबद्धं नाद्यादस्तमिते रवौ न च नग्नः शयीतैह न चौच्छिष्टः क्व चिद्व्रजेत्
4.e: Any food containing sesamum, he shall not eat after sunset; he shall never sleep naked; nor go anywhere with mouth unwashed after meals.

4.s: ārdrapādastu bhuñjīta nārdrapādastu saṃviśet ārdrapādastu bhuñjāno dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt
4.d: आर्द्रपादस्तु भुञ्जीत नार्द्रपादस्तु संविशेत् आर्द्रपादस्तु भुञ्जानो दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात्
4.e: He shall eat with wet feet; but he shall not sleep with his feet wet. By eating with wet feet, one would attain long life.

4.s: acakṣurviṣayaṃ durgaṃ na prapadyeta karhi cit na viṣmūtramudīkṣeta na bāhubhyāṃ nadīṃ taret
4.d: अचक्षुर्विषयं दुर्गं न प्रपद्येत कर्हि चित् न विष्मूत्रमुदीक्षेत न बाहुभ्यां नदीं तरेत्
4.e: He shall never approach a place difficult of access, which is not within range of his vision; he shall not look at urine or excreta; nor shall he cross a river with his arms

4.s: adhitiṣṭhenna keśāṃstu na bhasmāsthikapālikāḥ na kārpāsāsthi na tuṣān dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ
4.d: अधितिष्ठेन्न केशांस्तु न भस्मास्थिकपालिकाः न कार्पासास्थि न तुषान् दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः
4.e: One who is desirous of living a long life, shall not step on hair, nor on ashes, bones and potsherds; or on cotton-seed or chaff.

4.s: na saṃvasecca patitairna cāṇḍālairna pulkasaiḥ na mūrkhairnāvaliptaiśca nāntyairnāntyāvasāyibhiḥ
4.d: न संवसेच्च पतितैर्न चाण्डालैर्न पुल्कसैः न मूर्खैर्नावलिप्तैश्च नान्त्यैर्नान्त्यावसायिभिः
4.e: He shall not associate with outcasts, nor with Cāṇḍālas, nor with Pulkasas; nor with the illiterate; nor with the haughty; nor with Antyas; nor with Antyāvasāyins.

4.s: na śūdrāya matiṃ dadyānnaucchiṣṭaṃ na haviṣkṛtam na cāsyaupadiśeddharmaṃ na cāsya vratamādiśet
4.d: न शूद्राय मतिं दद्यान्नौच्छिष्टं न हविष्कृतम् न चास्यौपदिशेद्धर्मं न चास्य व्रतमादिशेत्
4.e: He shall not offer advice to a Śūdra, nor the leavings, nor what has been prepared as an offering to the Gods. He shall hot expound the law to him; nor shall he indicate to him any penance.

4.s: yo hyasya dharmamācaṣṭe yaścaivādiśati vratam so 'saṃvṛtaṃ nāma tamaḥ saha tenaiva majjati
4.d: यो ह्यस्य धर्ममाचष्टे यश्चैवादिशति व्रतम् सो ऽसंवृतं नाम तमः सह तेनैव मज्जति
4.e: He who expounds to him the law, and he who indicates the penance to him, will sink, along with him, into the hell called “asaṃvṛta.”

4.s: na saṃhatābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ kaṇḍūyedātmanaḥ śiraḥ na spṛśeccaitaducchiṣṭo na ca snāyādvinā tataḥ
4.d: न संहताभ्यां पाणिभ्यां कण्डूयेदात्मनः शिरः न स्पृशेच्चैतदुच्छिष्टो न च स्नायाद्विना ततः
4.e: He shall not scratch his own head with both hands joined together; he shall not touch it while unclean; and he shall not bathe without it.

4.s: keśagrahān prahārāṃśca śirasyetān vivarjayet śiraḥsnātaśca tailena nāṅgaṃ kiṃ cidapi spṛśet
4.d: केशग्रहान् प्रहारांश्च शिरस्येतान् विवर्जयेत् शिरःस्नातश्च तैलेन नाङ्गं किं चिदपि स्पृशेत्
4.e: Catching of the hair, as also striking on the head,—these he shall avoid; having his head bathed, he shall touch no limb with oil.

4.s: na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇīyādarājanyaprasūtitaḥ sūnācakradhvajavatāṃ veśenaiva ca jīvatām
4.d: न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णीयादराजन्यप्रसूतितः सूनाचक्रध्वजवतां वेशेनैव च जीवताम्
4.e: He shall not accept gifts from a king not born of the Kṣatriya caste; nor from the keepers of slaughterhouses, oil-presses or grog-shops; nor from those who live on brothels.

4.s: daśasūnāsamaṃ cakraṃ daśacakrasamo dhvajaḥ daśadhvajasamo veśo daśaveśasamo nṛpaḥ
4.d: दशसूनासमं चक्रं दशचक्रसमो ध्वजः दशध्वजसमो वेशो दशवेशसमो नृपः
4.e: One oil-press is equal to ten slaughter-houses; one grog-shop is equal to ten oil-presses; one brothel is equal to ten grog-shops; and one king is equal to ten brothels.

4.s: daśa sūṇāsahasrāṇi yo vāhayati saunikaḥ tena tulyaḥ smṛto rājā ghorastasya pratigrahaḥ
4.d: दश सूणासहस्राणि यो वाहयति सौनिकः तेन तुल्यः स्मृतो राजा घोरस्तस्य प्रतिग्रहः
4.e: A king has been declared to be equal to a butcher who maintains ten thousand slaughter-houses; and terrible is the receiving of gifts from him.

4.s: yo rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇāti lubdhasyaucchāstravartinaḥ sa paryāyeṇa yātīmānnarakānekaviṃśatim
4.d: यो राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णाति लुब्धस्यौच्छास्त्रवर्तिनः स पर्यायेण यातीमान्नरकानेकविंशतिम्
4.e: He who accepts gifts from a king who is avaricious and behaves contrary to the scriptures, goes, in succession, to these twenty-one hells:

4.s: tāmisramandhatāmisraṃ mahārauravarauravau narakaṃ kālasūtraṃ ca mahānarakameva ca
4.d: तामिस्रमन्धतामिस्रं महारौरवरौरवौ नरकं कालसूत्रं च महानरकमेव च
4.e: (1) Tāmisra, (2) Andhatāmisra, (3) Mahāraurava, (4) Raurava, (5) Kālasūtra-Naraka, (6) Mahānaraka, (7) Sañjīvana, (8) Mahāvīci, (9) Tāpana, (10) Sampatāpana, (11) Saṃhāta, (12) Sakākola, (13) Kuḍmala, (14) Pūtimṛttika, (15) Lohaśaṅku, (16) Ṛjīṣa, (17) Pathin, (18) Śālmalī, (19) Nadī, (20) Asipatravana and (21) Lohadāraka.

4.s: sañjīvanaṃ mahāvīciṃ tapanaṃ saṃpratāpanam saṃhātaṃ ca sakākolaṃ kuḍmalaṃ pratimūrtikam pūtimṛttikaṃ
4.d: सञ्जीवनं महावीचिं तपनं संप्रतापनम् संहातं च सकाकोलं कुड्मलं प्रतिमूर्तिकम् पूतिमृत्तिकं
4.e: (1) Tāmisra, (2) Andhatāmisra, (3) Mahāraurava, (4) Raurava, (5) Kālasūtra-Naraka, (6) Mahānaraka, (7) Sañjīvana, (8) Mahāvīci, (9) Tāpana, (10) Sampatāpana, (11) Saṃhāta, (12) Sakākola, (13) Kuḍmala, (14) Pūtimṛttika, (15) Lohaśaṅku, (16) Ṛjīṣa, (17) Pathin, (18) Śālmalī, (19) Nadī, (20) Asipatravana and (21) Lohadāraka.

4.s: lohaśaṅkuṃ ṛjīṣaṃ ca panthānaṃ śālmalīṃ nadīm asipatravanaṃ caiva lohadārakameva ca
4.d: लोहशङ्कुं ऋजीषं च पन्थानं शाल्मलीं नदीम् असिपत्रवनं चैव लोहदारकमेव च
4.e: (1) Tāmisra, (2) Andhatāmisra, (3) Mahāraurava, (4) Raurava, (5) Kālasūtra-Naraka, (6) Mahānaraka, (7) Sañjīvana, (8) Mahāvīci, (9) Tāpana, (10) Sampatāpana, (11) Saṃhāta, (12) Sakākola, (13) Kuḍmala, (14) Pūtimṛttika, (15) Lohaśaṅku, (16) Ṛjīṣa, (17) Pathin, (18) Śālmalī, (19) Nadī, (20) Asipatravana and (21) Lohadāraka.

4.s: etadvidanto vidvāṃso brāhmaṇā brahmavādinaḥ na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇanti pretya śreyo 'bhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ
4.d: एतद्विदन्तो विद्वांसो ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिनः न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति प्रेत्य श्रेयो ऽभिकाङ्क्षिणः
4.e: Knowing this, the learned Brāhmaṇas reading the Vedas do not accept gifts from a king, if they desire to secure welfare after death.

4.s: brāhme muhūrte budhyeta dharmārthau cānucintayet kāyakleśāṃśca tanmūlān vedatattvārthameva ca
4.d: ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते बुध्येत धर्मार्थौ चानुचिन्तयेत् कायक्लेशांश्च तन्मूलान् वेदतत्त्वार्थमेव च
4.e: He shall wake up at the point of time sacred to Brahman, and then think over the means of acquiring Merit and wealth, of the bodily troubles involved therein, and also of the true meaning of the Veda.

4.s: utthāyāvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā kṛtaśaucaḥ samāhitaḥ pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhet svakāle cāparāṃ ciram
4.d: उत्थायावश्यकं कृत्वा कृतशौचः समाहितः पूर्वां संध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठेत् स्वकाले चापरां चिरम्
4.e: Having risen, and saving accomplished the necessities of nature, he shall perform the purifications, and, with collected mind, he shall stand, repeating for a long time (the Sāvitrī), during the morning-twilight, as also during the evening-twilight, at its proper time.’

4.s: ṛṣayo dīrghasaṃdhyatvāddīrghamāyuravāpnuyuḥ prajñāṃ yaśaśca kīrtiṃ ca brahmavarcasameva ca
4.d: ऋषयो दीर्घसंध्यत्वाद्दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयुः प्रज्ञां यशश्च कीर्तिं च ब्रह्मवर्चसमेव च
4.e: It was by reason or their prolonged twilight-devotions that the sages obtained long life, wisdom, fame, refutation and Brahmic glory.

4.s: śrāvaṇyāṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ vā 'pyupākṛtya yathāvidhi yuktaśchandāṃsyadhīyīta māsān vipro 'rdhapañcamān
4.d: श्रावण्यां प्रौष्ठपद्यां वा ऽप्युपाकृत्य यथाविधि युक्तश्छन्दांस्यधीयीत मासान् विप्रो ऽर्धपञ्चमान्
4.e: Having perfomed the “Upākarma” (starting rite) on the full- moon day in the month of Śrāvaṇa or of Bhādrapada, the Brāhmaṇa shall, with due diligence, study the vedas, according to rule, during four months and a half.

4.s: puṣye tu chandasāṃ kuryādbahirutsarjanaṃ dvijaḥ māghaśuklasya vā prāpte pūrvāhṇe prathame 'hani
4.d: पुष्ये तु छन्दसां कुर्याद्बहिरुत्सर्जनं द्विजः माघशुक्लस्य वा प्राप्ते पूर्वाह्णे प्रथमे ऽहनि
4.e: The Brāhmaṇa shall perform, outside, the “Utsarjana” (Suspension) of the Vedas on the day of the Puṣya asterism, or on the forenoon of the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha.

4.s: yathāśāstraṃ tu kṛtvaivamutsargaṃ chandasāṃ bahiḥ viramet pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ tadevaikamaharṃiśam
4.d: यथाशास्त्रं तु कृत्वैवमुत्सर्गं छन्दसां बहिः विरमेत् पक्षिणीं रात्रिं तदेवैकमहर्ंइशम्
4.e: Having performed, according to law, the “Utsarga” of the Vedas, he shall cease for the night with its two wings, including the same day and night.

4.s: ata ūrdhvaṃ tu chandāṃsi śukleṣu niyataḥ paṭhet vedāṅgāni ca sarvāṇi kṛṣṇapakṣeṣu saṃpaṭhet
4.d: अत ऊर्ध्वं तु छन्दांसि शुक्लेषु नियतः पठेत् वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि कृष्णपक्षेषु संपठेत्
4.e: After this, he shall diligently read the Vedas during the bright fortnights, and all the subsidiary sciences during the dark fortnights.

4.s: nāvispaṣṭamadhīyīta na śūdrajanasannidhau na niśānte pariśrānto brahmādhītya punaḥ svapet
4.d: नाविस्पष्टमधीयीत न शूद्रजनसन्निधौ न निशान्ते परिश्रान्तो ब्रह्माधीत्य पुनः स्वपेत्
4.e: He shall recite, not indistinctly, nor in the proximity of Śūdras; nor shall he go to sleep again, at the end of night, when he is tired after having recited the Veda.

4.s: yathauditena vidhinā nityaṃ chandaskṛtaṃ paṭhet brahma chandaskṛtaṃ caiva dvijo yukto hyanāpadi
4.d: यथौदितेन विधिना नित्यं छन्दस्कृतं पठेत् ब्रह्म छन्दस्कृतं चैव द्विजो युक्तो ह्यनापदि
4.e: According to the prescribed rule, the Brāhmaṇa shall, every day, during normal times, diligently recite the Veda in verse, as also the Veda in verse and prose.

4.s: imānnityamanadhyāyānadhīyāno vivarjayet adhyāpanaṃ ca kurvāṇaḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ vidhipūrvakam
4.d: इमान्नित्यमनध्यायानधीयानो विवर्जयेत् अध्यापनं च कुर्वाणः शिष्याणां विधिपूर्वकम्
4.e: One who is studying the Veda should always avoid these days, as unfit for study; so also the person who is doing the teaching of pupils according to rule.

4.s: karṇaśrave 'nile rātrau divā pāṃsusamūhane etau varṣāsvanadhyāyāvadhyāyajñāḥ pracakṣate
4.d: कर्णश्रवे ऽनिले रात्रौ दिवा पांसुसमूहने एतौ वर्षास्वनध्यायावध्यायज्ञाः प्रचक्षते
4.e: (a) At night, when air is audible by the ear, and (b) in the day when there is dust-whorl,—these two occasions during the rains are declared by those versed in the rules of teaching to be unfit for study.

4.s: vidyutstanitavarṣeṣu mahaulkānāṃ ca saṃplave ākālikamanadhyāyameteṣu manurabravīt
4.d: विद्युत्स्तनितवर्षेषु महौल्कानां च संप्लवे आकालिकमनध्यायमेतेषु मनुरब्रवीत्
4.e: When there is lightning, thunder and rain,—when there is promiscuous falling of meteors;—on these occasions, there shall be no study till the same time (next day):—thus has Manu declared.

4.s: etāṃstvabhyuditān vidyādyadā prāduṣkṛtāgniṣu tadā vidyādanadhyāyamanṛtau cābhradarśane
4.d: एतांस्त्वभ्युदितान् विद्याद्यदा प्रादुष्कृताग्निषु तदा विद्यादनध्यायमनृतौ चाभ्रदर्शने
4.e: When these appear after the Fires have been lighted, then is it to be regarded as time unfit for study; as also when clouds are seen out of season.

4.s: nirghāte bhūmicalane jyotiṣāṃ caupasarjane etānākālikān vidyādanadhyāyān ṛtāvapi
4.d: निर्घाते भूमिचलने ज्योतिषां चौपसर्जने एतानाकालिकान् विद्यादनध्यायान् ऋतावपि
4.e: When there is preter-natural sound, when there is earthquake, and when there is an impact of planets,—these are to be regarded as time unfit for study, until the same hour next day,—even during the season.

4.s: prāduṣkṛteṣvagniṣu tu vidyutstanitaniḥsvane sajyotiḥ syādanadhyāyaḥ śeṣe rātrau yathā divā
4.d: प्रादुष्कृतेष्वग्निषु तु विद्युत्स्तनितनिःस्वने सज्योतिः स्यादनध्यायः शेषे रात्रौ यथा दिवा
4.e: When lightning and the roar of thunder appear after the Fires have been lighted, the time shall continue to be unfit for study, till the lights are there; and when the remaining (phenomenon) ocours, it is unfit for study during the night, as also during the day.

4.s: nityānadhyāya eva syādgrāmeṣu nagareṣu ca dharmanaipuṇyakāmānāṃ pūtigandhe ca sarvadā sarvaśaḥ
4.d: नित्यानध्याय एव स्याद्ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च धर्मनैपुण्यकामानां पूतिगन्धे च सर्वदा सर्वशः
4.e: In villages and cities, it is always unfit for study, for those who seek for perfect merit; as also in foul-shelling places.

4.s: antargataśave grāme vṛṣalasya ca sannidhau anadhyāyo rudyamāne samavāye janasya ca
4.d: अन्तर्गतशवे ग्रामे वृषलस्य च सन्निधौ अनध्यायो रुद्यमाने समवाये जनस्य च
4.e: In a village where a corpse still lies, in the presence of low people, during weeping, and in a crowd of hen,—it is unfit for study.

4.s: udake madhyarātre ca viṣmūtrasya visarjane ucchiṣṭaḥ śrāddhabhuk caiva manasā 'pi na cintayet
4.d: उदके मध्यरात्रे च विष्मूत्रस्य विसर्जने उच्छिष्टः श्राद्धभुक् चैव मनसा ऽपि न चिन्तयेत्
4.e: In water, at midnight, during the evacuation of the bladder and the bowels, while one is unclean, when one has eaten at a śrāddha, one shall not even think in his mind (of the Veda).

4.s: pratigṛhya dvijo vidvānekoddiṣṭasya ketanam ekoddiṣṭaniketanam tryahaṃ na kīrtayedbrahma rājño rāhośca sūtake
4.d: प्रतिगृह्य द्विजो विद्वानेकोद्दिष्टस्य केतनम् एकोद्दिष्टनिकेतनम् त्र्यहं न कीर्तयेद्ब्रह्म राज्ञो राहोश्च सूतके
4.e: After having accepted invitation to a unitary funeral rite, the learned Brāhmaṇa shall not recite the Veda for three days; as also during the impurity of the king and also of Rāhu.

4.s: yāvadekānudiṣṭasya gandho lepaśca tiṣṭhati viprasya viduṣo dehe tāvadbrahma na kīrtayet
4.d: यावदेकानुदिष्टस्य गन्धो लेपश्च तिष्ठति विप्रस्य विदुषो देहे तावद्ब्रह्म न कीर्तयेत्
4.e: While the odour and stain of a funeral rite not offered to his own ancestor remain upon the body of a learned Brāhmaṇa, he shall not recite the Veda.

4.s: śayānaḥ prauḍhapādaśca kṛtvā caivāvasakthikām nādhīyītāmiṣaṃ jagdhvā sūtakānnādyameva ca
4.d: शयानः प्रौढपादश्च कृत्वा चैवावसक्थिकाम् नाधीयीतामिषं जग्ध्वा सूतकान्नाद्यमेव च
4.e: While lying down, while his feet are prominently thrust forward, and while he is seated with his knees tied together, he shall not study; as also after having eaten meat or food given by a person during impurity.

4.s: nīhāre bāṇaśabde ca saṃdhyayoreva caubhayoḥ amāvāsyācaturdaśyoḥ paurṇamāsy 'ṣṭakāsu ca
4.d: नीहारे बाणशब्दे च संध्ययोरेव चौभयोः अमावास्याचतुर्दश्योः पौर्णमास्य् ऽष्टकासु च
4.e: Nor during a fog, nor during the sound of arrows, nor at the two twilights, nor on the Moonless Day, nor on the fourteenth day, nor on the Full Moon Day, nor on the eighth day.

4.s: amāvāsyā guruṃ hanti śiṣyaṃ hanti caturdaśī brahmāṣṭakapaurṇamāsyau tasmāt tāḥ parivarjayet
4.d: अमावास्या गुरुं हन्ति शिष्यं हन्ति चतुर्दशी ब्रह्माष्टकपौर्णमास्यौ तस्मात् ताः परिवर्जयेत्
4.e: The Moonless Day destroys the Teacher, the Fourteenth Day destroys the pupil, and the Eighth Day and the Full-moon days destroy the Veda; hence these he shall avoid.

4.s: pāṃsuvarṣe diśāṃ dāhe gomāyuvirute tathā śvakharauṣṭre ca ruvati paṅktau ca na paṭheddvijaḥ
4.d: पांसुवर्षे दिशां दाहे गोमायुविरुते तथा श्वखरौष्ट्रे च रुवति पङ्क्तौ च न पठेद्द्विजः
4.e: The Brāhmaṇa shall not read during a dust-storm, or while the sky is burning, or while jackals are howling, or while dogs ur donkeys or camels are crying in a line.

4.s: nādhīyīta śmaśānānte grāmānte govraje 'pi vā vasitvā maithunaṃ vāsaḥ śrāddhikaṃ pratigṛhya ca
4.d: नाधीयीत श्मशानान्ते ग्रामान्ते गोव्रजे ऽपि वा वसित्वा मैथुनं वासः श्राद्धिकं प्रतिगृह्य च
4.e: He shall not study near the cremation-ground, nor near the village, nor in the cow-pasture, nor while dressed in the garment worn during sexual intercourse, nor after receiving presents in connection with funeral rites.

4.s: prāṇi vā yadi vā 'prāṇi yat kiṃ citśrāddhikaṃ bhavet tadālabhyāpyanadhyāyaḥ pāṇyāsyo hi dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ
4.d: प्राणि वा यदि वा ऽप्राणि यत् किं चित्श्राद्धिकं भवेत् तदालभ्याप्यनध्यायः पाण्यास्यो हि द्विजः स्मृतः
4.e: Any śrāddha-gift, be it animate or inanimate, if the Brāhmaṇa accepts, it becomes an occasion unfit for study; because the Brāhmaṇa has been declared as having the hand for his mouth.

4.s: corairupadrute grāme saṃbhrame cāgnikārite caurairupaplute , saṃbhrame ākālikamanadhyāyaṃ vidyāt sarvādbhuteṣu ca
4.d: चोरैरुपद्रुते ग्रामे संभ्रमे चाग्निकारिते चौरैरुपप्लुते , संभ्रमे आकालिकमनध्यायं विद्यात् सर्वाद्भुतेषु च
4.e: When the village has bees beset with thieves, when alarm has been caused by fire, it is unfit for study, till the same time next day; as also at the appearance of all portents.

4.s: upākarmaṇi cautsarge trirātraṃ kṣepaṇaṃ smṛtam aṣṭakāsu tvahorātraṃ ṛtvantāsu ca rātriṣu
4.d: उपाकर्मणि चौत्सर्गे त्रिरात्रं क्षेपणं स्मृतम् अष्टकासु त्वहोरात्रं ऋत्वन्तासु च रात्रिषु
4.e: At the ceremony of upākarma and at that of utsarjana, omission of study has been prescribed for three days, but at the Aṣṭakāṣ for one day and night; as also on the last nights of the seasons.

4.s: nādhīyītāśvamārūḍho na vṛkṣaṃ na ca hastinam na nāvaṃ na kharaṃ nauṣṭraṃ nairiṇastho na yānagaḥ
4.d: नाधीयीताश्वमारूढो न वृक्षं न च हस्तिनम् न नावं न खरं नौष्ट्रं नैरिणस्थो न यानगः
4.e: He shall not recite the Veda while seated on a horse, or a tree, or an elephant, or a boat, or a donkey, or a camel; nor when seated on barren ground, nor when going on a conveyance.

4.s: na vivāde na kalahe na senāyāṃ na saṅgare na bhuktamātre nājīrṇe na vamitvā na śuktake
4.d: न विवादे न कलहे न सेनायां न सङ्गरे न भुक्तमात्रे नाजीर्णे न वमित्वा न शुक्तके
4.e: Non during an al tercation, ok during a fight; nor in the midst of an army, nor during a battle, nor when he has just eaten, nor during indigestion, nor after vomiting, nor when there is eructation.

4.s: atithiṃ cānanujñāpya mārute vāti vā bhṛśam rudhire ca srute gātrātśastreṇa ca parikṣate
4.d: अतिथिं चाननुज्ञाप्य मारुते वाति वा भृशम् रुधिरे च स्रुते गात्रात्शस्त्रेण च परिक्षते
4.e: Not without having obtained the permission of his guest, nor while the wind blows vehemently; nor when blood has flowed from his body, or his body has been wounded by a weapon.

4.s: sāmadhvanāvṛcyajuṣī nādhīyīta kadā cana vedasyādhītya vā 'pyantamāraṇyakamadhītya ca
4.d: सामध्वनावृच्यजुषी नाधीयीत कदा चन वेदस्याधीत्य वा ऽप्यन्तमारण्यकमधीत्य च
4.e: He shall never recite the Ṛk or the Yajuṣ during a Sāma-chant; nor after having read the end of the Veda, or after having read the Āraṇyaka.

4.s: ṛgvedo devadaivatyo yajurvedastu mānuṣaḥ sāmavedaḥ smṛtaḥ pitryastasmāt tasyāśucirdhvaniḥ
4.d: ऋग्वेदो देवदैवत्यो यजुर्वेदस्तु मानुषः सामवेदः स्मृतः पित्र्यस्तस्मात् तस्याशुचिर्ध्वनिः
4.e: The Ṛgveda is sacred to the gods and the Yajurveda is human; the Sāmaveda has been declared to be related to the Pitṛs; hence its sound is impure.

4.s: etadvidvanto vidvāṃsastrayīniṣkarṣamanvaham kramataḥ pūrvamabhyasya paścādvedamadhīyate
4.d: एतद्विद्वन्तो विद्वांसस्त्रयीनिष्कर्षमन्वहम् क्रमतः पूर्वमभ्यस्य पश्चाद्वेदमधीयते
4.e: Knowing this, the learned dally recite first the essence of the three Vedas, in due order; and it is only after this that they recite the Veda.

4.s: paśumaṇḍūkamārjāraśvasarpanakulākhubhiḥ antarāgamane vidyādanadhyāyamaharṃiśam
4.d: पशुमण्डूकमार्जारश्वसर्पनकुलाखुभिः अन्तरागमने विद्यादनध्यायमहर्ंइशम्
4.e: When cattle, a frog, a cat, a dog, a snake, a mongoose or a rat come between,—one should regard the day and night as unfit for study.

4.s: dvāveva varjayennityamanadhyāyau prayatnataḥ svādhyāyabhūmiṃ cāśuddhamātmānaṃ cāśuciṃ dvijaḥ
4.d: द्वावेव वर्जयेन्नित्यमनध्यायौ प्रयत्नतः स्वाध्यायभूमिं चाशुद्धमात्मानं चाशुचिं द्विजः
4.e: The twice-born man shall always carefully avoid only two conditions as unfit for study: viz. an unclean place of study and his own unclean condition.

4.s: amāvāsyāmaṣṭamīṃ ca paurṇamāsīṃ caturdaśīm brahmacārī bhavennityamapy ṛtau snātako dvijaḥ
4.d: अमावास्यामष्टमीं च पौर्णमासीं चतुर्दशीम् ब्रह्मचारी भवेन्नित्यमप्य् ऋतौ स्नातको द्विजः
4.e: On the Moonless Day, on the eighth, on the Full Moon Day, and on the Fourteenth, the twice-born Accomplished Student shall always remain a “Religious Student,” even during the “season.”

4.s: na snānamācaredbhuktvā nāturo na mahāniśi na vāsobhiḥ sahājasraṃ nāvijñāte jalāśaye
4.d: न स्नानमाचरेद्भुक्त्वा नातुरो न महानिशि न वासोभिः सहाजस्रं नाविज्ञाते जलाशये
4.e: He shall not bathe after a meal, nor when he is ill, nor at midnight, nor along with his garments; and never in an unknown water-reservoir.

4.s: devatānāṃ guro rājñaḥ snātakācāryayostathā nākrāmet kāmataśchāyāṃ babhruṇo dīkṣitasya ca
4.d: देवतानां गुरो राज्ञः स्नातकाचार्ययोस्तथा नाक्रामेत् कामतश्छायां बभ्रुणो दीक्षितस्य च
4.e: He shall not intentionally step over the shadow of the gods, of a superior, of the king, of an Accomplished Student, of his own Preceptor, of the tawny thing, or of the Initiated Person.

4.s: madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre ca śrāddhaṃ bhuktvā ca sāmiṣam saṃdhyayorubhayoścaiva na seveta catuṣpatham
4.d: मध्यंदिने ऽर्धरात्रे च श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा च सामिषम् संध्ययोरुभयोश्चैव न सेवेत चतुष्पथम्
4.e: He shall not have recourse to a cross-road at midday, or at midnight, or after having partaken of meat-food at a śrāddha, or at the two twilights.

4.s: udvartanamapasnānaṃ viṣmūtre raktameva ca śleśmaniṣṭhyūtavāntāni nādhitiṣṭhet tu kāmataḥ
4.d: उद्वर्तनमपस्नानं विष्मूत्रे रक्तमेव च श्लेश्मनिष्ठ्यूतवान्तानि नाधितिष्ठेत् तु कामतः
4.e: He shall not intentionally stand upon unguent-powder, or upon used water, or on urine or ordure, or on blood, or on mucus, spittings and vomitings.

4.s: vairiṇaṃ naupaseveta sahāyaṃ caiva vairiṇaḥ adhārmikaṃ taskaraṃ ca parasyaiva ca yoṣitam
4.d: वैरिणं नौपसेवेत सहायं चैव वैरिणः अधार्मिकं तस्करं च परस्यैव च योषितम्
4.e: He shall not pay attention to his enemy, or to his enemy’s friend, or to an unrighteous person, or to a thief, or to the lady of another person.

4.s: na hīidṛśamanāyuṣyaṃ loke kiṃ cana vidyate yādṛśaṃ puruṣasyaiha paradāraupasevanam
4.d: न हीइदृशमनायुष्यं लोके किं चन विद्यते यादृशं पुरुषस्यैह परदारौपसेवनम्
4.e: In this world, there is nothing so detrimental to a man’s longevity as paying attention to the wife of another person.

4.s: kṣatriyaṃ caiva sarpaṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ ca bahuśrutam nāvamanyeta vai bhūṣṇuḥ kṛśānapi kadā cana
4.d: क्षत्रियं चैव सर्पं च ब्राह्मणं च बहुश्रुतम् नावमन्येत वै भूष्णुः कृशानपि कदा चन
4.e: Desiring his own prosperity, he shall never despise a Kṣatriya, a serpent, a learned Brāhmaṇa,—even if they be feeble.

4.s: etat trayaṃ hi puruṣaṃ nirdahedavamānitam tasmādetat trayaṃ nityaṃ nāvamanyeta buddhimān
4.d: एतत् त्रयं हि पुरुषं निर्दहेदवमानितम् तस्मादेतत् त्रयं नित्यं नावमन्येत बुद्धिमान्
4.e: Because these three, when despised, may destroy the man,—therefore, the intelligent man shall never despise these three.

4.s: nātmānamavamanyeta purvābhirasamṛddhibhiḥ ā mṛtyoḥ śriyamanvicchennaināṃ manyeta durlabhām
4.d: नात्मानमवमन्येत पुर्वाभिरसमृद्धिभिः आ मृत्योः श्रियमन्विच्छेन्नैनां मन्येत दुर्लभाम्
4.e: He shall not despise himself by reason of former failures. Until death, he should seek fortune, and he should never think her unattainable.

4.s: satyaṃ brūyāt priyaṃ brūyānna brūyāt satyamapriyam priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
4.d: सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयान्न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयादेष धर्मः सनातनः
4.e: He shall say what is true; and he shall say what is agreeable; he shall not say what is true, but disagreeale; nor shall he say what is agreeable, but untrue; this is the eternal law.

4.s: bhadraṃ bhadramiti brūyādbhadramityeva vā vadet śuṣkavairaṃ vivādaṃ ca na kuryāt kena cit saha
4.d: भद्रं भद्रमिति ब्रूयाद्भद्रमित्येव वा वदेत् शुष्कवैरं विवादं च न कुर्यात् केन चित् सह
4.e: What is (not) well, he shall call “well”; or, he shall simply say “well;” he shall not create needless enmity or dispute with any one.

4.s: nātikalyaṃ nātisāyaṃ nātimadhyaṃdine sthite nājñātena samaṃ gacchennaiko na vṛṣalaiḥ saha
4.d: नातिकल्यं नातिसायं नातिमध्यंदिने स्थिते नाज्ञातेन समं गच्छेन्नैको न वृषलैः सह
4.e: He shall not go about either too early in the morning or too late in the evening, or just at midday; nor with an unknown person, nor alone, nor with Śūdras.

4.s: hīnāṅgānatiriktāṅgān vidyāhīnān vayo 'dhikān vayo'atigān rūpadraviṇahīnāṃśca jātihīnāṃśca nākṣipet rūpadravyahīnāṃśca
4.d: हीनाङ्गानतिरिक्ताङ्गान् विद्याहीनान् वयो ऽधिकान् वयोऽअतिगान् रूपद्रविणहीनांश्च जातिहीनांश्च नाक्षिपेत् रूपद्रव्यहीनांश्च
4.e: He shall not insult those who have redundant limbs, or those who are deficient in limbs, or those destitute of learning, or those who are far advanced in age, or those destitute of beauty or wealth, or those of low birth.

4.s: na spṛśet pāṇinaucchiṣṭo vipro gobrāhmaṇānalāṇ na cāpi paśyedaśuciḥ sustho jyotirgaṇān divā svastho jyotirgaṇān divi
4.d: न स्पृशेत् पाणिनौच्छिष्टो विप्रो गोब्राह्मणानलाण् न चापि पश्येदशुचिः सुस्थो ज्योतिर्गणान् दिवा स्वस्थो ज्योतिर्गणान् दिवि
4.e: A Brāhmaṇa, while unclean, shall hot touch, with his hand, a cow, a Brāhmaṇa or fire. Nor shall he, being in good health, look at the luminaries in the sky, while he is impure.

4.s: spṛṣṭvaitānaśucirnityamadbhiḥ prāṇānupaspṛśet gātrāṇi caiva sarvāṇi nābhiṃ pāṇitalena tu
4.d: स्पृष्ट्वैतानशुचिर्नित्यमद्भिः प्राणानुपस्पृशेत् गात्राणि चैव सर्वाणि नाभिं पाणितलेन तु
4.e: Having touched these, while impure, he shall always wipe with water, with his palm, his sense-organs, as also his limbs and the navel.

4.s: anāturaḥ svāni khāni na spṛśedanimittataḥ romāṇi ca rahasyāni sarvāṇyeva vivarjayet
4.d: अनातुरः स्वानि खानि न स्पृशेदनिमित्ततः रोमाणि च रहस्यानि सर्वाण्येव विवर्जयेत्
4.e: Unless he be in trouble, he shall not, without cause, touch his cavities. He shall also avoid all secret hairs.

4.s: maṅgalācārayuktaḥ syāt prayatātmā jitaindriyaḥ japecca juhuyāccaiva nityamagnimatandritaḥ
4.d: मङ्गलाचारयुक्तः स्यात् प्रयतात्मा जितैन्द्रियः जपेच्च जुहुयाच्चैव नित्यमग्निमतन्द्रितः
4.e: He shall be intent upon auspicious customs, with his mind under control and the senses subjugated; and he shall, untired, daily recite prayers and offer oblations into the fire.

4.s: maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ nityaṃ ca prayatātmanām japatāṃ juhvatāṃ caiva vinipāto na vidyate
4.d: मङ्गलाचारयुक्तानां नित्यं च प्रयतात्मनाम् जपतां जुह्वतां चैव विनिपातो न विद्यते
4.e: For those who are ever intent upon auspicious customs, who have their mind under control, and who go on reciting prayers and offering oblations,—there is no calamity.

4.s: vedamevābhyasennityaṃ yathākālamatandritaḥ vedameva japen taṃ hyasyāhuḥ paraṃ dharmamupadharmo 'nya ucyate
4.d: वेदमेवाभ्यसेन्नित्यं यथाकालमतन्द्रितः वेदमेव जपेन् तं ह्यस्याहुः परं धर्ममुपधर्मो ऽन्य उच्यते
4.e: He shall diligently recite the Veda, whenever he finds time. They declare this to be his primary duty; everything else is declared to be his secondary duty.

4.s: vedābhyāsena satataṃ śaucena tapasaiva ca adroheṇa ca bhūtānāṃ jātiṃ smarati paurvikīm
4.d: वेदाभ्यासेन सततं शौचेन तपसैव च अद्रोहेण च भूतानां जातिं स्मरति पौर्विकीम्
4.e: By the constant recitation of the Veda, by purification, by austerity, and by doing no harm to living beings, he remembers his previous birth.

4.s: paurvikīṃ saṃsmaran jātiṃ brahmaivābhyasyate punaḥ dvijaḥ brahmābhyāsena cājasramanantaṃ sukhamaśnute
4.d: पौर्विकीं संस्मरन् जातिं ब्रह्मैवाभ्यस्यते पुनः द्विजः ब्रह्माभ्यासेन चाजस्रमनन्तं सुखमश्नुते
4.e: Recollecting his former births, the twice-born person continues to study the Veda; and by his continuous study of the Veda, he obtains absolute, endless bliss.

4.s: sāvitrāṃśāntihomāṃśca kuryāt parvasu nityaśaḥ sāvitrān śāntihomāṃś pitr̥̄ṃścaivāṣṭakāsvarcennityamanvaṣṭakāsu ca
4.d: सावित्रांशान्तिहोमांश्च कुर्यात् पर्वसु नित्यशः सावित्रान् शान्तिहोमांश् पित्र्̥̄ंश्चैवाष्टकास्वर्चेन्नित्यमन्वष्टकासु च
4.e: On special days, he shall always offer the oblations to Savitṛ, and also the Pacificatory Oblations; on the “Aṣtakas” and on the “Anvaṣṭakas” he shall always worship the Pitṛs.’

4.s: dūrādāvasathān mūtraṃ dūrāt pādāvasecanam ucchiṣtānnaniṣekaṃ ca dūrādeva samācaret
4.d: दूरादावसथान् मूत्रं दूरात् पादावसेचनम् उच्छिष्तान्ननिषेकं च दूरादेव समाचरेत्
4.e: Far from the dwelling-place shall he perform urination, far off he shall perform feet-washing, and far away he shall do the throwing of the leavings of food.

4.s: maitraṃ prasādhanaṃ snānaṃ dantadhāvanamañjanam pūrvāhṇa eva kurvīta devatānāṃ ca pūjanam
4.d: मैत्रं प्रसाधनं स्नानं दन्तधावनमञ्जनम् पूर्वाह्ण एव कुर्वीत देवतानां च पूजनम्
4.e: In the forenoon, he shall perform the evacuation of bow els, toilette, bath, cleaning of the teeth, dying of the eyes, and the worship of the gods.

4.s: daivatānyabhigacchet tu dhārmikāṃśca dvijottamān īśvaraṃ caiva rakṣārthaṃ gurūneva ca parvasu
4.d: दैवतान्यभिगच्छेत् तु धार्मिकांश्च द्विजोत्तमान् ईश्वरं चैव रक्षार्थं गुरूनेव च पर्वसु
4.e: He shall, in his action, diligently attend to right conduct which is the root of Righteousness ordained in the Śruti and Smṛti.

4.s: abhivādayedvṛddhāṃśca dadyāccaivāsanaṃ svakam kṛtāñjalirupāsīta gacchataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nviyāt
4.d: अभिवादयेद्वृद्धांश्च दद्याच्चैवासनं स्वकम् कृताञ्जलिरुपासीत गच्छतः पृष्ठतो ऽन्वियात्
4.e: He shall, in his action, diligently attend to right conduct which is the root of Righteousness ordained in the Śruti and Smṛti.

4.s: śrutismṛtyoditaṃ samyalg nibaddhaṃ sveṣu karmasu dharmamūlaṃ niṣeveta sadācāramatandritaḥ
4.d: श्रुतिस्मृत्योदितं सम्यल्ग् निबद्धं स्वेषु कर्मसु धर्ममूलं निषेवेत सदाचारमतन्द्रितः
4.e: He shall, in his action, diligently attend to right conduct which is the root of Righteousness ordained in the Śruti and Smṛti.

4.s: ācārātlabhate hyāyurācārādīpsitāḥ prajāḥ ācārāddhanamakṣayyamācāro hantyalakṣaṇam
4.d: आचारात्लभते ह्यायुराचारादीप्सिताः प्रजाः आचाराद्धनमक्षय्यमाचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम्
4.e: By Right Conduct he attains longevity; by Right Conduct he obtains desirable children; by Right Conduct he obtains inexhaustible wealth; and Right Conduct destroys everything inauspicious.

4.s: durācāro hi puruṣo loke bhavati ninditaḥ duḥkhabhāgī ca satataṃ vyādhito 'lpāyureva ca
4.d: दुराचारो हि पुरुषो लोके भवति निन्दितः दुःखभागी च सततं व्याधितो ऽल्पायुरेव च
4.e: Even though devoid of all auspicious marks, the man who follows Right Conduct, has faith and is free from jealousy, lives for a hundred years

4.s: sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi yaḥ sadācāravānnaraḥ śraddadhāno 'nasūyaśca śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati
4.d: सर्वलक्षणहीनो ऽपि यः सदाचारवान्नरः श्रद्दधानो ऽनसूयश्च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति
4.e: Even though devoid of all auspicious marks, the man who follows Right Conduct, has faith and is free from jealousy, lives for a hundred years

4.s: yadyat paravaśaṃ karma tat tadyatnena varjayet yadyadātmavaśaṃ tu syāt tat tat seveta yatnataḥ
4.d: यद्यत् परवशं कर्म तत् तद्यत्नेन वर्जयेत् यद्यदात्मवशं तु स्यात् तत् तत् सेवेत यत्नतः
4.e: He shall carefully avoid every such act as is dependent upon others; such acts as are dependent upon himself, every one of these he shall eagerly pursue.

4.s: sarvaṃ paravaśaṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvamātmavaśaṃ sukham etadvidyāt samāsena lakṣaṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
4.d: सर्वं परवशं दुःखं सर्वमात्मवशं सुखम् एतद्विद्यात् समासेन लक्षणं सुखदुःखयोः
4.e: All that is dependent on others is painful; all that is dependent on oneself is pleasing; he shall know this to be, in short, the definition of pleasure and pain.

4.s: yat karma kurvato 'sya syāt paritoṣo 'ntarātmanaḥ tat prayatnena kurvīta viparītaṃ tu varjayet
4.d: यत् कर्म कुर्वतो ऽस्य स्यात् परितोषो ऽन्तरात्मनः तत् प्रयत्नेन कुर्वीत विपरीतं तु वर्जयेत्
4.e: He shall perform, with diligence that act, by performing which there arises satisfaction in his inner soul; and he shall avoid the contrary.

4.s: ācāryaṃ ca pravaktāraṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum na hiṃsyādbrāhmaṇān gāśca sarvāṃścaiva tapasvinaḥ
4.d: आचार्यं च प्रवक्तारं पितरं मातरं गुरुम् न हिंस्याद्ब्राह्मणान् गाश्च सर्वांश्चैव तपस्विनः
4.e: He shall not injure his Preceptor, or Teacher or Father, or mother, or another elder, or Brāhmaṇas, or Cows, or any persons performing austerities.

4.s: nāstikyaṃ vedanindāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca kutsanam dveṣaṃ dambhaṃ ca mānaṃ ca krodhaṃ taikṣṇyaṃ ca varjayet dveṣaṃ stambhaṃ ca
4.d: नास्तिक्यं वेदनिन्दां च देवतानां च कुत्सनम् द्वेषं दम्भं च मानं च क्रोधं तैक्ष्ण्यं च वर्जयेत् द्वेषं स्तम्भं च
4.e: He shall, avoid atheism, cavilling at the Vedas, abusing of the gods, hatred, haughtiness, pride, anger and hastiness.

4.s: parasya daṇḍaṃ naudyacchet kruddho nainaṃ nipātayet anyatra putrātśiṣyādvā śiṣṭiarthaṃ tāḍayet tu tau
4.d: परस्य दण्डं नौद्यच्छेत् क्रुद्धो नैनं निपातयेत् अन्यत्र पुत्रात्शिष्याद्वा शिष्टिअर्थं ताडयेत् तु तौ
4.e: He shall not, when angry, raise the rod against another person, nor shall he let it fall; except in the case of the son or the pupil; these two he may beat with a view to correction.

4.s: brāhmaṇāyāvaguryaiva dvijātirvadhakāmyayā śataṃ varṣāṇi tāmisre narake parivartate
4.d: ब्राह्मणायावगुर्यैव द्विजातिर्वधकाम्यया शतं वर्षाणि तामिस्रे नरके परिवर्तते
4.e: The twice-born person who threatens a Brāhmaṇa, with the intention of striking him, wanders about in the tāmisra hell for a hundred years.

4.s: tāḍayitvā tṛṇenāpi saṃrambhātmatipūrvakam ekaviṃśatīmājātīḥ pāpayoniṣu jāyate
4.d: ताडयित्वा तृणेनापि संरम्भात्मतिपूर्वकम् एकविंशतीमाजातीः पापयोनिषु जायते
4.e: Having, in anger, struck him intentionally, even with a straw, he is born, during twenty-one births, in sinful wombs.

4.s: ayudhyamānasyautpādya brāhmaṇasyāsṛgaṅgataḥ duḥkhaṃ sumahadāpnoti pretyāprājñatayā naraḥ
4.d: अयुध्यमानस्यौत्पाद्य ब्राह्मणस्यासृगङ्गतः दुःखं सुमहदाप्नोति प्रेत्याप्राज्ञतया नरः
4.e: The man, who, through folly, causes blood to flow from the body or a Brāhmaṇa who is not fighting, undergoes, after death, very great suffrring.

4.s: śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūn saṅgṛhṇāti mahītalāt tāvato 'bdānamutrānyaiḥ śoṇitautpādako 'dyate
4.d: शोणितं यावतः पांसून् सङ्गृह्णाति महीतलात् तावतो ऽब्दानमुत्रान्यैः शोणितौत्पादको ऽद्यते
4.e: As many particles of dust the blood takes up from the ground, during so many years is the blood-spiller devoured by others in the other world.

4.s: na kadā ciddvije tasmādvidvānavaguredapi na tāḍayet tṛṇenāpi na gātrāt srāvayedasṛk
4.d: न कदा चिद्द्विजे तस्माद्विद्वानवगुरेदपि न ताडयेत् तृणेनापि न गात्रात् स्रावयेदसृक्
4.e: For these reasons, the learned man shall never even threaten a twice-born person; he shall not strike him even with a straw; and he shall not spill blood from his body.

4.s: adhārmiko naro yo hi yasya cāpyanṛtaṃ dhanam hiṃsārataśca yo nityaṃ naihāsau sukhamedhate iṃsāratiś
4.d: अधार्मिको नरो यो हि यस्य चाप्यनृतं धनम् हिंसारतश्च यो नित्यं नैहासौ सुखमेधते इंसारतिश्
4.e: The man who is unrighteous, he whose wealth is mis-begotten, and he who is always addicted to injuring, never obtains happiness in this world.

4.s: na sīdannapi dharmeṇa mano 'dharme niveśayet adhārmikānāṃ pāpānāmāśu paśyan viparyayam
4.d: न सीदन्नपि धर्मेण मनो ऽधर्मे निवेशयेत् अधार्मिकानां पापानामाशु पश्यन् विपर्ययम्
4.e: Perceiving the quick overthrow of unrighteous sinners, he shall not turn his mind towards unrighteousness, even though suffering in consequence of righteonsness.

4.s: nādharmaścarito loke sadyaḥ phalati gauriva śanairāvartyamānastu karturmūlāni kṛntati
4.d: नाधर्मश्चरितो लोके सद्यः फलति गौरिव शनैरावर्त्यमानस्तु कर्तुर्मूलानि कृन्तति
4.e: Unrighteousness, practised in this world, does not, like the Earth (or the Cow) bring its fruit immediately; but, accumulating gradually, it outs off the roots of the perpetrator.

4.s: yadi nātmani putreṣu na cet putreṣu naptṛṣu na tveva tu kṛto 'dharmaḥ karturbhavati niṣphalaḥ kṛto dharmaḥ ?
4.d: यदि नात्मनि पुत्रेषु न चेत् पुत्रेषु नप्तृषु न त्वेव तु कृतो ऽधर्मः कर्तुर्भवति निष्फलः कृतो धर्मः ?
4.e: If not on himself, then on his sons,—if not on his sons, then on his grandsons (falls the punishment); an unrighteousness, once committed, never fails to bring its consequences to the perpetrator.

4.s: adharmeṇaidhate tāvat tato bhadrāṇi paśyati tataḥ sapatnān jayati samūlastu vinaśyati
4.d: अधर्मेणैधते तावत् ततो भद्राणि पश्यति ततः सपत्नान् जयति समूलस्तु विनश्यति
4.e: For a time one prospers through unrighteousness, for a while he experiences good things, and for a time he conquers his enemies; but, after all, he perishes root and branch.

4.s: satyadharmāryavṛtteṣu śauce caivāramet sadā śiṣyāṃśca śiṣyāddharmeṇa vācbāhūdarasaṃyataḥ
4.d: सत्यधर्मार्यवृत्तेषु शौचे चैवारमेत् सदा शिष्यांश्च शिष्याद्धर्मेण वाच्बाहूदरसंयतः
4.e: He shall always delight in truthfulness, Law and right conduct, as also in ceanliness (cleanliness?); he shall govern his pupils in accordance with law,—with his speech arms, and belly duly controlled.

4.s: parityajedarthakāmau yau syātāṃ dharmavarjitau dharmaṃ cāpyasukhaudarkaṃ lokasaṅkruṣṭameva ca
4.d: परित्यजेदर्थकामौ यौ स्यातां धर्मवर्जितौ धर्मं चाप्यसुखौदर्कं लोकसङ्क्रुष्टमेव च
4.e: He shall, avoid such wealth and pleasures as are opposed to righteousness, as also righteousness if it be conducive to unhappiness, or disapproved by the people.

4.s: na pāṇipādacapalo na netracapalo 'nṛjuḥ na syādvākcapalaścaiva na paradrohakarmadhīḥ
4.d: न पाणिपादचपलो न नेत्रचपलो ऽनृजुः न स्याद्वाक्चपलश्चैव न परद्रोहकर्मधीः
4.e: He shall not be fickle with his hands and feet, nor fickle with his eyes, nor crooked, nor fickle with his speech, nor harm others by deed or thought.

4.s: yenāsya pitaro yātā yena yātāḥ pitāmahāḥ tena yāyāt satāṃ mārgaṃ tena gacchanna riṣyati
4.d: येनास्य पितरो याता येन याताः पितामहाः तेन यायात् सतां मार्गं तेन गच्छन्न रिष्यति
4.e: He shall tread the path of the righteous by the same way in which his fathers and grandfathers have trodden; going by that way, he shall not suffer.

4.s: ṛtvikpurohitācāryairmātulātithisaṃśritaiḥ bālavṛddhāturairvaidyairjñātisaṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ
4.d: ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यैर्मातुलातिथिसंश्रितैः बालवृद्धातुरैर्वैद्यैर्ज्ञातिसंबन्धिबान्धवैः
4.e: He shall not have a quarrel with the officiating priest, the priest, or his Teacher, or with his maternal uncle, or his guests or dependants, with children, or with old or sick persons, or with doctors, with his paternal relations or marriage relations, with his parents, or female relations, or brother or son, or wife, or daughter, or with his slaves.

4.s: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ jāmībhirbhrātrā putreṇa bhāryayā duhitrā dāsavargeṇa vivādaṃ na samācaret
4.d: मातापितृभ्यां जामीभिर्भ्रात्रा पुत्रेण भार्यया दुहित्रा दासवर्गेण विवादं न समाचरेत्
4.e: He shall not have a quarrel with the officiating priest, the priest, or his Teacher, or with his maternal uncle, or his guests or dependants, with children, or with old or sick persons, or with doctors, with his paternal relations or marriage relations, with his parents, or female relations, or brother or son, or wife, or daughter, or with his slaves.

4.s: etairvivādān saṃtyajya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate etairjitaiśca jayati sarvānlokānimān gṛhī
4.d: एतैर्विवादान् संत्यज्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते एतैर्जितैश्च जयति सर्वान्लोकानिमान् गृही
4.e: Having renounced quarrel with these, the householder becomes freed from all sins; and, by ignoring them, he wins all these worlds.

4.s: ācāryo brahmalokaiśaḥ prājāpatye pitā prabhuḥ atithistvindralokaiśo devalokasya caṛtvijaḥ
4.d: आचार्यो ब्रह्मलोकैशः प्राजापत्ये पिता प्रभुः अतिथिस्त्विन्द्रलोकैशो देवलोकस्य चऋत्विजः
4.e: The teacher is the lord of the world of Brahmā; the Father is sovereign of the world of Prajāpati; the Guest is the master of the world of Indra; and the Priests are the lords of the world of gods.

4.s: jāmayo 'psarasāṃ loke vaiśvadevasya bāndhavāḥ saṃbandhino hyapāṃ loke pṛthivyāṃ mātṛmātulau
4.d: जामयो ऽप्सरसां लोके वैश्वदेवस्य बान्धवाः संबन्धिनो ह्यपां लोके पृथिव्यां मातृमातुलौ
4.e: Female relatives (have power) over the region of the Heavenly nymphs; maternal relations, over that of the Viśvedevas; marriage-relations, over the region of the Waters; the mother and maternal uncle, over the Earth; the children, the aged, the emaciated and the sick should be regarded as the lords of Ākāśa; the elder brother is equal to the Father; the wife and the son are one’s own body.

4.s: ākāśaiśāstu vijñeyā bālavṛddhakṛśāturāḥ bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ samaḥ pitrā bhāryā putraḥ svakā tanuḥ
4.d: आकाशैशास्तु विज्ञेया बालवृद्धकृशातुराः भ्राता ज्येष्ठः समः पित्रा भार्या पुत्रः स्वका तनुः
4.e: Female relatives (have power) over the region of the Heavenly nymphs; maternal relations, over that of the Viśvedevas; marriage-relations, over the region of the Waters; the mother and maternal uncle, over the Earth; the children, the aged, the emaciated and the sick should be regarded as the lords of Ākāśa; the elder brother is equal to the Father; the wife and the son are one’s own body.

4.s: chāyā svo dāsavargaśca duhitā kṛpaṇaṃ param tasmādetairadhikṣiptaḥ sahetāsañjvaraḥ sadā
4.d: छाया स्वो दासवर्गश्च दुहिता कृपणं परम् तस्मादेतैरधिक्षिप्तः सहेतासञ्ज्वरः सदा
4.e: Slaves are one’s own shadow; the daughter is the highest object of tenderness. For these reasons, when offended by these, he shall always bear it without heat.

4.s: pratigrahasamartho 'pi prasaṅgaṃ tatra varjayet pratigraheṇa hyasyāśu brāhmaṃ tejaḥ praśāmyati
4.d: प्रतिग्रहसमर्थो ऽपि प्रसङ्गं तत्र वर्जयेत् प्रतिग्रहेण ह्यस्याशु ब्राह्मं तेजः प्रशाम्यति
4.e: Though entitled to accept presents, he shall avoid addiction to it; because, by receiving gifts, his spiritual light is quickly extinguished.

4.s: na dravyāṇāmavijñāya vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ pratigrahe prājñaḥ pratigrahaṃ kuryādavasīdannapi kṣudhā
4.d: न द्रव्याणामविज्ञाय विधिं धर्म्यं प्रतिग्रहे प्राज्ञः प्रतिग्रहं कुर्यादवसीदन्नपि क्षुधा
4.e: Withuot knowing the lawful method of receiving gifts, the wise man shall not accept any gifts; even though he may be pining with hunger.

4.s: hiraṇyaṃ bhūmimaśvaṃ gāmannaṃ vāsastilān ghṛtam pratigṛhṇannavidvāṃstu bhasmībhavati dāruvat
4.d: हिरण्यं भूमिमश्वं गामन्नं वासस्तिलान् घृतम् प्रतिगृह्णन्नविद्वांस्तु भस्मीभवति दारुवत्
4.e: The illiterate person, accepting gold, land, horse, cow food, clothing, sesamum and clarified butter, becomes reduced to ashes, like wood.

4.s: hiraṇyamāyurannaṃ ca bhūrgauścāpyoṣatastanum aśvaścakṣustvacaṃ vāso ghṛtaṃ tejastilāḥ prajāḥ
4.d: हिरण्यमायुरन्नं च भूर्गौश्चाप्योषतस्तनुम् अश्वश्चक्षुस्त्वचं वासो घृतं तेजस्तिलाः प्रजाः
4.e: Gold and food destroy longevity; land and cow destroy the body; the horse destroys the eye; clothing destroys the skin; clarified butter destroys energy; and sesamum destroys offspring.

4.s: atapāstvanadhīyānaḥ pratigraharucirdvijaḥ ambhasyaśmaplavenaiva saha tenaiva majjati
4.d: अतपास्त्वनधीयानः प्रतिग्रहरुचिर्द्विजः अम्भस्यश्मप्लवेनैव सह तेनैव मज्जति
4.e: If the twice-born person,who is without austerities and does not study the Veda, seeks for gifts, he sinks along with him into water; just like one who sinks along with the stone-raft.

4.s: tasmādavidvān bibhiyādyasmāt tasmāt pratigrahāt svalpakenāpyavidvān hi paṅke gauriva sīdati
4.d: तस्मादविद्वान् बिभियाद्यस्मात् तस्मात् प्रतिग्रहात् स्वल्पकेनाप्यविद्वान् हि पङ्के गौरिव सीदति
4.e: For these reasons, the illiterate man should fight shy of accepting each and every gift. By receiving even a small gift, the illiterate person sinks, like the cow in a morass.

4.s: na vāryapi prayacchet tu baiḍālavratike dvije na bakavratike pāpe nāvedavidi dharmavit
4.d: न वार्यपि प्रयच्छेत् तु बैडालव्रतिके द्विजे न बकव्रतिके पापे नावेदविदि धर्मवित्
4.e: The man knowing the Law, shall not offer even water to the Brāhmaṇa who behaves like a cat; nor to the wicked Brāhmaṇa who behaves like a heron, nor to one ignorant of the Veda.

4.s: triṣvapyeteṣu dattaṃ hi vidhinā 'pyarjitaṃ dhanam dāturbhavatyanarthāya paratrādātureva ca
4.d: त्रिष्वप्येतेषु दत्तं हि विधिना ऽप्यर्जितं धनम् दातुर्भवत्यनर्थाय परत्रादातुरेव च
4.e: For property, even though acquired by lawful means,—if given to these three persons,—brings calamity, in the next world, to the giver, as also to the receiver.

4.s: yathā plavenaupalena nimajjatyudake taran tathā nimajjato 'dhastādajñau dātṛpratīcchakau
4.d: यथा प्लवेनौपलेन निमज्जत्युदके तरन् तथा निमज्जतो ऽधस्तादज्ञौ दातृप्रतीच्छकौ
4.e: Just as a man crossing water by means of a stone-raft sinks down, so also sink downwards the ignorant giver and receiver.

4.s: dharmadhvajī sadā lubdhaśchādmiko lokadambhakaḥ baiḍālavratiko jñeyo hiṃsraḥ sarvābhisaṃdhakaḥ
4.d: धर्मध्वजी सदा लुब्धश्छाद्मिको लोकदम्भकः बैडालव्रतिको ज्ञेयो हिंस्रः सर्वाभिसंधकः
4.e: He who displays his flag of virtue, is ever covetous, a cheat and a hypocrite, intent on doing harm, and the traducer of all persons, is to be known as “one behaving like the cat.”

4.s: adhodṛṣṭirnaiṣkṛtikaḥ svārthasādhanatatparaḥ śaṭho mithyāvinītaśca bakavratacaro dvijaḥ
4.d: अधोदृष्टिर्नैष्कृतिकः स्वार्थसाधनतत्परः शठो मिथ्याविनीतश्च बकव्रतचरो द्विजः
4.e: With eyes cast downwards, of cruel disposition, intent upon the accomplishment of his own ends, dishonest and falsely humble;—such is the Brāhmaṇa ‘who behaves like the heron’.

4.s: ye bakavratino viprā ye ca mārjāraliṅginaḥ te patantyandhatāmisre tena pāpena karmaṇā
4.d: ये बकव्रतिनो विप्रा ये च मार्जारलिङ्गिनः ते पतन्त्यन्धतामिस्रे तेन पापेन कर्मणा
4.e: Those Brāhmaṇas who are heron-like in their behaviour, and those who are cat-like, fall, by that sinful act, into the Andhatāmisra hell.

4.s: na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret vratena pāpaṃ pracchādya kurvan strīśūdradambhanam
4.d: न धर्मस्यापदेशेन पापं कृत्वा व्रतं चरेत् व्रतेन पापं प्रच्छाद्य कुर्वन् स्त्रीशूद्रदम्भनम्
4.e: Having committed a sin, he shall not perform penance un der the pretext of doing a righteous act,—deceiving women and Śūdras by thus covering his sin by a penance.

4.s: pretyaiha caidṛśā viprā garhyante brahmavādibhiḥ chadmanā caritaṃ yacca vrataṃ rakṣāṃsi gacchati
4.d: प्रेत्यैह चैदृशा विप्रा गर्ह्यन्ते ब्रह्मवादिभिः छद्मना चरितं यच्च व्रतं रक्षांसि गच्छति
4.e: Such Brāhmaṇas are condemned after death, and also here (in this life) by the expounders of the Veda; and penance done under a false pretence goes to the evil spirits.

4.s: aliṅgī liṅgiveṣeṇa yo vṛttimupajīvati sa liṅgināṃ haratyenastiryagyonau ca jāyate
4.d: अलिङ्गी लिङ्गिवेषेण यो वृत्तिमुपजीवति स लिङ्गिनां हरत्येनस्तिर्यग्योनौ च जायते
4.e: One who, though not entitled to the wearing of a certain badge, gains one’s living by wearing that badge, takes off the sins of persons entitled to that badge, and is born in the womb of a lower animal.

4.s: parakīyanipāneṣu na snāyāddhi kadā cana snāyācca kadā cana nipānakartuḥ snātvā tu duṣkṛtāṃśena lipyate
4.d: परकीयनिपानेषु न स्नायाद्धि कदा चन स्नायाच्च कदा चन निपानकर्तुः स्नात्वा तु दुष्कृतांशेन लिप्यते
4.e: He shall never bathe in the tanks belonging to other persons. Having bathed there, he becomes tainted with a part of the tank-digger’s sin.

4.s: yānaśayyā ''sanānyasya kūpaudyānagṛhāṇi ca adattānyupayuñjāna enasaḥ syāt turīyabhāk
4.d: यानशय्या 'ऽसनान्यस्य कूपौद्यानगृहाणि च अदत्तान्युपयुञ्जान एनसः स्यात् तुरीयभाक्
4.e: By using another person’s conveyance, couch, seat, well, garden or house,—when these have not been given,—one becomes the partaker of the fourth part of that person’s sins.

4.s: nadīṣu devakhāteṣu taḍāgeṣu saraḥsu ca snānaṃ samācarennityaṃ gartaprasravaṇeṣu ca
4.d: नदीषु देवखातेषु तडागेषु सरःसु च स्नानं समाचरेन्नित्यं गर्तप्रस्रवणेषु च
4.e: He shall always bathe in rivers and in tanks and lakes dug by the gods; as also in water-holes and springs.

4.s: yamān seveta satataṃ na nityaṃ niyamān budhaḥ yamān patatyakurvāṇo niyamān kevalān bhajan
4.d: यमान् सेवेत सततं न नित्यं नियमान् बुधः यमान् पतत्यकुर्वाणो नियमान् केवलान् भजन्
4.e: The wise man shall always observe the Restraints, but not necessarily the Observances. Not observing the Restraints, and keeping the Observances alone, he falls.

4.s: nāśrotriyatate yajñe grāmayājikṛte tathā striyā klībena ca hute bhuñjīta brāhmaṇaḥ kva cit
4.d: नाश्रोत्रियतते यज्ञे ग्रामयाजिकृते तथा स्त्रिया क्लीबेन च हुते भुञ्जीत ब्राह्मणः क्व चित्
4.e: The Brāhmaṇa shall never eat at a sacrifice performed by one who has not learnt the Veda; or at one performed by a village-priest, or at one offered by a woman or a eunuch.

4.s: aślīkametat sādhūnāṃ yatra juhvatyamī haviḥ 'ślīlam pratīpametaddevānāṃ tasmāt tat parivarjayet
4.d: अश्लीकमेतत् साधूनां यत्र जुह्वत्यमी हविः ऽश्लीलम् प्रतीपमेतद्देवानां तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत्
4.e: Where such persons pour the oblations, it is considered indecent by all good men; it is disagreeable to the gods; hence, one should avoid it

4.s: mattakruddhāturāṇāṃ ca na bhuñjīta kadā cana keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca padā spṛṣṭaṃ ca kāmataḥ
4.d: मत्तक्रुद्धातुराणां च न भुञ्जीत कदा चन केशकीटावपन्नं च पदा स्पृष्टं च कामतः
4.e: He shalll never eat food offered by intoxicated or angry or sick persons; nor that which is contaminated by hair or insects, or that which has been intentionally touched with the foot.

4.s: bhrūṇaghnāvekṣitaṃ caiva saṃspṛṣṭaṃ cāpyudakyayā patatriṇāvalīḍhaṃ ca śunā saṃspṛṣṭameva ca
4.d: भ्रूणघ्नावेक्षितं चैव संस्पृष्टं चाप्युदक्यया पतत्रिणावलीढं च शुना संस्पृष्टमेव च
4.e: Nor that which has been looked at by the Brāhmaṇa-slayer, or what has been toughed by a woman in her courses, or what has been pecked by the birds, or what has been touched by a dog.

4.s: gavā cānnamupaghrātaṃ ghuṣṭānnaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca viduṣā ca jugupsitam
4.d: गवा चान्नमुपघ्रातं घुष्टान्नं च विशेषतः गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च विदुषा च जुगुप्सितम्
4.e: Nor the food that has been smelt by the cow, nor particularly that food which has been publicly offered, nor the food that belongs to a multitude, nor the food of the harlot, nor that which has been censured by the learned.

4.s: stenagāyanayoścānnaṃ takṣṇo vārdhuṣikasya ca dīkṣitasya kadaryasya baddhasya nigaḍasya ca
4.d: स्तेनगायनयोश्चान्नं तक्ष्णो वार्धुषिकस्य च दीक्षितस्य कदर्यस्य बद्धस्य निगडस्य च
4.e: Nor the food of the thief or the singer, nor of the carpenter, the usurer, of the initiated person, of the miser, the prisoner and the fettered.

4.s: abhiśastasya ṣaṇḍhasya puṃścalyā dāmbhikasya ca śuktaṃ paryuṣitaṃ caiva śūdrasyaucchiṣṭameva ca
4.d: अभिशस्तस्य षण्ढस्य पुंश्चल्या दाम्भिकस्य च शुक्तं पर्युषितं चैव शूद्रस्यौच्छिष्टमेव च
4.e: Nor the food of an accused person, or of the hermaphrodite, or the unchaste woman, or the hypocrite; nor the food turned sour, or that kept overnight, or what forms the leavings of the Śūdra.

4.s: cikitsakasya mṛgayoḥ krūrasyaucchiṣṭabhojinaḥ ugrānnaṃ sūtikānnaṃ ca paryācāntamanirdaśam
4.d: चिकित्सकस्य मृगयोः क्रूरस्यौच्छिष्टभोजिनः उग्रान्नं सूतिकान्नं च पर्याचान्तमनिर्दशम्
4.e: Nor the food of this physician, or of the hunter, or of a cruel person, or of one who lives on leavings; nor the food of the “Ugra;” nor what has been cooked for the newly-delivered woman, until ten days have passed; nor that which has been interrupted by washing.

4.s: anarcitaṃ vṛthāmāṃsamavīrāyāśca yoṣitaḥ dviṣadannaṃ nagarīannaṃ patitānnamavakṣutam
4.d: अनर्चितं वृथामांसमवीरायाश्च योषितः द्विषदन्नं नगरीअन्नं पतितान्नमवक्षुतम्
4.e: Nor what is offered without respect, nor improper meat, nor food belonging to a male-less female, nor the food of an eneny, nor the food of the city-lord, nor the food of an outcast, nor that which has been sneezed at.

4.s: piśunānṛtinoścānnaṃ kratuvikrayiṇastathā kratuvikrayakasya ca śailūṣatunnavāyānnaṃ kṛtaghnasyānnameva ca
4.d: पिशुनानृतिनोश्चान्नं क्रतुविक्रयिणस्तथा क्रतुविक्रयकस्य च शैलूषतुन्नवायान्नं कृतघ्नस्यान्नमेव च
4.e: Nor the food of the informer and the perjurer, or of the seller of sacrifices; nor the food of the actor or the tailor; nor the food of the ungrateful person.

4.s: karmārasya niṣādasya raṅgāvatārakasya ca suvarṇakarturveṇasya śastravikrayiṇastathā
4.d: कर्मारस्य निषादस्य रङ्गावतारकस्य च सुवर्णकर्तुर्वेणस्य शस्त्रविक्रयिणस्तथा
4.e: ‘Nor or the blacksmith, of the Niṣāda, of the stage-player, of the goldsmith, of the plater of musical instruments, or of the dealer in weapons,—(215).’

4.s: śvavatāṃ śauṇḍikānāṃ ca cailanirṇejakasya ca rañjakasya nṛśaṃsasya yasya caupapatirgṛhe rajakasya
4.d: श्ववतां शौण्डिकानां च चैलनिर्णेजकस्य च रञ्जकस्य नृशंसस्य यस्य चौपपतिर्गृहे रजकस्य
4.e: Nor of dog-keepers, or of wine-sellers or of the clothes-washer, or of the dyer, or of the bard, or of the man in whose house there is a paramour.

4.s: mṛṣyanti ye caupapatiṃ strījitānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ anirdaśaṃ ca pretānnamatuṣṭikarameva ca
4.d: मृष्यन्ति ये चौपपतिं स्त्रीजितानां च सर्वशः अनिर्दशं च प्रेतान्नमतुष्टिकरमेव च
4.e: Nor of thos e who bear the presence of the paramour, or of those who are entirely ruled b y women; nor the food of those in whose house death has occurred and the ten days have not passed; nor that which is disagree able.

4.s: rājānnaṃ teja ādatte śūdrānnaṃ brahmavarcasam āyuḥ suvarṇakārānnaṃ yaśaścarmāvakartinaḥ
4.d: राजान्नं तेज आदत्ते शूद्रान्नं ब्रह्मवर्चसम् आयुः सुवर्णकारान्नं यशश्चर्मावकर्तिनः
4.e: The king’s food takes off one’s vigour and the Śūdra’s food his Brahmic glory; the goldsmith’s food his longevity, and the l eather-cutter’s food hi s fame.

4.s: kārukānnaṃ prajāṃ hanti balaṃ nirṇejakasya ca gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca lokebhyaḥ parikṛntati
4.d: कारुकान्नं प्रजां हन्ति बलं निर्णेजकस्य च गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च लोकेभ्यः परिकृन्तति
4.e: The food of artisans impairs the offspring, that of the clothes-washer impairs strength; the food of a multitude and the food of the harlot out off the max from the regions.

4.s: pūyaṃ cikitsakasyānnaṃ puṃścalyāstvannamindriyam viṣṭhā vārdhuṣikasyānnaṃ śastravikrayiṇo malam
4.d: पूयं चिकित्सकस्यान्नं पुंश्चल्यास्त्वन्नमिन्द्रियम् विष्ठा वार्धुषिकस्यान्नं शस्त्रविक्रयिणो मलम्
4.e: The food of the physician is pus; the food of the unchaste woman is semen; the food of the usurer is ordure, and that of the dealer in weapons is dirt.—(220.)

4.s: ya ete 'nye tvabhojyānnāḥ kramaśaḥ parikīrtitāḥ teṣāṃ tvagasthiromāṇi vadantyannaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
4.d: य एते ऽन्ये त्वभोज्यान्नाः क्रमशः परिकीर्तिताः तेषां त्वगस्थिरोमाणि वदन्त्यन्नं मनीषिणः
