4.e: The food of those other persons who have been successively mentioned as those whose food should not be eaten,—the wise men describe as skin, bones and hairs.

4.s: bhuktvā 'to 'nyatamasyānnamamatyā kṣapaṇaṃ tryaham matyā bhuktvā 'caret kṛcchraṃ retasviṣmūtrameva ca
4.d: भुक्त्वा ऽतो ऽन्यतमस्यान्नममत्या क्षपणं त्र्यहम् मत्या भुक्त्वा ऽचरेत् कृच्छ्रं रेतस्विष्मूत्रमेव च
4.e: After unknowingly eating the food of any one of these, there should be a three days’ fast. Having eaten it knowingly, as also on eating semen, ordure and urine, one should perform the “Kṛcchra” penance.

4.s: nādyātśūdrasya pakvānnaṃ vidvānaśrāddhino dvijaḥ ādadītāmamevāsmādavṛttāvekarātrikam
4.d: नाद्यात्शूद्रस्य पक्वान्नं विद्वानश्राद्धिनो द्विजः आददीताममेवास्मादवृत्तावेकरात्रिकम्
4.e: The learned Brāhmaṇa shall, not eat the cooked food of the Śūdra who performs no śrāddhas. In the absence of livelihood, he may receive from him raw grain sufficient for one day.

4.s: śrotriyasya kadaryasya vadānyasya ca vārdhuṣeḥ mīmāṃsitvaubhayaṃ devāḥ samamannamakalpayan
4.d: श्रोत्रियस्य कदर्यस्य वदान्यस्य च वार्धुषेः मीमांसित्वौभयं देवाः सममन्नमकल्पयन्
4.e: The gods having compared the food of the miserly Vedic Scholar and that of the liberal usurer, ordained the food of both to be equal.

4.s: tān prajāpatirāhaitya mā kṛdhvaṃ viṣamaṃ samam śraddhāpūtaṃ vadānyasya hatamaśraddhayaitarat
4.d: तान् प्रजापतिराहैत्य मा कृध्वं विषमं समम् श्रद्धापूतं वदान्यस्य हतमश्रद्धयैतरत्
4.e: Thereupon Prajāpati came to them and said—“Do not make the unequal equal: what belongs to the liberal man is purified by faith, while the other is defiled by want of faith.

4.s: śraddhayaiṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ca nityaṃ kuryādatandritaḥ śraddhākṛte hyakṣaye te bhavataḥ svāgatairdhanaiḥ
4.d: श्रद्धयैष्टं च पूर्तं च नित्यं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः श्रद्धाकृते ह्यक्षये ते भवतः स्वागतैर्धनैः
4.e: He shall always diliqenty perform, with faith, sacrifices and other religious acts; done with faith, and with well-begotten wealth, they become imperishable.

4.s: dānadharmaṃ niṣeveta nityamaiṣṭikapaurtikam parituṣṭena bhāvena pātramāsādya śaktitaḥ
4.d: दानधर्मं निषेवेत नित्यमैष्टिकपौर्तिकम् परितुष्टेन भावेन पात्रमासाद्य शक्तितः
4.e: He shall practise, to the best of his ability, charity and righteousness in connection with sacrifices and acts of piety with a cheerful heart, if he finds a suitable recipient.

4.s: yat kiṃ cidapi dātavyaṃ yācitenānasūyayā 'nasūyatā ? utpatsyate hi tat pātraṃ yat tārayati sarvataḥ
4.d: यत् किं चिदपि दातव्यं याचितेनानसूयया ऽनसूयता ? उत्पत्स्यते हि तत् पात्रं यत् तारयति सर्वतः
4.e: When asked, he should give something, without showing any displeasure. Because he may turn out to be a worthy recipient who will save him from everything.

4.s: vāridastṛptimāpnoti sukhamakṣayyamannadaḥ 'kṣayam tilapradaḥ prajāmiṣṭāṃ dīpadaścakṣuruttamam
4.d: वारिदस्तृप्तिमाप्नोति सुखमक्षय्यमन्नदः ऽक्षयम् तिलप्रदः प्रजामिष्टां दीपदश्चक्षुरुत्तमम्
4.e: The giver of water obtains satisfaction, the giver of food imperishable happiness, the giver of sesamum desirable offspring, and this giver of lamp most excellent eyesight.

4.s: bhūmido bhūmimāpnoti dīrghamāyurhiraṇyadaḥ gṛhado 'gryāṇi veśmāni rūpyado rūpamuttamam
4.d: भूमिदो भूमिमाप्नोति दीर्घमायुर्हिरण्यदः गृहदो ऽग्र्याणि वेश्मानि रूप्यदो रूपमुत्तमम्
4.e: The giver of land obtains land, the giver of gold long life, the giver of house excellent mansions, and the giver of silver exquisite beauty.

4.s: vāsodaścandrasālokyamaśvisālokyamaśvadaḥ anaḍuhaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo bradhnasya viṣṭapam
4.d: वासोदश्चन्द्रसालोक्यमश्विसालोक्यमश्वदः अनडुहः श्रियं पुष्टां गोदो ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम्
4.e: The giver of cloth obtains resemblance to the Moon, the giver of horse resemblance to horse-owners, the giver of the ox great good fortune, and the giver of the cow toe region of the Sun.

4.s: yānaśayyāprado bhāryāmaiśvaryamabhayapradaḥ dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahmasārṣṭitām
4.d: यानशय्याप्रदो भार्यामैश्वर्यमभयप्रदः धान्यदः शाश्वतं सौख्यं ब्रह्मदो ब्रह्मसार्ष्टिताम्
4.e: The giver or carriage and couch obtains a wife, the giver of fearlessness sovereignty, the giver of grains eternal happiness, and the giver of the Veda equality with Brahman.

4.s: sarveṣāmeva dānānāṃ brahmadānaṃ viśiṣyate vāriannagomahīvāsastilakāñcanasarpiṣām
4.d: सर्वेषामेव दानानां ब्रह्मदानं विशिष्यते वारिअन्नगोमहीवासस्तिलकाञ्चनसर्पिषाम्
4.e: The giving or Veda surpasses all gifts or water, food, cows, buffaloes, clothes, sesamum, gold and clarified butter.

4.s: yena yena tu bhāvena yadyaddānaṃ prayacchati tat tat tenaiva bhāvena prāpnoti pratipūjitaḥ
4.d: येन येन तु भावेन यद्यद्दानं प्रयच्छति तत् तत् तेनैव भावेन प्राप्नोति प्रतिपूजितः
4.e: In whatever spirit a man bestows a gift, in that same spirit he himself receives it with due honour.

4.s: yo 'rcitaṃ pratigṛhṇāti dadātyarcitameva vā tāvubhau gacchataḥ svargaṃ narakaṃ tu viparyaye
4.d: यो ऽर्चितं प्रतिगृह्णाति ददात्यर्चितमेव वा तावुभौ गच्छतः स्वर्गं नरकं तु विपर्यये
4.e: He who receives respectfully, as well as he who gives respectfully,—both these go to heaven; but to hell, in the contrary case.

4.s: na vismayeta tapasā vadediṣṭvā ca nānṛtam nārto 'pyapavadedviprānna dattvā parikīrtayet datvā
4.d: न विस्मयेत तपसा वदेदिष्ट्वा च नानृतम् नार्तो ऽप्यपवदेद्विप्रान्न दत्त्वा परिकीर्तयेत् दत्वा
4.e: He shall not be proud of his austerities; having offered a sacrifice, he shall not utter a lie; even when tormented, he shall not revile the brāhmaṇas; having bestowed a gift, he shall not advertise it.

4.s: yajño 'nṛtena kṣarati tapaḥ kṣarati vismayāt āyurviprāpavādena dānaṃ ca parikīrtanāt
4.d: यज्ञो ऽनृतेन क्षरति तपः क्षरति विस्मयात् आयुर्विप्रापवादेन दानं च परिकीर्तनात्
4.e: The sacrifice trickles away by falsehood, the austerity trickles away by vanity, longevity by the reviling of Brāhmaṇas, and gifts by advertisement.

4.s: dharmaṃ śanaiḥ sañcinuyādvalmīkamiva puttikāḥ sañcinuyād paralokasahāyārthaṃ sarvabhūtānyapīḍayan
4.d: धर्मं शनैः सञ्चिनुयाद्वल्मीकमिव पुत्तिकाः सञ्चिनुयाद् परलोकसहायार्थं सर्वभूतान्यपीडयन्
4.e: Without causing pain to any beings, he shall, for the purpose of obtaining a companion in the other world, accumulate spiritual merit, slowly; just as the white ants accumulate the ant-hill.

4.s: nāmutra hi sahāyārthaṃ pitā mātā ca tiṣṭhataḥ na putradāraṃ na jñātirdharmastiṣṭhati kevalaḥ
4.d: नामुत्र हि सहायार्थं पिता माता च तिष्ठतः न पुत्रदारं न ज्ञातिर्धर्मस्तिष्ठति केवलः
4.e: There, neither father, nor mother, nor wife, nor sons, nor relations stay as companions; spiritual merit alone remains.

4.s: ekaḥ prajāyate jantureka eva pralīyate eko 'nubhuṅkte sukṛtameka eva ca duṣkṛtam
4.d: एकः प्रजायते जन्तुरेक एव प्रलीयते एको ऽनुभुङ्क्ते सुकृतमेक एव च दुष्कृतम्
4.e: Alone is a creature born, and alone does it cease to be; alone it enjoys its good deeds and also its evil deeds.

4.s: mṛtaṃ śarīramutsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṃ kṣitau vimukhā bāndhavā yānti dharmastamanugacchati
4.d: मृतं शरीरमुत्सृज्य काष्ठलोष्टसमं क्षितौ विमुखा बान्धवा यान्ति धर्मस्तमनुगच्छति
4.e: Leaving the dead body on the ground, like a log of wood or a clod of earth, the relations depart with averted faces; spiritual merit alone follows him.

4.s: tasmāddharmaṃ sahāyārthaṃ nityaṃ sañcinuyātśanaiḥ dharmeṇa hi sahāyena tamastarati dustaram
4.d: तस्माद्धर्मं सहायार्थं नित्यं सञ्चिनुयात्शनैः धर्मेण हि सहायेन तमस्तरति दुस्तरम्
4.e: He shall, therefore, slowly accumulate Spiritual Merit, for the purpose of securing a companion; for, with Merit as his companion, the man crosses over unfordable darkness.

4.s: dharmapradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ tapasā hatakilbiṣam paralokaṃ nayatyāśu bhāsvantaṃ khaśarīriṇam
4.d: धर्मप्रधानं पुरुषं तपसा हतकिल्बिषम् परलोकं नयत्याशु भास्वन्तं खशरीरिणम्
4.e: It speedily carries the man, who is devoted to duty and has his sins destroyed by austerities, clothed in his own (spiritual) body, to the brighter regions above.

4.s: uttamairuttamairnityaṃ saṃbandhānācaret saha saṃbhandhān ninīṣuḥ kulamutkarṣamadhamānadhamāṃstyajet
4.d: उत्तमैरुत्तमैर्नित्यं संबन्धानाचरेत् सह संभन्धान् निनीषुः कुलमुत्कर्षमधमानधमांस्त्यजेत्
4.e: Being desirous of raising his family to eminence, he shall always form connections with superior kinds of people; he shalt, avoid all inferior ones.

4.s: uttamānuttamāneva gacchan hīnāṃstu varjayan brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhatāmeti pratyavāyena śūdratām
4.d: उत्तमानुत्तमानेव गच्छन् हीनांस्तु वर्जयन् ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठतामेति प्रत्यवायेन शूद्रताम्
4.e: Having recourse to superior kinds of people, and avoiding the inferior kinds, the Brāhmaṇa attains eminence; by the contrary procedure, he becomes a Śūdra.

4.s: dṛḍhakārī mṛdurdāntaḥ krūrācārairasaṃvasan ahiṃsro damadānābhyāṃ jayet svargaṃ tathāvrataḥ
4.d: दृढकारी मृदुर्दान्तः क्रूराचारैरसंवसन् अहिंस्रो दमदानाभ्यां जयेत् स्वर्गं तथाव्रतः
4.e: He who acts resolutely, is gentle and tolerant, who does not associate with persons of cruel disposition, and who does no injury to others, shall win heaven by his self-control and liberality, if he sticks to this practice.

4.s: edhaudakaṃ mūlaphalamannamabhyudyataṃ ca yat sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyātmadhuathābhayadakṣiṇām
4.d: एधौदकं मूलफलमन्नमभ्युद्यतं च यत् सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयात्मधुअथाभयदक्षिणाम्
4.e: He may accept from all persons fuel, water, roots, and fruits, and food that is offered, as also honey and the gift of fearlessness.’

4.s: āhṛtābhyudyatāṃ bhikṣāṃ purastādapracoditām mene prajāpatirgrāhyāmapi duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ
4.d: आहृताभ्युद्यतां भिक्षां पुरस्तादप्रचोदिताम् मेने प्रजापतिर्ग्राह्यामपि दुष्कृतकर्मणः
4.e: Alms brougt forward and offered, and not previously begged, Prajāpati has declared to be acceptable, even from a sinful person.

4.s: nāśnanti pitarastasya daśavarṣāṇi pañca ca na ca havyaṃ vahatyagniryastāmabhyavamanyate
4.d: नाश्नन्ति पितरस्तस्य दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च न च हव्यं वहत्यग्निर्यस्तामभ्यवमन्यते
4.e: Of the man that disdains it, the Pitṛs do no eat any food for ten and five years; nor does fire convey his offering to the gods.

4.s: śayyāṃ gṛhān kuśān gandhānapaḥ puṣpaṃ maṇīn dadhi dhānā matsyān payo māṃsaṃ śākaṃ caiva na nirṇudet
4.d: शय्यां गृहान् कुशान् गन्धानपः पुष्पं मणीन् दधि धाना मत्स्यान् पयो मांसं शाकं चैव न निर्णुदेत्
4.e: He shall not refuse a couch, a house, kuśa grass, perfumes, water, flowers, jewels, curd, grain, fish, milk, meat and vegetables.

4.s: gurūn bhṛtyāṃścaujjihīrṣannarciṣyan devatā 'tithīn sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna tu tṛpyet svayaṃ tataḥ
4.d: गुरून् भृत्यांश्चौज्जिहीर्षन्नर्चिष्यन् देवता ऽतिथीन् सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न तु तृप्येत् स्वयं ततः
4.e: For the purpose of bringing relief to his teachers and dependents, and for the purpose of honoring the gods and guests, he may accept gifts from all persons; but he shall not derive from them satisfaction for himself.

4.s: guruṣu tvabhyatīteṣu vinā vā tairgṛhe vasan ātmano vṛttimanvicchan gṛhṇīyāt sādhutaḥ sadā
4.d: गुरुषु त्वभ्यतीतेषु विना वा तैर्गृहे वसन् आत्मनो वृत्तिमन्विच्छन् गृह्णीयात् साधुतः सदा
4.e: When, however, the Teachers are dead, or when one lives in his house without them,—then, seeking for his own subsistence, he may always accept gifts from good persons.

4.s: ārdhikaḥ kulamitraṃ ca gopālo dāsanāpitau ete śūdreṣu bhojyānnā yāścātmānaṃ nivedayet
4.d: आर्धिकः कुलमित्रं च गोपालो दासनापितौ एते शूद्रेषु भोज्यान्ना याश्चात्मानं निवेदयेत्
4.e: His own ploughman, hereditary friend, cowherd, slave and barder,—among Śūdras; these are persons whose food may be eaten; as also one who offers himself.

4.s: yādṛśo 'sya bhavedātmā yādṛśaṃ ca cikīrṣitam yathā caupacaredenaṃ tathā 'tmānaṃ nivedayet
4.d: यादृशो ऽस्य भवेदात्मा यादृशं च चिकीर्षितम् यथा चौपचरेदेनं तथा ऽत्मानं निवेदयेत्
4.e: As the man’s character may be, as may be the nature of the work he wishes to do, and as may be the manner in which he may serve,—even so must he offer himself.

4.s: yo 'nyathā santamātmānamanyathā satsu bhāṣate sa pāpakṛttamo loke stena ātmāpahārakaḥ
4.d: यो ऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा सत्सु भाषते स पापकृत्तमो लोके स्तेन आत्मापहारकः
4.e: He, who describes himself to good men otherwise than what he is, is the worst sinner in the world, a thief stealing himself.

4.s: vācyarthā niyatāḥ sarve vācmūlā vācviniḥsṛtāḥ tāṃstu yaḥ stenayedvācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛtnaraḥ tān tu ?
4.d: वाच्यर्था नियताः सर्वे वाच्मूला वाच्विनिःसृताः तांस्तु यः स्तेनयेद्वाचं स सर्वस्तेयकृत्नरः तान् तु ?
4.e: All things are regulated by speech, have their root in speech, and emanate from speech. The man who steals such speech is the stealer of all things.

4.s: maharṣipitṛdevānāṃ gatvā 'nṛṇyaṃ yathāvidhi putre sarvaṃ samāsajya vasen mādhyasthyamāsśritaḥ āsthitaḥ
4.d: महर्षिपितृदेवानां गत्वा ऽनृण्यं यथाविधि पुत्रे सर्वं समासज्य वसेन् माध्यस्थ्यमास्श्रितः आस्थितः
4.e: Having paid off, according to law, the debts owing to the Great Sages, to the Pitṛs and to the Gods, he shall consign everything to his son and remain fixed in neutrality.

4.s: ekākī cintayennityaṃ vivikte hitamātmanaḥ itamātmani ekākī cintayāno hi paraṃ śreyo 'dhigacchati
4.d: एकाकी चिन्तयेन्नित्यं विविक्ते हितमात्मनः इतमात्मनि एकाकी चिन्तयानो हि परं श्रेयो ऽधिगच्छति
4.e: Alone, in solitude, he shall meditate upon what is good for himself. By meditating in solitude, he attains the highest good.

4.s: eṣauditā gṛhasthasya vṛttirviprasya śāśvatī snātakavratakalpaśca sattvavṛddhikaraḥ śubhaḥ
4.d: एषौदिता गृहस्थस्य वृत्तिर्विप्रस्य शाश्वती स्नातकव्रतकल्पश्च सत्त्ववृद्धिकरः शुभः
4.e: Thus has been described the eternal course of life of the Brāhmaṇa-Householder, as also the series of observances for the Accomplished Student, which is conducive to the increase of the quality of goodness, and is praiseworthy.

5.s: anena vipro vṛttena vartayan vedaśāstravit vyapetakalmaṣo nityaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate
5.d: अनेन विप्रो वृत्तेन वर्तयन् वेदशास्त्रवित् व्यपेतकल्मषो नित्यं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते

5.s: śrutvaitān ṛṣayo dharmān snātakasya yathauditān idamūcurmahātmānamanalaprabhavaṃ bhṛgum
5.d: श्रुत्वैतान् ऋषयो धर्मान् स्नातकस्य यथौदितान् इदमूचुर्महात्मानमनलप्रभवं भृगुम्
5.e: The sages, having heard the duties of the Accomplished Student as just described, said this to the high-souled Bhṛgu, who sprang from fire.

5.s: evaṃ yathauktaṃ viprāṇāṃ svadharmamanutiṣṭhatām kathaṃ mṛtyuḥ prabhavati vedaśāstravidāṃ prabho
5.d: एवं यथौक्तं विप्राणां स्वधर्ममनुतिष्ठताम् कथं मृत्युः प्रभवति वेदशास्त्रविदां प्रभो
5.e: “How is it, O Lord, that Death overpowers the Brāhmaṇas who are learned in the Vedic lore, and who perform their duty exactly as it has been thus described?”

5.s: sa tānuvāca dharmātmā maharṣīn mānavo bhṛguḥ śrūyatāṃ yena doṣeṇa mṛtyurviprān jighāṃsati
5.d: स तानुवाच धर्मात्मा महर्षीन् मानवो भृगुः श्रूयतां येन दोषेण मृत्युर्विप्रान् जिघांसति
5.e: Death seeks to destroy the Brāhmaṇas on account of their omitting the study of the Vedas, on account of neglect of right conduct, on account of slothfulness and on account of the defects of food.

5.s: anabhyāsena vedānāmācārasya ca varjanāt ālasyādannadoṣācca mṛtyurviprāñjighāṃsati viprān
5.d: अनभ्यासेन वेदानामाचारस्य च वर्जनात् आलस्यादन्नदोषाच्च मृत्युर्विप्राञ्जिघांसति विप्रान्
5.e: Death seeks to destroy the Brāhmaṇas on account of their omitting the study of the Vedas, on account of neglect of right conduct, on account of slothfulness and on account of the defects of food.

5.s: laśunaṃ gṛñjanaṃ caiva palāṇḍuṃ kavakāni ca abhakṣyāṇi dvijātīnāmamedhyaprabhavāni ca
5.d: लशुनं गृञ्जनं चैव पलाण्डुं कवकानि च अभक्ष्याणि द्विजातीनाममेध्यप्रभवानि च
5.e: Garlic, leeks and onions, mushrooms and all that proceeds from impure things, are unfit to re eaten by twice-born men.

5.s: lohitān vṛkṣaniryāsān vṛścanaprabhavāṃstathā vraścanaprabhavāṃḥ śeluṃ gavyaṃ ca peyūṣaṃ prayatnena vivarjayet pīyūṣaṃ
5.d: लोहितान् वृक्षनिर्यासान् वृश्चनप्रभवांस्तथा व्रश्चनप्रभवांः शेलुं गव्यं च पेयूषं प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् पीयूषं
5.e: He shall carefully avoid the red exudation from trees, as also those flowing from incisions, the śelu berries, and ‘curdled milk’ of the cow.

5.s: vṛthā kṛsarasaṃyāvaṃ pāyasāpūpameva ca anupākṛtamāṃsāni devānnāni havīṃṣi ca
5.d: वृथा कृसरसंयावं पायसापूपमेव च अनुपाकृतमांसानि देवान्नानि हवींषि च
5.e: Needlessly cooked Rice-sesamum and Butter-sugar-sesamum, milk-rice and flour-cakes, unconsecrated meat, food of the gods and sacrificial viands;

5.s: anirdaśāyā goḥ kṣīramauṣṭramaikaśaphaṃ tathā āvikaṃ saṃdhinīkṣīraṃ vivatsāyāśca goḥ payaḥ sandhinīkṣīraṃ
5.d: अनिर्दशाया गोः क्षीरमौष्ट्रमैकशफं तथा आविकं संधिनीक्षीरं विवत्सायाश्च गोः पयः सन्धिनीक्षीरं
5.e: The milk of the cow that has not passed its ten days, as also that of the camel and of one-hoofed animals and of sheep; the milk of the irregular cow, as also the milk of the cow without her calf.

5.s: āraṇyānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ māhiṣaṃ vinā strīkṣīraṃ caiva varjyāni sarvaśuktāni caiva hi
5.d: आरण्यानां च सर्वेषां मृगाणां माहिषं विना स्त्रीक्षीरं चैव वर्ज्यानि सर्वशुक्तानि चैव हि
5.e: That of all wild animals, except the buffalo; the milk of females (women) and all soured substances should be avoided.

5.s: dadhi bhakṣyaṃ ca śukteṣu sarvaṃ ca dadhisaṃbhavam dadhisaṃbhavam yāni caivābhiṣūyante puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ
5.d: दधि भक्ष्यं च शुक्तेषु सर्वं च दधिसंभवम् दधिसंभवम् यानि चैवाभिषूयन्ते पुष्पमूलफलैः शुभैः
5.e: Among Soured Substances, the curd is fit to be eaten, and all that is prepared out of it; as also all that is distilled from pure flowers, roots and fruits;

5.s: kravyādāñ śakunān sarvāntathā grāmanivāsinaḥ kravyādaḥ śakunīn anirdiṣṭāṃścaikaśaphāṃṣ ṭiṭṭibhaṃ ca vivarjayet
5.d: क्रव्यादाञ् शकुनान् सर्वान्तथा ग्रामनिवासिनः क्रव्यादः शकुनीन् अनिर्दिष्टांश्चैकशफांष् टिट्टिभं च विवर्जयेत्
5.e: He shall avoid all carnivorous birds, and also those living in villages, the one-hoofed animals not specified, and also the Ṭiṭṭibha.

5.s: kalaviṅkaṃ plavaṃ haṃsaṃ cakrāhvaṃ grāmakukkuṭam sārasaṃ rajjuvālaṃ ca dātyūhaṃ śukasārike rajjudālaṃ
5.d: कलविङ्कं प्लवं हंसं चक्राह्वं ग्रामकुक्कुटम् सारसं रज्जुवालं च दात्यूहं शुकसारिके रज्जुदालं
5.e: The Sparrow, the Plava, the Haṃsa, the Cakravāka; the village-cock, the Crane, the Rajjudāla, the Dātyūha, the Parrot and the Starling.

5.s: pratudāñjālapādāṃśca koyaṣṭinakhaviṣkirān pratudān nimajjataśca matsyādān saunaṃ vallūrameva ca
5.d: प्रतुदाञ्जालपादांश्च कोयष्टिनखविष्किरान् प्रतुदान् निमज्जतश्च मत्स्यादान् सौनं वल्लूरमेव च
5.e: Those birds that feed by striking with their beaks, those that are web-footed, the koyaṣṭi, those that scratch with their nails, those that dive and eat fish, slaughter-house meat, and dried meat.

5.s: bakaṃ caiva balākāṃ ca kākolaṃ khañjarīṭakam matsyādān viḍvarāhāṃśca matsyāneva ca sarvaśaḥ
5.d: बकं चैव बलाकां च काकोलं खञ्जरीटकम् मत्स्यादान् विड्वराहांश्च मत्स्यानेव च सर्वशः
5.e: The Baka, the Balākā, the Kākola, the Khañjarīṭa, the fish-eaters, and village pigs; as also fish always.

5.s: yo yasya māṃsamaśnāti sa tanmāṃsāda ucyate matsyādaḥ sarvamāṃsādastasmān matsyān vivarjayet
5.d: यो यस्य मांसमश्नाति स तन्मांसाद उच्यते मत्स्यादः सर्वमांसादस्तस्मान् मत्स्यान् विवर्जयेत्
5.e: He who eats the flesh of an animal, is called the ‘eater of its flesh’; he who eats fish is the ‘eater of all kinds of flesh’; hence one shall avoid fish.

5.s: pāṭhīnarohitāvādyau niyuktau havyakavyayoḥ rājīvān siṃhatuṇḍāśca saśalkāścaiva sarvaśaḥ rājīvāḥ
5.d: पाठीनरोहितावाद्यौ नियुक्तौ हव्यकव्ययोः राजीवान् सिंहतुण्डाश्च सशल्काश्चैव सर्वशः राजीवाः
5.e: The ‘Pāṭhīna’ and the ‘Rohita’ are fit to be eaten when used as offerings to gods or Pitṛs; the ‘Rājīva’, the ‘Siṃhatuṇḍa’ and the ‘Saśalka,’ (one may eaṭ) on all occasions

5.s: na bhakṣayedekacarānajñātāṃśca mṛgadvijān bhakṣyeṣvapi samuddiṣṭān sarvān pañcanakhāṃstathā
5.d: न भक्षयेदेकचरानज्ञातांश्च मृगद्विजान् भक्ष्येष्वपि समुद्दिष्टान् सर्वान् पञ्चनखांस्तथा
5.e: He shall not eat solitary animals, nor unknown beasts and birds, even though indicated among those fit to be eaten; nor any five-nailed animals.

5.s: śvāvidhaṃ śalyakaṃ godhāṃ khaḍgakūrmaśaśāṃstathā bhakṣyān pañcanakheṣvāhuranuṣṭrāṃścaikatodataḥ
5.d: श्वाविधं शल्यकं गोधां खड्गकूर्मशशांस्तथा भक्ष्यान् पञ्चनखेष्वाहुरनुष्ट्रांश्चैकतोदतः
5.e: Among five-nailed animals they declare the porcupine, the hedge-hog, the alligator, the rhinoceros, the tortoise and the hare, as fit to be eaten; as also all animals having one line of teeth. except the camel.

5.s: chatrākaṃ viḍvarāhaṃ ca laśunaṃ grāmakukkuṭam palāṇḍuṃ gṛñjanaṃ caiva matyā jagdhvā pateddvijaḥ
5.d: छत्राकं विड्वराहं च लशुनं ग्रामकुक्कुटम् पलाण्डुं गृञ्जनं चैव मत्या जग्ध्वा पतेद्द्विजः
5.e: The mushroom, the village-pig, garlic, the village-cock, onions and leeks,—the twice-born man eating these intentionally would become an ou tcast.

5.s: amatyaitāni ṣaḍ jagdhvā kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret yaticāndrāyāṇaṃ vā 'pi śeṣeṣūpavasedahaḥ
5.d: अमत्यैतानि षड् जग्ध्वा कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं चरेत् यतिचान्द्रायाणं वा ऽपि शेषेषूपवसेदहः
5.e: Having eaten these unintentionally, he should perform the ‘Kṛcchra Sāntapana’, or the ‘Yati-Cāndrāyaṇa’; and in the case of the rest one should fast for a day.

5.s: saṃvatsarasyaikamapi caret kṛcchraṃ dvijottamaḥ ajñātabhuktaśuddhiarthaṃ jñātasya tu viṣeśataḥ
5.d: संवत्सरस्यैकमपि चरेत् कृच्छ्रं द्विजोत्तमः अज्ञातभुक्तशुद्धिअर्थं ज्ञातस्य तु विषेशतः
5.e: Once a year the Brāhmaṇa shall perform the ‘Kṛcchra’ penance, in order to atone for unintentional eating; but for intentional eating, special ones.

5.s: yajñārthaṃ brāhmaṇairvadhyāḥ praśastā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ bhṛtyānāṃ caiva vṛttiarthamagastyo hyācarat purā
5.d: यज्ञार्थं ब्राह्मणैर्वध्याः प्रशस्ता मृगपक्षिणः भृत्यानां चैव वृत्तिअर्थमगस्त्यो ह्याचरत् पुरा
5.e: The commended beasts and birds may be killed by Brāhmaṇas for the purpose of sacrifice, and for the purpose of feeding their dependents; as Agastya did this of old.

5.s: babhūvurhi puroḍāśā bhakṣyāṇāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām purāṇeṣvapi yajñeṣu brahmakṣatrasaveṣu ca purāṇeṣvṛṣiyajñeṣu
5.d: बभूवुर्हि पुरोडाशा भक्ष्याणां मृगपक्षिणाम् पुराणेष्वपि यज्ञेषु ब्रह्मक्षत्रसवेषु च पुराणेष्वृषियज्ञेषु
5.e: In ancient times, at sacrifices performed by the sages, as also at sacrifices performed by Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas, the sacrificial cakes were made of eatable beasts and birds.

5.s: yat kiṃ cit snehasaṃyuktaṃ bhakṣyaṃ bhojyamagarhitam tat paryuṣitamapyādyaṃ haviḥśeṣaṃ ca yadbhavet
5.d: यत् किं चित् स्नेहसंयुक्तं भक्ष्यं भोज्यमगर्हितम् तत् पर्युषितमप्याद्यं हविःशेषं च यद्भवेत्
5.e: Such Food and eatables as are mixed with oils may be eaten though stale, if unspoilt; so also what may be the remnant of a sacrificial offering.

5.s: cirasthitamapi tvādyamasnehāktaṃ dvijātibhiḥ yavagodhūmajaṃ sarvaṃ payasaścaiva vikriyā
5.d: चिरस्थितमपि त्वाद्यमस्नेहाक्तं द्विजातिभिः यवगोधूमजं सर्वं पयसश्चैव विक्रिया
5.e: All that is made of barley and wheat, as also all preparations of milk, may be eaten by twice-born men, without being mixed with oils, even though they may have been kept long

5.s: etaduktaṃ dvijātīnāṃ bhakṣyābhakṣyamaśeṣataḥ māṃsasyātaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ bhakṣaṇavarjane
5.d: एतदुक्तं द्विजातीनां भक्ष्याभक्ष्यमशेषतः मांसस्यातः प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं भक्षणवर्जने
5.e: Thus has been described is full what is fit and what unfit to be eaten by twice-born men. Next I am going to explain the rule regarding the eating and avoiding of meat.

5.s: prokṣitaṃ bhakṣayen māṃsaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca kāmyayā yathāvidhi niyuktastu prāṇānāmeva cātyaye
5.d: प्रोक्षितं भक्षयेन् मांसं ब्राह्मणानां च काम्यया यथाविधि नियुक्तस्तु प्राणानामेव चात्यये
5.e: He may eat meat that has been consecrated; also at the wish of Brāhmaṇas; and when invited according to law; and when his life is in danger.

5.s: prāṇasyānnamidaṃ sarvaṃ prajāpatirakalpayat sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva sarvaṃ prāṇasya bhojanam
5.d: प्राणस्यान्नमिदं सर्वं प्रजापतिरकल्पयत् स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव सर्वं प्राणस्य भोजनम्
5.e: Prajāpati created all this as food for the vital spirit; and all that is movable or immovable is the food of the vital spirit

5.s: carāṇāmannamacarā daṃṣṭriṇāmapyadaṃṣṭriṇaḥ ahastāśca sahastānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ caiva bhīravaḥ
5.d: चराणामन्नमचरा दंष्ट्रिणामप्यदंष्ट्रिणः अहस्ताश्च सहस्तानां शूराणां चैव भीरवः
5.e: The immobile is the food of the mobile; those devoid of fangs are the food of those endowed with fangs; those without hands are the food of those with hands; and cowards are the food of the brave.

5.s: nāttā duṣyatyadannādyān prāṇino 'hany 'hanyapi dhātraiva sṛṣṭā hyādyāśca prāṇino 'ttāra eva ca
5.d: नात्ता दुष्यत्यदन्नाद्यान् प्राणिनो ऽहन्य् ऽहन्यपि धात्रैव सृष्टा ह्याद्याश्च प्राणिनो ऽत्तार एव च
5.e: The eater incurs no sin by eating, even daily, such animals as are eatable: since the eater as well as the eaten animals have been created by the creator himself

5.s: yajñāya jagdhirmāṃsasyaityeṣa daivo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ato 'nyathā pravṛttistu rākṣaso vidhirucyate
5.d: यज्ञाय जग्धिर्मांसस्यैत्येष दैवो विधिः स्मृतः अतो ऽन्यथा प्रवृत्तिस्तु राक्षसो विधिरुच्यते
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: krītvā svayaṃ vā 'pyutpādya paraupakṛtameva vā devān pitr̥̄ṃścārcayitvā khādan māṃsaṃ na duṣyati
5.d: क्रीत्वा स्वयं वा ऽप्युत्पाद्य परौपकृतमेव वा देवान् पित्र्̥̄ंश्चार्चयित्वा खादन् मांसं न दुष्यति
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: nādyādavidhinā māṃsaṃ vidhijño 'nāpadi dvijaḥ jagdhvā hyavidhinā māṃsaṃ pretastairadyate 'vaśaḥ
5.d: नाद्यादविधिना मांसं विधिज्ञो ऽनापदि द्विजः जग्ध्वा ह्यविधिना मांसं प्रेतस्तैरद्यते ऽवशः
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: na tādṛśaṃ bhavatyeno mṛgahanturdhanārthinaḥ yādṛśaṃ bhavati pretya vṛthāmāṃsāni khādataḥ
5.d: न तादृशं भवत्येनो मृगहन्तुर्धनार्थिनः यादृशं भवति प्रेत्य वृथामांसानि खादतः
5.e: The sin of the man who kills animals for gain is not so great, after death, as that of the man who eats needlessly-prepared meat.

5.s: niyuktastu yathānyāyaṃ yo māṃsaṃ nātti mānavaḥ sa pretya paśutāṃ yāti saṃbhavānekaviṃśatim
5.d: नियुक्तस्तु यथान्यायं यो मांसं नात्ति मानवः स प्रेत्य पशुतां याति संभवानेकविंशतिम्
5.e: But when invited according to law, if a man does not e at meat, he becomes, after death, a beast, during twenty- one births.

5.s: asaṃskṛtān paśūn mantrairnādyādvipraḥ kadā cana mantraistu saṃskṛtānadyātśāśvataṃ vidhimāsthitaḥ
5.d: असंस्कृतान् पशून् मन्त्रैर्नाद्याद्विप्रः कदा चन मन्त्रैस्तु संस्कृतानद्यात्शाश्वतं विधिमास्थितः
5.e: The Brāhmaṇa shall never eat animals that have not been consecrated with sacred texts; but those that have been consecrated with sacred texts, he shall eat, taking, his stand upon the eternal law.

5.s: kuryādghṛtapaśuṃ saṅge kuryāt piṣṭapaśuṃ tathā na tveva tu vṛthā hantuṃ paśumicchet kadā cana
5.d: कुर्याद्घृतपशुं सङ्गे कुर्यात् पिष्टपशुं तथा न त्वेव तु वृथा हन्तुं पशुमिच्छेत् कदा चन
5.e: If there is occasion, he shall make an animal of clarified butter, or an animal of flour; but he shall never seek to kill an animal needlessly.

5.s: yāvanti paśuromāṇi tāvatkṛtvo ha māraṇam vṛthāpaśughnaḥ prāpnoti pretya janmani janmani
5.d: यावन्ति पशुरोमाणि तावत्कृत्वो ह मारणम् वृथापशुघ्नः प्राप्नोति प्रेत्य जन्मनि जन्मनि
5.e: As many hairs there are on the body of the animal, so m any times after dying does its needless killer suffer violent death, birth after birth.—(38.)

5.s: yajñārthaṃ paśavaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayameva svayaṃbhuvā yajño 'sya bhūtyai sarvasya tasmādyajñe vadho 'vadhaḥ
5.d: यज्ञार्थं पशवः सृष्टाः स्वयमेव स्वयंभुवा यज्ञो ऽस्य भूत्यै सर्वस्य तस्माद्यज्ञे वधो ऽवधः
5.e: Animals have been created by the Self-born God himself for the purpose of sacrifice: sacrifice is conducive to the well-being of all this would; hence killing at a sacrifice is no ‘killing’ at all

5.s: oṣadhyaḥ paśavo vṛkṣāstiryañcaḥ pakṣiṇastathā yajñārthaṃ nidhanaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvantyutsṛtīḥ punaḥ ucchritīḥ
5.d: ओषध्यः पशवो वृक्षास्तिर्यञ्चः पक्षिणस्तथा यज्ञार्थं निधनं प्राप्ताः प्राप्नुवन्त्युत्सृतीः पुनः उच्छ्रितीः
5.e: Herbs, animals, trees, beasts and birds, reaching death for the sake of sacrifices, attain advancements.

5.s: madhuparke ca yajñe ca pitṛdaivatakarmaṇi atraiva paśavo hiṃsyā nānyatraityabravīn manuḥ
5.d: मधुपर्के च यज्ञे च पितृदैवतकर्मणि अत्रैव पशवो हिंस्या नान्यत्रैत्यब्रवीन् मनुः
5.e: The twice-born person, knowing the real import of the Veda, killing animals on these occasions, carries himself and the animal to the most excellent state.

5.s: eṣvartheṣu paśūn hiṃsan vedatattvārthaviddvijaḥ ātmānaṃ ca paśuṃ caiva gamayatyuttamaṃ gatim
5.d: एष्वर्थेषु पशून् हिंसन् वेदतत्त्वार्थविद्द्विजः आत्मानं च पशुं चैव गमयत्युत्तमं गतिम्
5.e: The twice-born person, knowing the real import of the Veda, killing animals on these occasions, carries himself and the animal to the most excellent state.

5.s: gṛhe gurāvaraṇye vā nivasannātmavān dvijaḥ nāvedavihitāṃ hiṃsāmāpadyapi samācaret
5.d: गृहे गुरावरण्ये वा निवसन्नात्मवान् द्विजः नावेदविहितां हिंसामापद्यपि समाचरेत्
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: yā vedavihitā hiṃsā niyatā 'smiṃścarācare ahiṃsāmeva tāṃ vidyādvedāddharmo hi nirbabhau
5.d: या वेदविहिता हिंसा नियता ऽस्मिंश्चराचरे अहिंसामेव तां विद्याद्वेदाद्धर्मो हि निर्बभौ
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: yo 'hiṃsakāni bhūtāni hinastyātmasukhaicchayā sa jīvāṃśca mṛtaścaiva na kva cit sukhamedhate
5.d: यो ऽहिंसकानि भूतानि हिनस्त्यात्मसुखैच्छया स जीवांश्च मृतश्चैव न क्व चित् सुखमेधते
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: yo bandhanavadhakleśān prāṇināṃ na cikīrṣati sa sarvasya hitaprepsuḥ sukhamatyantamaśnute
5.d: यो बन्धनवधक्लेशान् प्राणिनां न चिकीर्षति स सर्वस्य हितप्रेप्सुः सुखमत्यन्तमश्नुते
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: yaddhyāyati yat kurute ratiṃ badhnāti yatra ca tadavāpnotyayatnena yo hinasti na kiṃ cana
5.d: यद्ध्यायति यत् कुरुते रतिं बध्नाति यत्र च तदवाप्नोत्ययत्नेन यो हिनस्ति न किं चन
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: nākṛtvā prāṇināṃ hiṃsāṃ māṃsamutpadyate kva cit na ca prāṇivadhaḥ svargyastasmān māṃsaṃ vivarjayet
5.d: नाकृत्वा प्राणिनां हिंसां मांसमुत्पद्यते क्व चित् न च प्राणिवधः स्वर्ग्यस्तस्मान् मांसं विवर्जयेत्
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: samutpattiṃ ca māṃsasya vadhabandhau ca dehinām prasamīkṣya nivarteta sarvamāṃsasya bhakṣaṇāt
5.d: समुत्पत्तिं च मांसस्य वधबन्धौ च देहिनाम् प्रसमीक्ष्य निवर्तेत सर्वमांसस्य भक्षणात्
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: na bhakṣayati yo māṃsaṃ vidhiṃ hitvā piśācavat na loke priyatāṃ yāti vyādhibhiśca na pīḍyate
5.d: न भक्षयति यो मांसं विधिं हित्वा पिशाचवत् न लोके प्रियतां याति व्याधिभिश्च न पीड्यते
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: anumantā viśasitā nihantā krayavikrayī saṃskartā caupahartā ca khādakaścaiti ghātakāḥ
5.d: अनुमन्ता विशसिता निहन्ता क्रयविक्रयी संस्कर्ता चौपहर्ता च खादकश्चैति घातकाः
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsena yo vardhayitumicchati anabhyarcya pitr̥̄n devāṃstato 'nyo nāstyapuṇyakṛt
5.d: स्वमांसं परमांसेन यो वर्धयितुमिच्छति अनभ्यर्च्य पित्र्̥̄न् देवांस्ततो ऽन्यो नास्त्यपुण्यकृत्
5.e: Sanskrit text, Unicode transliteration and English translation by Ganganath Jha:

5.s: varṣe varṣe 'śvamedhena yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ māṃsāni ca na khādedyastayoḥ puṇyaphalaṃ samam
5.d: वर्षे वर्षे ऽश्वमेधेन यो यजेत शतं समाः मांसानि च न खादेद्यस्तयोः पुण्यफलं समम्
5.e: If a man performs the Aśvamedha Sacrifice every year, for a hundred tears,—and another does not eat meat,—the merit and reward of both these are the same.—(53.)

5.s: phalamūlāśanairmedhyairmuniannānāṃ ca bhojanaiḥ na tat phalamavāpnoti yatmāṃsaparivarjanāt
5.d: फलमूलाशनैर्मेध्यैर्मुनिअन्नानां च भोजनैः न तत् फलमवाप्नोति यत्मांसपरिवर्जनात्
5.e: By subsisting upon sacred fruits and roots, and by eating the food of hermits, one does not obtain that reward which he does by abstaining from meat

5.s: māṃ sa bhakṣayitā 'mutra yasya māṃsamihādmyaham etatmāṃsasya māṃsatvaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
5.d: मां स भक्षयिता ऽमुत्र यस्य मांसमिहाद्म्यहम् एतत्मांसस्य मांसत्वं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः
5.e: ‘Me he (māṃ-sa) will devour in the next world, whose meat I eat in this’—this is the ‘meatness’ (māṃsatva) of the ‘meat’ (māṃsa), as the wise ones declare.

5.s: na māṃsabhakṣaṇe doṣo na madye na ca maithune pravṛttireṣā bhūtānāṃ nivṛttistu mahāphalā
5.d: न मांसभक्षणे दोषो न मद्ये न च मैथुने प्रवृत्तिरेषा भूतानां निवृत्तिस्तु महाफला
5.e: There is no sin in the eating of meat, nor in wine, nor in sexual intercourse. Such is the natural way of living beings; but abstention is conducive to great rewards.

5.s: pretaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi dravyaśuddhiṃ tathaiva ca caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ
5.d: प्रेतशुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि द्रव्यशुद्धिं तथैव च चतुर्णामपि वर्णानां यथावदनुपूर्वशः
5.e: I am going to describe, in due order, purification on death, as also purification of substances, as prescribed for all the four castes.

5.s: dantajāte 'nujāte ca kṛtacūḍe ca saṃsthite aśuddhā bāndhavāḥ sarve sūtake ca tathaucyate
5.d: दन्तजाते ऽनुजाते च कृतचूडे च संस्थिते अशुद्धा बान्धवाः सर्वे सूतके च तथौच्यते
5.e: When a child dies that has teethed, or one younger than it when its tonsure has been performed, all its relatives are ‘impure’. The same is declared to be the case with births also.

5.s: daśāhaṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate arvāk sañcayanādasthnāṃ tryahamekāhameva vā
5.d: दशाहं शावमाशौचं सपिण्डेषु विधीयते अर्वाक् सञ्चयनादस्थ्नां त्र्यहमेकाहमेव वा
5.e: Among ‘Sapiṇḍas’. the period of impurity due to death is ordained to last for ten days; or till the collecting of the bones, or for three days, or for one day only

5.s: sapiṇḍatā tu puruṣe saptame vinivartate samānodakabhāvastu janmanāmnoravedane
5.d: सपिण्डता तु पुरुषे सप्तमे विनिवर्तते समानोदकभावस्तु जन्मनाम्नोरवेदने
5.e: The ‘Sapiṇḍa-relationship’ ceases with the person in the seventh-degree and the ‘Samānodaka-relationship,’ when the origin and the name become unrecognisable

5.s: yathaidaṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate janane 'pyevameva syātnipuṇaṃ śuddhimicchatām
5.d: यथैदं शावमाशौचं सपिण्डेषु विधीयते जनने ऽप्येवमेव स्यात्निपुणं शुद्धिमिच्छताम्
5.e: Thus also should it be at a birth; but the parturient disability attaches to the parents only; or, the parturient disability would attach to the mother alone, and the father would become purified by bathing.

5.s: sarveṣāṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ mātāpitrostu sūtakam janane 'pyevameva syān mātāpitrostu sūtakaṃ sūtakaṃ mātureva syādupaspṛśya pitā śuciḥ
5.d: सर्वेषां शावमाशौचं मातापित्रोस्तु सूतकम् जनने ऽप्येवमेव स्यान् मातापित्रोस्तु सूतकं सूतकं मातुरेव स्यादुपस्पृश्य पिता शुचिः
5.e: The man, having emitted semen becomes pure by bathing; hence, on account of seminal filiation he should observe impurity for these days.

5.s: nirasya tu pumāṃśukramupaspṛsyaiva śudhyati baijikādabhisaṃbandhādanurundhyādaghaṃ tryaham
5.d: निरस्य तु पुमांशुक्रमुपस्पृस्यैव शुध्यति बैजिकादभिसंबन्धादनुरुन्ध्यादघं त्र्यहम्
5.e: Those who touch this corpse become pure after one day and one day along with three three-day periods; those who offer water, after three days.

5.s: ahnā caikena rātryā ca trirātraireva ca tribhiḥ śavaspṛśo viśudhyanti tryahādudakadāyinaḥ
5.d: अह्ना चैकेन रात्र्या च त्रिरात्रैरेव च त्रिभिः शवस्पृशो विशुध्यन्ति त्र्यहादुदकदायिनः
5.e: The pupil performing the ‘Pitṛmedha’ for his dead Teacher becomes purified in ten days; just as those who carry the dead body.

5.s: guroḥ pretasya śiṣyastu pitṛmedhaṃ samācaran pretahāraiḥ samaṃ tatra daśarātreṇa śudhyati pretāhāraiḥ
5.d: गुरोः प्रेतस्य शिष्यस्तु पितृमेधं समाचरन् प्रेतहारैः समं तत्र दशरात्रेण शुध्यति प्रेताहारैः
5.e: In the case of miscarriage, the woman becomes pure in so mamy days as there have been months; and the woman in her courses becomes fit by bathing after the ceasing of the menstrual flow.

5.s: rātribhirmāsatulyābhirgarbhasrāve viśudhyati rajasyuparate sādhvī snānena strī rajasvalā
5.d: रात्रिभिर्मासतुल्याभिर्गर्भस्रावे विशुध्यति रजस्युपरते साध्वी स्नानेन स्त्री रजस्वला
5.e: In the case of persons whose tonsure has not been performed purification has been declared to come after a night; but in the case of those whose tonsure has been performed, purification is held to come after three days.

5.s: nṛṇāmakṛtacūḍānāṃ viśuddhirnaiśikī smṛtā nirvṛttacūḍakānāṃ tu trirātrātśuddhiriṣyate nirvṛttamuṇḍakānāṃ
5.d: नृणामकृतचूडानां विशुद्धिर्नैशिकी स्मृता निर्वृत्तचूडकानां तु त्रिरात्रात्शुद्धिरिष्यते निर्वृत्तमुण्डकानां
5.e: The child that dies while less than two years old, the relations should, after having decked it, place outside, under the ground that is clean and not defiled by heaps of bones.

5.s: ūnadvivārṣikaṃ pretaṃ nidadhyurbāndhavā bahiḥ alaṅkṛtya śucau bhūmāvasthisañcayanādṛte
5.d: ऊनद्विवार्षिकं प्रेतं निदध्युर्बान्धवा बहिः अलङ्कृत्य शुचौ भूमावस्थिसञ्चयनादृते
5.e: For this child no sanctification by fire shall be performed; nor shall water-offering he made to it; having left it like a log of wood, in the forest, one shall keep aloof for three days.

5.s: nāsya kāryo 'gnisaṃskāro na ca kāryaudakakriyā araṇye kāṣṭhavat tyaktvā kṣapeyustryahameva tu kṣapeta tryahameva ca
5.d: नास्य कार्यो ऽग्निसंस्कारो न च कार्यौदकक्रिया अरण्ये काष्ठवत् त्यक्त्वा क्षपेयुस्त्र्यहमेव तु क्षपेत त्र्यहमेव च
5.e: For the child up to three years of age, the relations shall not make water-offerings; but for one whose teeth had appeared, or whose naming had been done, it may be done optionally.

5.s: nātrivarṣasya kartavyā bāndhavairudakakriyā jātadantasya vā kuryurnāmni vā 'pi kṛte sati
5.d: नात्रिवर्षस्य कर्तव्या बान्धवैरुदकक्रिया जातदन्तस्य वा कुर्युर्नाम्नि वा ऽपि कृते सति
5.e: On the death of a fellow-student, the impurity has been declared to last for one day. In the case of a birth, the purity of the ‘Samānopaka’ relations is held to come after three pays.

5.s: sabrahmacāriṇyekāhamatīte kṣapaṇaṃ smṛtam janmanyekaudakānāṃ tu trirātrātśuddhiriṣyate
5.d: सब्रह्मचारिण्येकाहमतीते क्षपणं स्मृतम् जन्मन्येकौदकानां तु त्रिरात्रात्शुद्धिरिष्यते
5.e: In the case of women whose sacramentary rite has not been performed, the marital relations become pure after three days; and their paternal relations also become pure according to the rule prescribed before

5.s: strīṇāmasaṃskṛtānāṃ tu tryahātśudhyanti bāndhavāḥ yathauktenaiva kalpena śudhyanti tu sanābhayaḥ
5.d: स्त्रीणामसंस्कृतानां तु त्र्यहात्शुध्यन्ति बान्धवाः यथौक्तेनैव कल्पेन शुध्यन्ति तु सनाभयः
5.e: For three days they should eat food free from salines and salts, should bathe, should not eat meat-food and should sleep apart on the ground.

5.s: akṣāralavaṇānnāḥ syurnimajjeyuśca te tryaham māṃsāśanaṃ ca nāśnīyuḥ śayīraṃśca pṛthak kṣitau
5.d: अक्षारलवणान्नाः स्युर्निमज्जेयुश्च ते त्र्यहम् मांसाशनं च नाश्नीयुः शयीरंश्च पृथक् क्षितौ
5.e: This rule regarding Impurity due to death has been described in reference to cases where the parties are near one another. In reference to cases where they are not near, Kinsmen and relations should observe the following rule.

5.s: saṃnidhāveṣa vai kalpaḥ śāvāśaucasya kīrtitaḥ asaṃnidhāvayaṃ jñeyo vidhiḥ saṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ
5.d: संनिधावेष वै कल्पः शावाशौचस्य कीर्तितः असंनिधावयं ज्ञेयो विधिः संबन्धिबान्धवैः
5.e: He who hears, within ten days, of a relation resident in a foreign land having died, shall, remain impure for the remainder of the period of ten days.

5.s: vigataṃ tu videśasthaṃ śṛṇuyādyo hyanirdaśam yatśeṣaṃ daśarātrasya tāvadevāśucirbhavet
5.d: विगतं तु विदेशस्थं शृणुयाद्यो ह्यनिर्दशम् यत्शेषं दशरात्रस्य तावदेवाशुचिर्भवेत्
5.e: If the period of ten days has elapsed, he shall remain impure for three days; but when a year has elapsed, he becomes pure by merely touching water.

5.s: atikrānte daśāhe ca trirātramaśucirbhavet saṃvatsare vyatīte tu spṛṣṭvaivāpo viśudhyati
5.d: अतिक्रान्ते दशाहे च त्रिरात्रमशुचिर्भवेत् संवत्सरे व्यतीते तु स्पृष्ट्वैवापो विशुध्यति
5.e: Hearing of the death of a kinsman, or of the birth of a son, after the ten days have elapsed, the man becomes pure by plunging into water with his clothes

5.s: nirdaśaṃ jñātimaraṇaṃ śrutvā putrasya janma ca savāsā jalamāplutya śuddho bhavati mānavaḥ
5.d: निर्दशं ज्ञातिमरणं श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य जन्म च सवासा जलमाप्लुत्य शुद्धो भवति मानवः
5.e: In the event of a child, resident in a foreign country, who is a non-sapiṇḍa relation, dying,—one becomes pure immediately, by plunging into water wth his clothes on.

5.s: bāle deśāntarasthe ca pṛthakpiṇḍe ca saṃsthite savāsā jalamāplutya sadya eva viśudhyati
5.d: बाले देशान्तरस्थे च पृथक्पिण्डे च संस्थिते सवासा जलमाप्लुत्य सद्य एव विशुध्यति
5.e: If, within ten days, another birth or death happen to befall, the Brāhmaṇa shall remain impure until that period of ten days shall have elapsed.

5.s: antardaśāhe syātāṃ cet punarmaraṇajanmanī cet syātāṃ tāvat syādaśucirvipro yāvat tat syādanirdaśam
5.d: अन्तर्दशाहे स्यातां चेत् पुनर्मरणजन्मनी चेत् स्यातां तावत् स्यादशुचिर्विप्रो यावत् तत् स्यादनिर्दशम्
5.e: On the death of the Teacher, they declare the impurity to last for three days; on the death of his son or wife, it lasts for one day and night; such is the law.

5.s: trirātramāhurāśaucamācārye saṃsthite sati tasya putre ca patnyāṃ ca divārātramiti sthitiḥ
5.d: त्रिरात्रमाहुराशौचमाचार्ये संस्थिते सति तस्य पुत्रे च पत्न्यां च दिवारात्रमिति स्थितिः
5.e: In the case of a learned companion, one shall remain impure for three days; in the case of a maternal uncle, a pupil, an officiating priest and relation, for a night along with the two days (preceding and following it).

5.s: śrotriye tūpasaṃpanne trirātramaśucirbhavet mātule pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ śiṣyaṛtvigbāndhaveṣu ca
5.d: श्रोत्रिये तूपसंपन्ने त्रिरात्रमशुचिर्भवेत् मातुले पक्षिणीं रात्रिं शिष्यऋत्विग्बान्धवेषु च
5.e: On the death of the King in whose realm he lives, it lasts till the light; in the case of a non-learned teacher, for the whole day; as also in the case of the (ordinary) teacher.

5.s: prete rājani sajyotiryasya syādviṣaye sthitaḥ aśrotriye tvahaḥ kṛtsnamanūcāne tathā gurau kṛtsnāṃ
5.d: प्रेते राजनि सज्योतिर्यस्य स्याद्विषये स्थितः अश्रोत्रिये त्वहः कृत्स्नमनूचाने तथा गुरौ कृत्स्नां
5.e: The Brāhmaṇa becomes pure in the days, the Kṣatriya in twelve days, the Vaiśya in fifteen days and the Śūdra in a month.

5.s: śuddhyedvipro daśāhena dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śudhyati
5.d: शुद्ध्येद्विप्रो दशाहेन द्वादशाहेन भूमिपः वैश्यः पञ्चदशाहेन शूद्रो मासेन शुध्यति
5.e: One should not prolong the days of impurity; nor should he interrupt the rites performed in the fires; because he who performs those rites, even if he be a Sapiṇḍa, would never he impure.

5.s: na vardhayedaghāhāni pratyūhennāgniṣu kriyāḥ na ca tatkarma kurvāṇaḥ sanābhyo 'pyaśucirbhavet
5.d: न वर्धयेदघाहानि प्रत्यूहेन्नाग्निषु क्रियाः न च तत्कर्म कुर्वाणः सनाभ्यो ऽप्यशुचिर्भवेत्
5.e: After having touched the Cāndāla, the menstruating woman, the outcast, the woman in child-bed, the dead body, or toucher thereof—one becomes pure by bathing.

5.s: divākīrtimudakyāṃ ca patitaṃ sūtikāṃ tathā śavaṃ tatspṛṣṭinaṃ caiva spṛṣṭvā snānena śudhyati
5.d: दिवाकीर्तिमुदक्यां च पतितं सूतिकां तथा शवं तत्स्पृष्टिनं चैव स्पृष्ट्वा स्नानेन शुध्यति
5.e: On seeing unclean things, the man, after having sipped water, shall always attentively recite the Solar Mantras according to his inclination, as also the Pāvamānī verses, according to his capacity.

5.s: ācamya prayato nityaṃ japedaśucidarśane saurān mantrān yathautsāhaṃ pāvamānīśca śaktitaḥ
5.d: आचम्य प्रयतो नित्यं जपेदशुचिदर्शने सौरान् मन्त्रान् यथौत्साहं पावमानीश्च शक्तितः
5.e: Having touched a fatty human bone, the Brāhmaṇa becomes pure by bathing, but if it be free from fat, then by sipping water and touching a cow, or looking at the sun

5.s: nāraṃ spṛṣṭvā 'sthi sasnehaṃ snātvā vipro viśudhyati ācamyaiva tu niḥsnehaṃ gāmālabhyārkamīkṣya vā
5.d: नारं स्पृष्ट्वा ऽस्थि सस्नेहं स्नात्वा विप्रो विशुध्यति आचम्यैव तु निःस्नेहं गामालभ्यार्कमीक्ष्य वा
5.e: The person under instruction shall not make water-offerings till the completion of his pupilage; at its completion, he becomes pure in three days, after having made the water-offerings.

5.s: ādiṣṭī naudakaṃ kuryādā vratasya samāpanāt samāpte tūdakaṃ kṛtvā trirātreṇaiva śudhyati
5.d: आदिष्टी नौदकं कुर्यादा व्रतस्य समापनात् समाप्ते तूदकं कृत्वा त्रिरात्रेणैव शुध्यति
5.e: The water-offering is withdrawn from those born in vain and from intermixture, from those who are addicted to asceticism and from those who have abandoned themselves.

5.s: vṛthāsaṅkarajātānāṃ pravrajyāsu ca tiṣṭhatām ātmanastyāgināṃ caiva nivartetaudakakriyā
5.d: वृथासङ्करजातानां प्रव्रज्यासु च तिष्ठताम् आत्मनस्त्यागिनां चैव निवर्तेतौदकक्रिया
5.e: Also from women, who have joined a heretic, who behave too freely, who have injured a child in their womb or their husband, and those who drink wine

5.s: pāṣaṇḍamāśritānāṃ ca carantīnāṃ ca kāmataḥ garbhabhartṛdruhāṃ caiva surāpīnāṃ ca yoṣitām
5.d: पाषण्डमाश्रितानां च चरन्तीनां च कामतः गर्भभर्तृद्रुहां चैव सुरापीनां च योषिताम्
5.e: The student, carrying his own dead Teacher, or tutor, or father, or mother, or monitor,—does not suffer in his observances.

5.s: ācāryaṃ svamupādhyāyaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum nirhṛtya tu vratī pretānna vratena viyujyate
5.d: आचार्यं स्वमुपाध्यायं पितरं मातरं गुरुम् निर्हृत्य तु व्रती प्रेतान्न व्रतेन वियुज्यते
5.e: One should carry the dead śūdra by the southern gate of the city; but the twice-born persons by the western, northern and eastern gates respectively

5.s: dakṣiṇena mṛtaṃ śūdraṃ puradvāreṇa nirharet paścimauttarapūrvaistu yathāyogaṃ dvijanmanaḥ
5.d: दक्षिणेन मृतं शूद्रं पुरद्वारेण निर्हरेत् पश्चिमौत्तरपूर्वैस्तु यथायोगं द्विजन्मनः
5.e: This taint of uncleanliness does not attach to Kings, or to those keeping a vow, or to the performers of sacrificial sessions; because they occupy the position of sovereigns and are ever of the nature of Brahman.

5.s: na rājñāmaghadoṣo 'sti vratināṃ na ca sattriṇām aindraṃ sthānamupāsīnā brahmabhūtā hi te sadā
5.d: न राज्ञामघदोषो ऽस्ति व्रतिनां न च सत्त्रिणाम् ऐन्द्रं स्थानमुपासीना ब्रह्मभूता हि ते सदा
5.e: Immediate purification has been ordained for the king on the majestic throne; and the reason for this lies in his occupying that position for the protection of the people.

5.s: rājño mahātmike sthāne sadyaḥśaucaṃ vidhīyate prajānāṃ parirakṣārthamāsanaṃ cātra kāraṇam
5.d: राज्ञो महात्मिके स्थाने सद्यःशौचं विधीयते प्रजानां परिरक्षार्थमासनं चात्र कारणम्
5.e: Also in the case of those killed in a riot or Battle or by lightning or by the king; and of those who have died for the sake of cows and Brāhmaṇas; as also for the person for whom the king desires it.

5.s: ḍimbhāhavahatānāṃ ca vidyutā pārthivena ca ḍimbāhavahatānāṃ gobrāhmaṇasya caivārthe yasya caicchati pārthivaḥ
5.d: डिम्भाहवहतानां च विद्युता पार्थिवेन च डिम्बाहवहतानां गोब्राह्मणस्य चैवार्थे यस्य चैच्छति पार्थिवः
5.e: The King holds in himself the body of the eight guardian deities of the world, of the Moon, the Fire, the Sun, the Wind, Indra, the Lord of Wealth, the Lord of Water, and of Yama.

5.s: somāgniarkānilaindrāṇāṃ vittāppatyoryamasya ca aṣṭānāṃ lokapālānāṃ vapurdhārayate nṛpaḥ
5.d: सोमाग्निअर्कानिलैन्द्राणां वित्ताप्पत्योर्यमस्य च अष्टानां लोकपालानां वपुर्धारयते नृपः
5.e: The King is possessed by the Lords of the World; no im purity, therefore, has been ordained for him; for the purity and impurity affect mortals and have their origin and end in the worldly regions.

5.s: lokeśādhiṣṭhito rājā nāsyāśaucaṃ vidhīyate śaucāśaucaṃ hi martyānāṃ lokebhyaḥ prabhavāpyayau
5.d: लोकेशाधिष्ठितो राजा नास्याशौचं विधीयते शौचाशौचं हि मर्त्यानां लोकेभ्यः प्रभवाप्ययौ
5.e: For one who is killed in battle with brandished weapons, in the manner befitting the kṣatriya, sacrificial performances become instantly completed; and so also is the impurity; such is the established law

5.s: udyatairāhave śastraiḥ kṣatradharmahatasya ca sadyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yajñastathā 'śaucamiti sthitiḥ
5.d: उद्यतैराहवे शस्त्रैः क्षत्रधर्महतस्य च सद्यः संतिष्ठते यज्ञस्तथा ऽशौचमिति स्थितिः
5.e: The Brāhmaṇa becomes purified by touching water; the Kṣatriya by touching his conveyance and weapons; the vaiśya by touching either the goad or the leading-strings; and the Śūdra by touching the stick,—after he has performed the rite

5.s: vipraḥ śudhyatyapaḥ spṛṣṭvā kṣatriyo vāhanāyudham vaiśyaḥ pratodaṃ raśmīn vā yaṣṭiṃ śūdraḥ kṛtakriyaḥ
5.d: विप्रः शुध्यत्यपः स्पृष्ट्वा क्षत्रियो वाहनायुधम् वैश्यः प्रतोदं रश्मीन् वा यष्टिं शूद्रः कृतक्रियः
5.e: O Best or Brāhmaṇas, thus has been described to you the purification necesssary in the case of ‘Sapiṇḍa-relations.’

5.s: etadvo 'bhihitaṃ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu dvijottamāḥ asapiṇḍeṣu sarveṣu pretaśuddhiṃ nibodhata
5.d: एतद्वो ऽभिहितं शौचं सपिण्डेषु द्विजोत्तमाः असपिण्डेषु सर्वेषु प्रेतशुद्धिं निबोधत
5.e: A Brāhmaṇa, having carried, like a relation, a dead Brāhmaṇa who is not his ‘Sapiṇḍa’ relation,—or the near relatives of his mother,—becomes pure in three days.

5.s: asapiṇḍaṃ dvijaṃ pretaṃ vipro nirhṛtya bandhuvat viśudhyati trirātreṇa māturāptāṃśca bāndhavān
5.d: असपिण्डं द्विजं प्रेतं विप्रो निर्हृत्य बन्धुवत् विशुध्यति त्रिरात्रेण मातुराप्तांश्च बान्धवान्
5.e: But if he eats their food, he becomes pure in ten days; if however he does not eat their food, he is purified in one day, if he does not dwell in that house.

5.s: yadyannamatti teṣāṃ tu daśāhenaiva śudhyati anadannannamahnaiva na cet tasmin gṛhe vaset
5.d: यद्यन्नमत्ति तेषां तु दशाहेनैव शुध्यति अनदन्नन्नमह्नैव न चेत् तस्मिन् गृहे वसेत्
5.e: Having voluntarily followed a dead person, whether he be a relation or not, he becomes pure by bathing with his clothes on, touching fire and eating clarified butter.

5.s: anugamyaicchayā pretaṃ jñātimajñātimeva ca ajñātimeva vā snātvā sacailaḥ spṛṣṭvā 'gniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati sacailaṃ , viśuddhyati
5.d: अनुगम्यैच्छया प्रेतं ज्ञातिमज्ञातिमेव च अज्ञातिमेव वा स्नात्वा सचैलः स्पृष्ट्वा ऽग्निं घृतं प्राश्य विशुध्यति सचैलं , विशुद्ध्यति
5.e: One should not have a dead Brāhmaṇa carried by a Śūdra, while his own people are there. For it would be an oblation into fire, defiled by the touch of the Śūdra, and as such not conducive to heaven.—(l 03).

5.s: na vipraṃ sveṣu tiṣṭhatsu mṛtaṃ śūdreṇa nāyayet asvargyā hyāhutiḥ sā syātśūdrasaṃsparśadūṣitā
5.d: न विप्रं स्वेषु तिष्ठत्सु मृतं शूद्रेण नाययेत् अस्वर्ग्या ह्याहुतिः सा स्यात्शूद्रसंस्पर्शदूषिता
5.e: Wisdom, austerity, fire, food, clay, mind, water, smearing, wind, action, the sun and time are means of purification for corporeal beings.

5.s: jñānaṃ tapo 'gnirāhāro mṛtmano vāryupāñjanam vāyuḥ karmārkakālau ca śuddheḥ kartr̥̄ṇi dehinām
5.d: ज्ञानं तपो ऽग्निराहारो मृत्मनो वार्युपाञ्जनम् वायुः कर्मार्ककालौ च शुद्धेः कर्त्र्̥̄णि देहिनाम्
5.e: Among all modes of purification, purity in regard to wealth has been ordained to be the most important; for he who is pure in regard to wealth is really pure, and he is not pure who is merely purified by clay and water.

5.s: sarveṣāmeva śaucānāmarthaśaucaṃ paraṃ smṛtam yo 'rthe śucirhi sa śucirna mṛtvāriśuciḥ śuciḥ
5.d: सर्वेषामेव शौचानामर्थशौचं परं स्मृतम् यो ऽर्थे शुचिर्हि स शुचिर्न मृत्वारिशुचिः शुचिः
5.e: Learned men become pure by tolerance; by liberality those who have done what should not be done; secret sinners by the repeating of sacred texts; and by austerity those who are well-versed in the Veda.

5.s: kṣāntyā śudhyanti vidvāṃso dānenākāryakāriṇaḥ śuddhyanti pracchannapāpā japyena tapasā vedavittamāḥ
5.d: क्षान्त्या शुध्यन्ति विद्वांसो दानेनाकार्यकारिणः शुद्ध्यन्ति प्रच्छन्नपापा जप्येन तपसा वेदवित्तमाः
5.e: What needs purification is purified by clay and water; the river is purified by its current; the woman of uhclean mind by menstruation; and Brāhmaṇas by renunciation.

5.s: mṛttoyaiḥ śudhyate śodhyaṃ nadī vegena śudhyati rajasā strī manoduṣṭā saṃnyāsena dvijottamāḥ
5.d: मृत्तोयैः शुध्यते शोध्यं नदी वेगेन शुध्यति रजसा स्त्री मनोदुष्टा संन्यासेन द्विजोत्तमाः
5.e: The limbs are purified by water; the mind is purified by truthfulness; the soul proper by learning and austerity; and cognition is purified by knowledge.

5.s: adbhirgātrāṇi śudhyanti manaḥ satyena śudhyati vidyātapobhyāṃ bhūtātmā buddhirjñānena śudhyati śuddhyati
5.d: अद्भिर्गात्राणि शुध्यन्ति मनः सत्येन शुध्यति विद्यातपोभ्यां भूतात्मा बुद्धिर्ज्ञानेन शुध्यति शुद्ध्यति
5.e: Thus has been explained to you the rule regarding bodily purification; listen now to the rule regarding the purification of various substances.—(109.)

5.s: eṣa śaucasya vaḥ proktaḥ śarīrasya vinirṇayaḥ nānāvidhānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ śuddheḥ śṛṇuta nirṇayam
5.d: एष शौचस्य वः प्रोक्तः शरीरस्य विनिर्णयः नानाविधानां द्रव्याणां शुद्धेः शृणुत निर्णयम्
5.e: Of igneous substances, of gems and of everything made of stone,—the purification has been ordained to be accomplished by means of ash, by water and by clay.

5.s: taijasānāṃ maṇīnāṃ ca sarvasyāśmamayasya ca bhasmanā 'dbhirmṛdā caiva śuddhiruktā manīṣibhiḥ
5.d: तैजसानां मणीनां च सर्वस्याश्ममयस्य च भस्मना ऽद्भिर्मृदा चैव शुद्धिरुक्ता मनीषिभिः
5.e: A golden vessel, free from stains, becomes pure by water alone; so also what is produced in water, what is made of stone and what is made of silver, if it is not enchased (or verse much defiled).

5.s: nirlepaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhāṇḍamadbhireva viśudhyati viśuddhyati apjamaśmamayaṃ caiva rājataṃ cānupaskṛtam
5.d: निर्लेपं काञ्चनं भाण्डमद्भिरेव विशुध्यति विशुद्ध्यति अप्जमश्ममयं चैव राजतं चानुपस्कृतम्
5.e: Gold and silver sprang out of the union of water and fire; for these reasons the purification of these two is best done by means of their source.—(112.)

5.s: apāmagneśca saṃyogāddhaimaṃ raupyaṃ ca nirbabhau tasmāt tayoḥ svayonyaiva nirṇeko guṇavattaraḥ
5.d: अपामग्नेश्च संयोगाद्धैमं रौप्यं च निर्बभौ तस्मात् तयोः स्वयोन्यैव निर्णेको गुणवत्तरः
5.e: Of copper, iron, brass, pewter and tin, the purification should be done, according to suitability, by means of alkaline substances, of liquid acids and of water.

5.s: tāmrāyaskāṃsyaraityānāṃ trapuṇaḥ sīsakasya ca śaucaṃ yathārhaṃ kartavyaṃ kṣārāmlodakavāribhiḥ
5.d: ताम्रायस्कांस्यरैत्यानां त्रपुणः सीसकस्य च शौचं यथार्हं कर्तव्यं क्षाराम्लोदकवारिभिः
5.e: For all liquids, purification has been declared to consist in throwing out a little; for solids, in sprinkling; and for wooden articles, in scraping.

5.s: dravāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śuddhirutpavanaṃ smṛtam prokṣaṇaṃ saṃhatānāṃ ca dāravāṇāṃ ca takṣaṇam
5.d: द्रवाणां चैव सर्वेषां शुद्धिरुत्पवनं स्मृतम् प्रोक्षणं संहतानां च दारवाणां च तक्षणम्
5.e: The purification of the ‘Caru’, the ‘Sruk’ and the ‘Sruva’ is done by means of hot water; as also of the ‘Sphya’, the winnowing basket, the cart, the pestle and the mortar.

5.s: mārjanaṃ yajñapātrāṇāṃ pāṇinā yajñakarmaṇi camasānāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca śuddhiḥ prakṣālanena tu
5.d: मार्जनं यज्ञपात्राणां पाणिना यज्ञकर्मणि चमसानां ग्रहाणां च शुद्धिः प्रक्षालनेन तु
5.e: The purification of the ‘Caru’, the ‘Sruk’ and the ‘Sruva’ is done by means of hot water; as also of the ‘Sphya’, the winnowing basket, the cart, the pestle and the mortar.

5.s: carūṇāṃ sruksruvāṇāṃ ca śuddhiruṣṇena vāriṇā sphyaśūrpaśakaṭānāṃ ca musalaulūkhalasya ca
5.d: चरूणां स्रुक्स्रुवाणां च शुद्धिरुष्णेन वारिणा स्फ्यशूर्पशकटानां च मुसलौलूखलस्य च
5.e: Of grains and cloth, in large quantities, there is sprinkling with water; and in small quantities, their purification has been ordained to be secured by means of washing with water.

5.s: adbhistu prokṣaṇaṃ śaucaṃ bahūnāṃ dhānyavāsasām prakṣālanena tvalpānāmadbhiḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate
5.d: अद्भिस्तु प्रोक्षणं शौचं बहूनां धान्यवाससाम् प्रक्षालनेन त्वल्पानामद्भिः शौचं विधीयते
5.e: The method of purifying leather and tree-barks is similar to that of clothes; and for vegetables, roots and fruits, the purification is like that of grains.

5.s: cailavatcarmaṇāṃ śuddhirvaidalānāṃ tathaiva ca śākamūlaphalānāṃ ca dhānyavatśuddhiriṣyate tu
5.d: चैलवत्चर्मणां शुद्धिर्वैदलानां तथैव च शाकमूलफलानां च धान्यवत्शुद्धिरिष्यते तु
5.e: Of Silken and woolen stuffs, by means of saline earth; of blankets by soap-berries; of ‘aṃśupaṭṭa,’ by the Bel-fruit; and of linen by white mustard.

5.s: kauśeyāvikayorūṣaiḥ kutapānāmariṣṭakaiḥ śrīphalairaṃśupaṭṭānāṃ kṣaumāṇāṃ gaurasarṣapaiḥ
5.d: कौशेयाविकयोरूषैः कुतपानामरिष्टकैः श्रीफलैरंशुपट्टानां क्षौमाणां गौरसर्षपैः
5.e: The learned man should purify conch-shells, horn and things mads of bone and tusk, like linen; and by c ow’s urine or water.

5.s: kṣaumavatśaṅkhaśṛṅgāṇāmasthidantamayasya ca śuddhirvijānatā kāryā gomūtreṇaudakena vā
5.d: क्षौमवत्शङ्खशृङ्गाणामस्थिदन्तमयस्य च शुद्धिर्विजानता कार्या गोमूत्रेणौदकेन वा
5.e: Grass and wood and straw become pure by sprinkling; the house by sweeping and sprinkling; and an earthen pot by re-baking.

5.s: prokṣaṇāt tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca palālaṃ caiva śudhyati mārjanaupāñjanairveśma punaḥpākena mṛtmayam
5.d: प्रोक्षणात् तृणकाष्ठं च पलालं चैव शुध्यति मार्जनौपाञ्जनैर्वेश्म पुनःपाकेन मृत्मयम्
5.e: An earthen vessel which has been defiled by spirituous liquor, urine, ordure, saliva, pus or blood cannot be purified by another burning.—(122)

5.s: madyairmūtraiḥ purīṣairvā ṣṭhīvanaiḥ pūyaśoṇitaiḥ saṃspṛṣṭaṃ naiva śuddhyeta punaḥpākena mṛtmayam
5.d: मद्यैर्मूत्रैः पुरीषैर्वा ष्ठीवनैः पूयशोणितैः संस्पृष्टं नैव शुद्ध्येत पुनःपाकेन मृत्मयम्
5.e: What has been eaten by a bird, what has been smelt by a cow, blown upon, or sneezed at, or defiled by hair and insects, becomes pure by scattering earth.

5.s: saṃmārjanaupāñjanena sekenaullekhanena ca gavāṃ ca parivāsena bhūmiḥ śudhyati pañcabhiḥ śuddhyati
5.d: संमार्जनौपाञ्जनेन सेकेनौल्लेखनेन च गवां च परिवासेन भूमिः शुध्यति पञ्चभिः शुद्ध्यति
5.e: From an object tainted by an unclean substance, as long as the smell and the stain caused by it do not disappear, so long should earth and water be applied to it,—in all cases of the purification of things.

5.s: pakṣijagdhaṃ gavā ghrātamavadhūtamavakṣutam dūṣitaṃ keśakīṭaiśca mṛtprakṣepeṇa śudhyati
5.d: पक्षिजग्धं गवा घ्रातमवधूतमवक्षुतम् दूषितं केशकीटैश्च मृत्प्रक्षेपेण शुध्यति
5.e: The gods ordained three things pure for the Brāhmaṇas: what is not seen, what is washed with water and what is commended by word.

5.s: yāvatnāpaityamedhyāktādgandho lepaśca tatkṛtaḥ tāvan mṛdvāri cādeyaṃ sarvāsu dravyaśuddhiṣu
5.d: यावत्नापैत्यमेध्याक्ताद्गन्धो लेपश्च तत्कृतः तावन् मृद्वारि चादेयं सर्वासु द्रव्यशुद्धिषु
5.e: Water collected on the ground is pure, if it is sufficient to allay the thirst of the cow; but only if it is not contaminated by any unclean thing, becoming affected by with its smell, colour and taste.

5.s: trīṇi devāḥ pavitrāṇi brāhmaṇānāmakalpayan adṛṣṭamadbhirnirṇiktaṃ yacca vācā praśasyate
5.d: त्रीणि देवाः पवित्राणि ब्राह्मणानामकल्पयन् अदृष्टमद्भिर्निर्णिक्तं यच्च वाचा प्रशस्यते
5.e: The artisan’s hand is always pure; so also is merchandise spread out for sale; the food begged and held by the student is ever sacred; such is the established rule

5.s: āpaḥ śuddhā bhūmigatā vaitṛṣṇyaṃ yāsu gorbhavet avyāptāścedamedhyena gandhavarṇarasānvitāḥ
5.d: आपः शुद्धा भूमिगता वैतृष्ण्यं यासु गोर्भवेत् अव्याप्ताश्चेदमेध्येन गन्धवर्णरसान्विताः
5.e: The mouth of women is always pure; as also the bird in the dropping of fruits; the calf is pure in causing the flow (of milk); and the dog is pure in the catching of deer

5.s: nityaṃ śuddhaḥ kāruhastaḥ paṇye yacca prasāritam paṇyaṃ brahmacārigataṃ bhaikṣyaṃ nityaṃ medhyamiti sthitiḥ
5.d: नित्यं शुद्धः कारुहस्तः पण्ये यच्च प्रसारितम् पण्यं ब्रह्मचारिगतं भैक्ष्यं नित्यं मेध्यमिति स्थितिः
5.e: The flesh of the animal killed by dogs Manu has declared to be pure; as also that of the animal killed by other carnivorous animals and by the Cāṇḍāla and other low castes.

5.s: nityamāsyaṃ śuci strīṇāṃ śakuniḥ phalapātane prasrave ca śucirvatsaḥ śvā mṛgagrahaṇe śuciḥ
5.d: नित्यमास्यं शुचि स्त्रीणां शकुनिः फलपातने प्रस्रवे च शुचिर्वत्सः श्वा मृगग्रहणे शुचिः
5.e: The cavities that are above the navel are all pure; those that are below it are impure; as, also are all excretions dropped fr om the body.

5.s: śvabhirhatasya yan māṃsaṃ śuci tan manurabravīt kravyādbhiśca hatasyānyaiścaṇḍālādyaiśca dasyubhiḥ
5.d: श्वभिर्हतस्य यन् मांसं शुचि तन् मनुरब्रवीत् क्रव्याद्भिश्च हतस्यान्यैश्चण्डालाद्यैश्च दस्युभिः
5.e: Flies, water-drops, shadow, the cow, the horse, the sun’s rays, dust, earth, air and fire—should be regarded as pure to the touch.

5.s: ūrdhvaṃ nābheryāni khāni tāni medhyāni sarvaśaḥ yānyadhastānyamedhyāni dehāccaiva malāścyutāḥ
5.d: ऊर्ध्वं नाभेर्यानि खानि तानि मेध्यानि सर्वशः यान्यधस्तान्यमेध्यानि देहाच्चैव मलाश्च्युताः
5.e: For the cleansing of the ejectors or urine and faeces, earth and water should be used, as much as may be necessary; as also in the twelve cleansings of the bodily excretions.

5.s: makṣikā vipruṣaśchāyā gauraśvaḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ rajo bhūrvāyuragniśca sparśe medhyāni nirdiśet
5.d: मक्षिका विप्रुषश्छाया गौरश्वः सूर्यरश्मयः रजो भूर्वायुरग्निश्च स्पर्शे मेध्यानि निर्दिशेत्
5.e: Fat, man, blood, marrow, urine, ordure, nasal excretion, eab-wax, phlegm, tears, rheum of the eyes and perspiration,—these twelve are the ‘excretions’ of human beings.

5.s: viṣmūtrautsargaśuddhiarthaṃ mṛtvāryādeyamarthavat daihikānāṃ malānāṃ ca śuddhiṣu dvādaśasvapi
5.d: विष्मूत्रौत्सर्गशुद्धिअर्थं मृत्वार्यादेयमर्थवत् दैहिकानां मलानां च शुद्धिषु द्वादशस्वपि
5.e: One who desires cleanliness should apply earth—once to the urinary organ, thrice to the anus, ten times to one hand and seven times to both hands.

5.s: vasā śukramasṛjmajjā mūtraviṣghrāṇakarṇaviṣ śleśma aśru dūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ
5.d: वसा शुक्रमसृज्मज्जा मूत्रविष्घ्राणकर्णविष् श्लेश्म अश्रु दूषिका स्वेदो द्वादशैते नृणां मलाः
5.e: Such is the purification for householders; double of this for students, treble for hermits, and quadruple for renunciates.

5.s: ekā liṅge gude tisrastathaikatra kare daśa ubhayoḥ sapta dātavyā mṛdaḥ śuddhimabhīpsatā
5.d: एका लिङ्गे गुदे तिस्रस्तथैकत्र करे दश उभयोः सप्त दातव्या मृदः शुद्धिमभीप्सता
5.e: Having passed urine or faeces, and sipped water, one should touch. with water the cavities; also when he may be going to read the Veda, and always when going to take food.

5.s: etatśaucaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇām triguṇaṃ syādvanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam
5.d: एतत्शौचं गृहस्थानां द्विगुणं ब्रह्मचारिणाम् त्रिगुणं स्याद्वनस्थानां यतीनां तु चतुर्गुणम्
5.e: Desiring bodily purification, one should sip water thrice; then he should twice wipe his mouth; but the woman and the śūdra should each do it once only.

5.s: kṛtvā mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā khānyācānta upaspṛśet vedamadhyeṣyamāṇaśca annamaśnaṃśca sarvadā
5.d: कृत्वा मूत्रं पुरीषं वा खान्याचान्त उपस्पृशेत् वेदमध्येष्यमाणश्च अन्नमश्नंश्च सर्वदा
5.e: By śūdras living according to law, shaving should be done every month; thus manner of purification should be like that of the Vaiśya; and their food shall consist of the leavings of twice-born men.

5.s: trirācāmedapaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāt tato mukham śarīraṃ śaucamicchan hi strī śūdrastu sakṛt sakṛt
5.d: त्रिराचामेदपः पूर्वं द्विः प्रमृज्यात् ततो मुखम् शरीरं शौचमिच्छन् हि स्त्री शूद्रस्तु सकृत् सकृत्
5.e: Drops from the mouth, if they do not reach the body, do not make one impure; nor the hairs of the beard that enter the mouth; nor what adheres to the teeth.

5.s: śūdrāṇāṃ māsikaṃ kāryaṃ vapanaṃ nyāyavartinām vaiśyavatśaucakalpaśca dvijaucchiṣṭaṃ ca bhojanam
5.d: शूद्राणां मासिकं कार्यं वपनं न्यायवर्तिनाम् वैश्यवत्शौचकल्पश्च द्विजौच्छिष्टं च भोजनम्
5.e: The drops that touch the feet of one who is helping others to wash should be regarded as on the same footing as those on the ground; and he is not rendered impure by them.

5.s: naucchiṣṭaṃ kurvate mukhyā vipruṣo 'ṅgaṃ na yānti yāḥ na śmaśrūṇi gatānyāsyaṃ na dantāntar 'dhiṣṭhitam
5.d: नौच्छिष्टं कुर्वते मुख्या विप्रुषो ऽङ्गं न यान्ति याः न श्मश्रूणि गतान्यास्यं न दन्तान्तर् ऽधिष्ठितम्
5.e: He who, with some substance in hand, happens to be touched by an unclean object, becomes pure by washing, without laying down that substance.

5.s: spṛśanti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān bhaumikaiste samā jñeyā na tairāprayato bhavet aprayato
5.d: स्पृशन्ति बिन्दवः पादौ य आचामयतः परान् भौमिकैस्ते समा ज्ञेया न तैराप्रयतो भवेत् अप्रयतो
5.e: Having vomitted or purged, one should bath and then eat clarified butter. After having eaten his food, he should only sip water. For one who has copulated bathing has been ordained.

5.s: ucchiṣṭena tu saṃspṛṣṭo dravyahastaḥ kathaṃ cana anidhāyaiva taddravyamācāntaḥ śucitāmiyāt
5.d: उच्छिष्टेन तु संस्पृष्टो द्रव्यहस्तः कथं चन अनिधायैव तद्द्रव्यमाचान्तः शुचितामियात्
5.e: One should sip water after having slept, after having sneezed, after having eaten, after having spat, after having told a lie, after having drunk water, and when going to read the Veda, even though he may be quite pure.

5.s: vānto viriktaḥ snātvā tu ghṛtaprāśanamācaret ācāmedeva bhuktvā 'nnaṃ snānaṃ maithuninaḥ smṛtam
5.d: वान्तो विरिक्तः स्नात्वा तु घृतप्राशनमाचरेत् आचामेदेव भुक्त्वा ऽन्नं स्नानं मैथुनिनः स्मृतम्
5.e: Thus has the whole rule regarding cleanliness and purification of substances for all castes been expounded to you; listen now to the duties of women.

5.s: suptvā kṣutvā ca bhuktvā ca niṣṭhīvyauktvā 'nṛtāni ca pītvā 'po 'dhyeṣyamāṇaśca ācāmet prayato 'pi san
5.d: सुप्त्वा क्षुत्वा च भुक्त्वा च निष्ठीव्यौक्त्वा ऽनृतानि च पीत्वा ऽपो ऽध्येष्यमाणश्च आचामेत् प्रयतो ऽपि सन्
5.e: Whether she be a child, or a young woman, or an aged woman, she should not do any act by herself, even in the house.

5.s: eṣāṃ śaucavidhiḥ kṛtsno dravyaśuddhistathaiva ca eṣa ukto vaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ strīṇāṃ dharmānnibodhata
5.d: एषां शौचविधिः कृत्स्नो द्रव्यशुद्धिस्तथैव च एष उक्तो वः सर्ववर्णानां स्त्रीणां धर्मान्निबोधत
5.e: In childhood she should remain under the control of her father, in youth under that of her husband, and on the husband’s death under that of her sons; the woman should never have recourse to independence.

5.s: bālayā vā yuvatyā vā vṛddhayā vā 'pi yoṣitā na svātantryeṇa kartavyaṃ kiṃ cidkāryaṃ gṛheṣvapi
5.d: बालया वा युवत्या वा वृद्धया वा ऽपि योषिता न स्वातन्त्र्येण कर्तव्यं किं चिद्कार्यं गृहेष्वपि
5.e: She should not seek separation from her father, husband or sons: by separating, the woman would render both families disreputable.

5.s: bālye piturvaśe tiṣṭhet pāṇigrāhasya yauvane putrāṇāṃ bhartari prete na bhajet strī svatantratām
5.d: बाल्ये पितुर्वशे तिष्ठेत् पाणिग्राहस्य यौवने पुत्राणां भर्तरि प्रेते न भजेत् स्त्री स्वतन्त्रताम्
5.e: She should be always cheerful and alert in household-work; she should have the utensils well-cleaned and in spending she should be close-fisted.

5.s: pitrā bhartrā sutairvā 'pi naicchedvirahamātmanaḥ eṣāṃ hi viraheṇa strī garhye kuryādubhe kule
5.d: पित्रा भर्त्रा सुतैर्वा ऽपि नैच्छेद्विरहमात्मनः एषां हि विरहेण स्त्री गर्ह्ये कुर्यादुभे कुले
5.e: Him to whom her father may give her,—or her brother with the father’s permission,—she shall attend upon as long as he lives, and shall not disregard him when he is dead.

5.s: sadā prahṛṣṭayā bhāvyaṃ gṛhakārye ca dakṣayā susaṃskṛtaupaskarayā vyaye cāmuktahastayā
5.d: सदा प्रहृष्टया भाव्यं गृहकार्ये च दक्षया सुसंस्कृतौपस्करया व्यये चामुक्तहस्तया
5.e: At their wedding, the sacrifice to Prajāpati, which is the means of securing welfare, is performed for the purpose of procuring good fortune; it is the giving away that is the source of ownership.

5.s: yasmai dadyāt pitā tvenāṃ bhrātā vā 'numate pituḥ taṃ śuśrūṣeta jīvantaṃ saṃsthitaṃ ca na laṅghayet
5.d: यस्मै दद्यात् पिता त्वेनां भ्राता वा ऽनुमते पितुः तं शुश्रूषेत जीवन्तं संस्थितं च न लङ्घयेत्
5.e: The husband who has performed the mantric sacramental rites for women is the imparter of happiness to them both in season and out of season, here as well as in the next world.

5.s: maṅgalārthaṃ svastyayanaṃ yajñaścāsāṃ prajāpateḥ prayujyate vivāhe tu pradānaṃ svāmyakāraṇam
5.d: मङ्गलार्थं स्वस्त्ययनं यज्ञश्चासां प्रजापतेः प्रयुज्यते विवाहे तु प्रदानं स्वाम्यकारणम्
5.e: Be he ill-mannered or of licentious habits or destitute of good qualities,—the husband should always be attended upon like a god by the true wive.

5.s: anṛtāvṛtukāle ca mantrasaṃskārakṛt patiḥ sukhasya nityaṃ dātaiha paraloke ca yoṣitaḥ
5.d: अनृतावृतुकाले च मन्त्रसंस्कारकृत् पतिः सुखस्य नित्यं दातैह परलोके च योषितः
5.e: There is no separate sacrificing for women, no observances, no fastings; it is by means of serving her husband that she becomes exalted in heaven.

5.s: viśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā guṇairvā parivarjitaḥ upacāryaḥ striyā sādhvyā satataṃ devavat patiḥ
5.d: विशीलः कामवृत्तो वा गुणैर्वा परिवर्जितः उपचार्यः स्त्रिया साध्व्या सततं देववत् पतिः
5.e: The good wife, desirous of reaching her husband’s regions, should never do anything that m ay be disagreeable to her husband, alive or dead.

5.s: nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthag yajño na vrataṃ nāpyupoṣaṇam upoṣitam patiṃ śuśrūṣate yena tena svarge mahīyate
5.d: नास्ति स्त्रीणां पृथग् यज्ञो न व्रतं नाप्युपोषणम् उपोषितम् पतिं शुश्रूषते येन तेन स्वर्गे महीयते
5.e: Well might she macerate her body by means of pure flowers, roots and fruits; but she should not even mention the name of another man, after her husband is dead

5.s: pāṇigrāhasya sādhvī strī jīvato vā mṛtasya vā patilokamabhīpsantī nācaret kiṃ cidapriyam
5.d: पाणिग्राहस्य साध्वी स्त्री जीवतो वा मृतस्य वा पतिलोकमभीप्सन्ती नाचरेत् किं चिदप्रियम्
5.e: Till her death, she should remain patient, self-controlled and chaste,—seeking that most excellent merit that accrues to women having a single husband.

5.s: kāmaṃ tu ksapayeddehaṃ puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ na tu nāmāpi gṛhṇīyāt patyau prete parasya tu
5.d: कामं तु क्सपयेद्देहं पुष्पमूलफलैः शुभैः न तु नामापि गृह्णीयात् पत्यौ प्रेते परस्य तु
5.e: Many thousands of unmarried Brāhmaṇa students have gone to heaven, without having perpetuated their race

5.s: āsītā maraṇāt ksāntā niyatā brahmacāriṇī yo dharma ekapatnīnāṃ kāṅkṣantī tamanuttamam
5.d: आसीता मरणात् क्सान्ता नियता ब्रह्मचारिणी यो धर्म एकपत्नीनां काङ्क्षन्ती तमनुत्तमम्
5.e: On the death of her husband, the good wife who remains firm, goes to heaven, even though childless; just like those students

5.s: anekāni sahasrāṇi kumārabrahmacāriṇām divaṃ gatāni viprāṇāmakṛtvā kulasaṃtatim
5.d: अनेकानि सहस्राणि कुमारब्रह्मचारिणाम् दिवं गतानि विप्राणामकृत्वा कुलसंततिम्
5.e: That woman, however, who from a longing for a child, disregards her husband, brings disgrace to herself in this world and falls off from her place in the other world.

5.s: mṛte bhartari sāḍhvī strī brahmacarye vyavasthitā svargaṃ gacchatyaputrā 'pi yathā te brahmacāriṇaḥ
5.d: मृते भर्तरि साढ्वी स्त्री ब्रह्मचर्ये व्यवस्थिता स्वर्गं गच्छत्यपुत्रा ऽपि यथा ते ब्रह्मचारिणः
5.e: What is born of another is not a ‘child’: nor is one begotten on another man’s wife; for good women a second husband is nowhere ordained.

5.s: apatyalobhādyā tu strī bhartāramativartate saiha nindāmavāpnoti paralokācca hīyate
5.d: अपत्यलोभाद्या तु स्त्री भर्तारमतिवर्तते सैह निन्दामवाप्नोति परलोकाच्च हीयते
5.e: She, who, having abandoned her own husband who is inerior, has recourse to another person who is superior, becomes contemptible in this world and is called a ‘remarried woman.’

5.s: nānyautpannā prajā 'stīha na cāpyanyaparigrahe na cānyasya parigrahe na dvitīyaśca sādhvīnāṃ kva cidbhartaupadiśyate
5.d: नान्यौत्पन्ना प्रजा ऽस्तीह न चाप्यन्यपरिग्रहे न चान्यस्य परिग्रहे न द्वितीयश्च साध्वीनां क्व चिद्भर्तौपदिश्यते
5.e: The woman, who, through failure in her duty to her husband, becomes an object of contempt in the world, comes to be born as a jackal and is tormented by foul diseases.

5.s: patiṃ hitvā 'pakṛṣṭaṃ svamutkṛṣṭaṃ yā niṣevate itvā 'vakṛṣṭaṃ nindyaiva sā bhavelloke parapūrvaiti caucyate
5.d: पतिं हित्वा ऽपकृष्टं स्वमुत्कृष्टं या निषेवते इत्वा ऽवकृष्टं निन्द्यैव सा भवेल्लोके परपूर्वैति चौच्यते
5.e: By such conduct, the woman, having her thought, word and body well controlled, obtains excellent fame in this world, and also her husband’s region in the other world.

5.s: vyabhicārāt tu bhartuḥ strī loke prāpnoti nindyatām vyabhicāre tu śṛgālayoniṃ prāpnoti pāparogaiśca pīḍyate
5.d: व्यभिचारात् तु भर्तुः स्त्री लोके प्राप्नोति निन्द्यताम् व्यभिचारे तु शृगालयोनिं प्राप्नोति पापरोगैश्च पीड्यते
5.e: By such conduct, the woman, having her thought, word and body well controlled, obtains excellent fame in this world, and also her husband’s region in the other world.

5.s: patiṃ yā nābhicarati manovāgdehasaṃyutā dehasaṃyatā sā bhartṛlokamāpnoti sadbhiḥ sādhvīiti caucyate
5.d: पतिं या नाभिचरति मनोवाग्देहसंयुता देहसंयता सा भर्तृलोकमाप्नोति सद्भिः साध्वीइति चौच्यते
5.e: The twice-born man, knowing the law, should cremate the wife of his own caste,—who behaves herself in the said manner, and dies before him,—with the sacred fire and along with the sacrificial implements.

5.s: anena nārī vṛttena manovāgdehasaṃyatā ihāgryāṃ kīrtimāpnoti patilokaṃ paratra ca
5.d: अनेन नारी वृत्तेन मनोवाग्देहसंयता इहाग्र्यां कीर्तिमाप्नोति पतिलोकं परत्र च
5.e: Having, during the last rites, given away the sacred fires to his wife who died before him, he may marry again and kindle the fires again.

5.s: evaṃ vṛttāṃ savarṇāṃ strīṃ dvijātiḥ pūrvamāriṇīm dāhayedagnihotreṇa yajñapātraiśca dharmavit
5.d: एवं वृत्तां सवर्णां स्त्रीं द्विजातिः पूर्वमारिणीम् दाहयेदग्निहोत्रेण यज्ञपात्रैश्च धर्मवित्
5.e: In this manner, one shall not omit the Five Sacrifices; and during the second part of his life, he shall take to a wife and dwell in the house.

5.s: bhāryāyai pūrvamāriṇyai dattvā 'gnīnantyakarmaṇi punardārakriyāṃ kuryāt punarādhānameva ca
5.d: भार्यायै पूर्वमारिण्यै दत्त्वा ऽग्नीनन्त्यकर्मणि पुनर्दारक्रियां कुर्यात् पुनराधानमेव च

6.s: anena vidhinā nityaṃ pañcayajñānna hāpayet dvitīyamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ kṛtadāro gṛhe vaset
6.d: अनेन विधिना नित्यं पञ्चयज्ञान्न हापयेत् द्वितीयमायुषो भागं कृतदारो गृहे वसेत्

6.s: evaṃ gṛhāśrame sthitvā vidhivat snātako dvijaḥ vane vaset tu niyato yathāvadvijitaindriyaḥ
6.d: एवं गृहाश्रमे स्थित्वा विधिवत् स्नातको द्विजः वने वसेत् तु नियतो यथावद्विजितैन्द्रियः
6.e: The twice-born accomplished student, having, in the afore- said manner, lived, according to law, the life of the householder, should dwell in the forest, in the proper manner, self-controlled and with his organs under subjection

6.s: gṛhasthastu yathā paśyedvalīpalitamātmanaḥ apatyasyaiva cāpatyaṃ tadā 'raṇyaṃ samāśrayet
6.d: गृहस्थस्तु यथा पश्येद्वलीपलितमात्मनः अपत्यस्यैव चापत्यं तदा ऽरण्यं समाश्रयेत्
6.e: When the householder notices his wrinkles and greyness, and sees his child’s child,—then he should r etire to the forest,

6.s: saṃtyajya grāmyamāhāraṃ sarvaṃ caiva paricchadam putreṣu bhāryāṃ nikṣipya vanaṃ gacchet sahaiva vā
6.d: संत्यज्य ग्राम्यमाहारं सर्वं चैव परिच्छदम् पुत्रेषु भार्यां निक्षिप्य वनं गच्छेत् सहैव वा
6.e: Having given up cultivated food and all his belongings, he shall repair to the forest, either making over his wife to his sons, or along with her.

6.s: agnihotraṃ samādāya gṛhyaṃ cāgniparicchadam grāmādaraṇyaṃ niḥsṛtya nivasenniyataindriyaḥ niṣkramya
6.d: अग्निहोत्रं समादाय गृह्यं चाग्निपरिच्छदम् ग्रामादरण्यं निःसृत्य निवसेन्नियतैन्द्रियः निष्क्रम्य
6.e: Taking with him the Sacred Fire, as also all the ritualistic appurtenances of the Fire, the man shall go forth from the village to the forest and live there, with his senses under control.

6.s: muniannairvividhairmedhyaiḥ śākamūlaphalena vā etāneva mahāyajñānnirvapedvidhipūrvakam
6.d: मुनिअन्नैर्विविधैर्मेध्यैः शाकमूलफलेन वा एतानेव महायज्ञान्निर्वपेद्विधिपूर्वकम्
6.e: These same ‘Great Sacrifices’ he should offer, according to rule, with various kinds of pure food fit for hermits, or with herbs, roots and fruits.

6.s: vasīta carma cīraṃ vā sāyaṃ snāyāt prage tathā jaṭāśca bibhṛyānnityaṃ śmaśrulomanakhāni ca
6.d: वसीत चर्म चीरं वा सायं स्नायात् प्रगे तथा जटाश्च बिभृयान्नित्यं श्मश्रुलोमनखानि च
6.e: He should wear either skin or a bit of cloth; he shall bathe in the evening, as also in the meaning; he shall always wear matted locks, as also beard, hair on his body and nails.

6.s: yadbhakṣyaṃ syādtato dadyādbaliṃ bhikṣāṃ ca śaktitaḥ yadbhakṣaḥ apmūlaphalabhikṣābhirarcayedāśramāgatān :āśramāgataṃ
6.d: यद्भक्ष्यं स्याद्ततो दद्याद्बलिं भिक्षां च शक्तितः यद्भक्षः अप्मूलफलभिक्षाभिरर्चयेदाश्रमागतान् :आश्रमागतं
6.e: What he eats, cut of that he should make the offerings and give alms, according to his capacity; and those who come to his hermitage he should honour with water, roots and fruits and alms

6.s: svādhyāye nityayuktaḥ syāddānto maitraḥ samāhitaḥ dātā nityamanādātā sarvabhūtānukampakaḥ
6.d: स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्याद्दान्तो मैत्रः समाहितः दाता नित्यमनादाता सर्वभूतानुकम्पकः
6.e: He should be always engaged in Vedic study, meek, conciliatory, quiet, ever liberal, not accepting any gifts, and compassionate towards all living beings.

6.s: vaitānikaṃ ca juhuyādagnihotraṃ yathāvidhi darśamaskandayan parva paurṇamāsaṃ ca yogataḥ
6.d: वैतानिकं च जुहुयादग्निहोत्रं यथाविधि दर्शमस्कन्दयन् पर्व पौर्णमासं च योगतः
6.e: He shall offer, according to rule, the sacrificial oblations, taking case not to omit the ‘Darśa’ and the ‘Paurnamāsa’ sacrifice.

6.s: ṛkṣeṣṭyāgrayaṇaṃ caiva cāturmāsyāni cāharet darśeṣṭy āgrayaṇaṃ turāyaṇaṃ ca kramaśo dakṣasyāyanameva ca dākṣasyāyanaṃ
6.d: ऋक्षेष्ट्याग्रयणं चैव चातुर्मास्यानि चाहरेत् दर्शेष्ट्य् आग्रयणं तुरायणं च क्रमशो दक्षस्यायनमेव च दाक्षस्यायनं
6.e: He shall perform the Darśeṣṭi and the Āgrayaṇa; as also the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, and the Turāyaṇa and Dākṣāyaṇa in due order.

6.s: vāsantaśāradairmedhyairmuniannaiḥ svayamāhṛtaiḥ puroḍāśāṃścarūṃścaiva vidhivatnirvapet pṛthak
6.d: वासन्तशारदैर्मेध्यैर्मुनिअन्नैः स्वयमाहृतैः पुरोडाशांश्चरूंश्चैव विधिवत्निर्वपेत् पृथक्
6.e: With the pure grains fit for hermits, which grow in spring and in autumn, and which he has himself gathered, he shall severally prepare cakes and boiled messes, according to law

6.s: devatābhyastu taddhutvā vanyaṃ medhyataraṃ haviḥ śeṣamātmani yuñjīta lavaṇaṃ ca svayaṃ kṛtam
6.d: देवताभ्यस्तु तद्धुत्वा वन्यं मेध्यतरं हविः शेषमात्मनि युञ्जीत लवणं च स्वयं कृतम्
6.e: Having offered to the gods that most pure offering consisting of wild-growing things, he shall take to himself the remnant, as also the salt prepared by himself

6.s: sthalajaudakaśākāni puṣpamūlaphalāni ca medhyavṛkṣaudbhavānyadyāt snehāṃśca phalasaṃbhavān
6.d: स्थलजौदकशाकानि पुष्पमूलफलानि च मेध्यवृक्षौद्भवान्यद्यात् स्नेहांश्च फलसंभवान्
6.e: He should eat the vegetables that grow on land and in water; also flowers, roots and fruits, the productions of pure trees; as well as oils produced from fruits.

6.s: varjayen madhu māṃsaṃ ca bhaumāni kavakāni ca bhūstṛṇaṃ śigrukaṃ caiva śleśmātakaphalāni ca
6.d: वर्जयेन् मधु मांसं च भौमानि कवकानि च भूस्तृणं शिग्रुकं चैव श्लेश्मातकफलानि च
6.e: He shall avoid honey, meat, cabbages, mushrooms, the fragrant grass, the pot-herb and the ‘Śleṣmātaka (Śleśmātaka?)’ fruits.

6.s: tyajedāśvayuje māsi muniannaṃ pūrvasañcitam jīrṇāni caiva vāsāṃsi śākamūlaphalāni ca
6.d: त्यजेदाश्वयुजे मासि मुनिअन्नं पूर्वसञ्चितम् जीर्णानि चैव वासांसि शाकमूलफलानि च
6.e: In the month of Āśvina he shall throw away the formerly-gathered ‘hermit’s food’, as also the worn-out clothes and the herbs, roots and fruits.

6.s: na phālakṛṣṭamaśnīyādutsṛṣṭamapi kena cit na grāmajātānyārto 'pi mūlāṇi ca phalāni ca puṣpāni ca phalāni ca
6.d: न फालकृष्टमश्नीयादुत्सृष्टमपि केन चित् न ग्रामजातान्यार्तो ऽपि मूलाणि च फलानि च पुष्पानि च फलानि च
6.e: He shall not eat anything produced by ploughing, even though it mat have been thrown away by some one; nor such flowers and fruits as are grown in villages, even though he in be in distress.

6.s: agnipakvāśano vā syāt kālapakvabhujeva vā aśmakuṭṭo bhavedvā 'pi dantaulūkhaliko 'pi vā
6.d: अग्निपक्वाशनो वा स्यात् कालपक्वभुजेव वा अश्मकुट्टो भवेद्वा ऽपि दन्तौलूखलिको ऽपि वा
6.e: He may be one living on food cooked by fire, or one eating only what Ripens in its own time; he may use the stone for grinding or he may use his teeth as the mortar.

6.s: sadyaḥ prakṣālako vā syān māsasañcayiko 'pi vā ṣaṇmāsanicayo vā syāt samānicaya eva vā
6.d: सद्यः प्रक्षालको वा स्यान् माससञ्चयिको ऽपि वा षण्मासनिचयो वा स्यात् समानिचय एव वा
6.e: He may be either one who washes off immediately, or one who lays by for a month, or one who lays by for six months, or one who lays by for a year.

6.s: naktaṃ cānnaṃ samaśnīyāddivā vā 'hṛtya śaktitaḥ caturthakāliko vā syāt syādvā 'pyaṣṭamakālikaḥ
6.d: नक्तं चान्नं समश्नीयाद्दिवा वा ऽहृत्य शक्तितः चतुर्थकालिको वा स्यात् स्याद्वा ऽप्यष्टमकालिकः
