6.e: Having collected food to the best of his ability, he should eat it at night, or during the day; or he may do it at every fourth time, or at every eighth time.

6.s: cāndrāyaṇavidhānairvā śuklakṛṣṇe ca vartayet pakṣāntayorvā 'pyaśnīyādyavāgūṃ kvathitāṃ sakṛt
6.d: चान्द्रायणविधानैर्वा शुक्लकृष्णे च वर्तयेत् पक्षान्तयोर्वा ऽप्यश्नीयाद्यवागूं क्वथितां सकृत्
6.e: Or he may live during the bright and dark fortnights in th e manner of the ‘Cāndrāyaṇa’ penance; or he may eat once at the end of each of the two fortnights, boiled barley-gruel.

6.s: puṣpamūlaphalairvā 'pi kevalairvartayet sadā kālapakvaiḥ svayaṃ śīrṇairvaikhānasamate sthitaḥ
6.d: पुष्पमूलफलैर्वा ऽपि केवलैर्वर्तयेत् सदा कालपक्वैः स्वयं शीर्णैर्वैखानसमते स्थितः
6.e: Or, he may always subsist only on flowers, roots and fruits, which have ripened in their own season and fallen down spontaneously,—keeping firm in the ways of life prescribed in the ‘Vaikhānasa’ Institutes.

6.s: bhūmau viparivarteta tiṣṭhedvā prapadairdinam sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharet savaneṣūpayannapaḥ
6.d: भूमौ विपरिवर्तेत तिष्ठेद्वा प्रपदैर्दिनम् स्थानासनाभ्यां विहरेत् सवनेषूपयन्नपः
6.e: He shall roll about on the ground, or stand on tip-toe during the day; he shall beguile his time by standing and sitting, going to water at the ‘Savanas’.

6.s: grīṣme pañcatapāstu syādvarṣāsvabhrāvakāśikaḥ ārdravāsāstu hemante kramaśo vardhayaṃstapaḥ
6.d: ग्रीष्मे पञ्चतपास्तु स्याद्वर्षास्वभ्रावकाशिकः आर्द्रवासास्तु हेमन्ते क्रमशो वर्धयंस्तपः
6.e: During summer he shall keep five fires; during the rains, he shall have the sky for his shelter; and during the winter he shall keep wet clothes: gradually increasing his austerities.—(23 ).

6.s: upaspṛśaṃstriṣavaṇaṃ pitr̥̄n devāṃśca tarpayet tapascaraṃścaugrataraṃ śoṣayeddehamātmanaḥ
6.d: उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं पित्र्̥̄न् देवांश्च तर्पयेत् तपस्चरंश्चौग्रतरं शोषयेद्देहमात्मनः
6.e: Bathing at the three Savanas, he shall offer libations to the gods and Pitṛs; and practising harsher and harsher austerities, he shall emaciate his body.

6.s: agnīnātmani vaitānān samāropya yathāvidhi anagniraniketaḥ syān munirmūlaphalāśanaḥ
6.d: अग्नीनात्मनि वैतानान् समारोप्य यथाविधि अनग्निरनिकेतः स्यान् मुनिर्मूलफलाशनः
6.e: Haying reposited, according to rule, the Śrauta Fires within himself, he shall be a silent hermit, without fires and without a house, living upon roots and fruits.

6.s: aprayatnaḥ sukhārtheṣu brahmacārī dharā ''śayaḥ śaraṇeṣvamamaścaiva vṛkṣamūlaniketanaḥ
6.d: अप्रयत्नः सुखार्थेषु ब्रह्मचारी धरा 'ऽशयः शरणेष्वममश्चैव वृक्षमूलनिकेतनः
6.e: Making no effort to obtain pleasure-giving objects, and maintaining celibacy, he shall sleep on the ground; and not caring for shelter, he shall have the roots of trees for his dwelling.

6.s: tāpaseṣveva vipreṣu yātrikaṃ bhaikṣamāharet gṛhamedhiṣu cānyeṣu dvijeṣu vanavāsiṣu
6.d: तापसेष्वेव विप्रेषु यात्रिकं भैक्षमाहरेत् गृहमेधिषु चान्येषु द्विजेषु वनवासिषु
6.e: He shall receive alms just enough for subsistence, only from brāhmaṇa-hermits, or from such twice-born householders as live in the forests.

6.s: grāmādāhṛtya vā 'śnīyādaṣṭau grāsān vane vasan pratigṛhya puṭenaiva pāṇinā śakalena vā
6.d: ग्रामादाहृत्य वा ऽश्नीयादष्टौ ग्रासान् वने वसन् प्रतिगृह्य पुटेनैव पाणिना शकलेन वा
6.e: While dwelling in the forest, he may bring food from the village,—receiving it either in his hollowed hand or in a potsherd,—and eat eight morsels.

6.s: etāścānyāśca seveta dīkṣā vipro vane vasan vividhāścaupaniṣadīrātmasaṃsiddhaye śrutīḥ
6.d: एताश्चान्याश्च सेवेत दीक्षा विप्रो वने वसन् विविधाश्चौपनिषदीरात्मसंसिद्धये श्रुतीः
6.e: The Brāhmaṇa dwelling in the forest shall attend to these and other restraints; and also to the several Vedic texts contained in the Upaniṣads, in order to attain the Self.

6.s: ṛṣibhirbrāhmaṇaiścaiva gṛhasthaireva sevitāḥ vidyātapovivṛddhyarthaṃ śarīrasya ca śuddhaye
6.d: ऋषिभिर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैव गृहस्थैरेव सेविताः विद्यातपोविवृद्ध्यर्थं शरीरस्य च शुद्धये
6.e: Such of these as have been attended to by sages and Brāhmaṇa householders, for the advancement of knowledge and austerities, and also for the purification of the body

6.s: aparājitāṃ vā 'sthāya vrajeddiśamajihmagaḥ ā nipātātśarīrasya yukto vārianilāśanaḥ
6.d: अपराजितां वा ऽस्थाय व्रजेद्दिशमजिह्मगः आ निपातात्शरीरस्य युक्तो वारिअनिलाशनः
6.e: Or, having fixed upon the North-Easterly direction, he shall go forward, moving straight on, intent and living upon water and air,—till the falling off of his body.

6.s: āsāṃ maharṣicaryāṇāṃ tyaktvā 'nyatamayā tanum vītaśokabhayo vipro brahmaloke mahīyate
6.d: आसां महर्षिचर्याणां त्यक्त्वा ऽन्यतमया तनुम् वीतशोकभयो विप्रो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते
6.e: Having discarded his body by one of these methods adopted by the Great Sages, the Brāhmaṇa, with sorrow and fear departed, becomes exalted in the region of Brahman.

6.s: vaneṣu ca vihṛtyaivaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bhāgamāyuṣaḥ caturthamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ tyakvā saṅgān parivrajet
6.d: वनेषु च विहृत्यैवं तृतीयं भागमायुषः चतुर्थमायुषो भागं त्यक्वा सङ्गान् परिव्रजेत्
6.e: Having thus passed the third part of his life in the forest, the man shall, during the fourth part, renounce all attachments and go forth (a wandering mendicant).

6.s: āśramādāśramaṃ gatvā hutahomo jitaindriyaḥ bhikṣābalipariśrāntaḥ pravrajan pretya vardhate
6.d: आश्रमादाश्रमं गत्वा हुतहोमो जितैन्द्रियः भिक्षाबलिपरिश्रान्तः प्रव्रजन् प्रेत्य वर्धते
6.e: If one, after passing from stage to stage and after offering the sacrifices, with senses subdued, tired of alms and offerings,—goes forth as a wandering mendicant, and then dies, then he prospers.

6.s: ṛṇāni trīṇyapākṛtya mano mokṣe niveśayet anapākṛtya mokṣaṃ tu sevamāno vrajatyadhaḥ
6.d: ऋणानि त्रीण्यपाकृत्य मनो मोक्षे निवेशयेत् अनपाकृत्य मोक्षं तु सेवमानो व्रजत्यधः
6.e: One shall turn his mind towards Liberation only after having paid off the three debts; without having paid them, if he seeks for Liberation, he sinks downwards.

6.s: adhītya vidhivadvedān putrāṃścautpādya dharmataḥ iṣṭvā ca śaktito yajñairmano mokṣe niveśayet
6.d: अधीत्य विधिवद्वेदान् पुत्रांश्चौत्पाद्य धर्मतः इष्ट्वा च शक्तितो यज्ञैर्मनो मोक्षे निवेशयेत्
6.e: After having studied the Vedas according to rule, having begotten sons in the rightful manner, and having offered sacrifices to the rest of his ability,—he shall turn his mind towards Liberation.

6.s: anadhītya dvijo vedānanutpādya tathā sutān tathā prajāṃ aniṣṭvā caiva yajñaiśca mokṣamicchan vrajatyadhaḥ
6.d: अनधीत्य द्विजो वेदाननुत्पाद्य तथा सुतान् तथा प्रजां अनिष्ट्वा चैव यज्ञैश्च मोक्षमिच्छन् व्रजत्यधः
6.e: The twice-born person, who seeks Liberation, without having studied the Vedas, without having begotten offspring, and without having offered sacrificis, sinks downwards.

6.s: prājāpatyaṃ nirupyaiṣṭiṃ sarvavedasadakṣiṇām sārvavedasadakṣiṇām ātmanyagnīn samāropya brāhmaṇaḥ pravrajedgṛhāt
6.d: प्राजापत्यं निरुप्यैष्टिं सर्ववेदसदक्षिणाम् सार्ववेदसदक्षिणाम् आत्मन्यग्नीन् समारोप्य ब्राह्मणः प्रव्रजेद्गृहात्
6.e: Having performed the Prājāpatya Sacrifice, wherein all his belongings are given away as the sacrificial fee,—and having reposited the Fires within himself,—the Brāhmaṇa should go forth from his house.

6.s: yo dattvā sarvabhūtebhyaḥ pravrajatyabhayaṃ gṛhāt tasya tejomayā lokā bhavanti brahmavādinaḥ
6.d: यो दत्त्वा सर्वभूतेभ्यः प्रव्रजत्यभयं गृहात् तस्य तेजोमया लोका भवन्ति ब्रह्मवादिनः
6.e: He who goes forth from home after having granted freedom from all fear to all beings,—to that expounder of the Veda belong regions of light.

6.s: yasmādaṇuapi bhūtānāṃ dvijānnautpadyate bhayam tasya dehādvimuktasya bhayaṃ nāsti kutaścana
6.d: यस्मादणुअपि भूतानां द्विजान्नौत्पद्यते भयम् तस्य देहाद्विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कुतश्चन
6.e: The twice-born person, from whom not the slightest danger arises to living beings, suffers no danger from any source, when he has become freed from his body.

6.s: agārādabhiniṣkrāntaḥ pavitraupacito muniḥ samupoḍheṣu kāmeṣu nir 'pekṣaḥ parivrajet
6.d: अगारादभिनिष्क्रान्तः पवित्रौपचितो मुनिः समुपोढेषु कामेषु निर् ऽपेक्षः परिव्रजेत्
6.e: Having departed from his house, fully equipped with the sacred things, he shall go forth, silent and wholly indifferent towards pleasures that may be presented to him.—(41.)

6.s: eka eva carennityaṃ siddhyarthamasahāyavān siddhimekasya saṃpaśyanna jahāti na hīyate siddham
6.d: एक एव चरेन्नित्यं सिद्ध्यर्थमसहायवान् सिद्धिमेकस्य संपश्यन्न जहाति न हीयते सिद्धम्
6.e: He shall always wander about alone, without a companion, in order to attain success; when one realises that success accrues to the solitary man, he neither forsakes nor becomes forsaken.

6.s: anagniraniketaḥ syādgrāmamannārthamāśrayet upekṣako 'saṅkusuko munirbhāvasamāhitaḥ 'sāṅkusuko
6.d: अनग्निरनिकेतः स्याद्ग्राममन्नार्थमाश्रयेत् उपेक्षको ऽसङ्कुसुको मुनिर्भावसमाहितः ऽसाङ्कुसुको
6.e: He shall be without fires and without home; he may go to a village for food;—disinterested, steady, silent and calmly-disposed.

6.s: kapālaṃ vṛkṣamūlāni kucelamasahāyatā kucailaṃ samatā caiva sarvasminnetatmuktasya lakṣaṇam
6.d: कपालं वृक्षमूलानि कुचेलमसहायता कुचैलं समता चैव सर्वस्मिन्नेतत्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम्
6.e: The potsherd, the roots of trees, coarse cloth, solitude, e quality towards all,—are the mark of the liberated man.

6.s: nābhinandeta maraṇaṃ nābhinandeta jīvitam kālameva pratīkṣeta nirveśaṃ bhṛtako yathā
6.d: नाभिनन्देत मरणं नाभिनन्देत जीवितम् कालमेव प्रतीक्षेत निर्वेशं भृतको यथा
6.e: He shall not rejoice at death; nor shall he rejoice at life; he shall await his time, just as the servant awaits the fulfilment of his contract

6.s: dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet satyapūtāṃ vadedvācaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret
6.d: दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत् पादं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिबेत् सत्यपूतां वदेद्वाचं मनःपूतं समाचरेत्
6.e: He shall place his foot sight-purified, drink water cloth-clarified, utter speech truth-sanctified and act with pure mind

6.s: ativādāṃstitikṣeta nāvamanyeta kaṃ cana na caimaṃ dehamāśritya vairaṃ kurvīta kena cit
6.d: अतिवादांस्तितिक्षेत नावमन्येत कं चन न चैमं देहमाश्रित्य वैरं कुर्वीत केन चित्
6.e: He shall patiently bear improper words, and shall not insult anyone; and he shall not make enmity with any one, for the sake of his present body

6.s: kruddhyantaṃ na pratikrudhyedākruṣṭaḥ kuśalaṃ vadet saptadvārāvakīrṇāṃ ca na vācamanṛtāṃ vadet
6.d: क्रुद्ध्यन्तं न प्रतिक्रुध्येदाक्रुष्टः कुशलं वदेत् सप्तद्वारावकीर्णां च न वाचमनृतां वदेत्
6.e: Towards an angry man he shall not retort in anger; when he is cursed, he shall pronounce a blessing; and he shall not utter an untrue word, spreading over the seven openings.

6.s: adhyātmaratirāsīno nir 'pekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ ātmanaiva sahāyena sukhārthī vicarediha
6.d: अध्यात्मरतिरासीनो निर् ऽपेक्षो निरामिषः आत्मनैव सहायेन सुखार्थी विचरेदिह
6.e: Centered in spirituality, disinterested, free from longings, with himself as his sole companion, he shall wander forth in the world, seeking bliss.

6.s: na cautpātanimittābhyāṃ na nakṣatrāṅgavidyayā nānuśāsanavādābhyāṃ bhikṣāṃ lipseta karhi cit
6.d: न चौत्पातनिमित्ताभ्यां न नक्षत्राङ्गविद्यया नानुशासनवादाभ्यां भिक्षां लिप्सेत कर्हि चित्
6.e: He shall never obtain alms either by means of prodigies and portents, or by means of the science of astrology and palmistry, or by means of counsel and discussion.

6.s: na tāpasairbrāhmaṇairvā vayobhirapi vā śvabhiḥ ākīrṇaṃ bhikṣukairvā 'nyairagāramupasaṃvrajet
6.d: न तापसैर्ब्राह्मणैर्वा वयोभिरपि वा श्वभिः आकीर्णं भिक्षुकैर्वा ऽन्यैरगारमुपसंव्रजेत्
6.e: He shall not go near a house that is filled by hermits, brāhmaṇas, birds, dogs or other mendicants

6.s: kḷptakeśanakhaśmaśruḥ pātrī daṇḍī kusumbhavān vicarenniyato nityaṃ sarvabhūtānyapīḍayan
6.d: कॢप्तकेशनखश्मश्रुः पात्री दण्डी कुसुम्भवान् विचरेन्नियतो नित्यं सर्वभूतान्यपीडयन्
6.e: His hair, nails and beard clipped, equipped with vessels, staffs and water-pot, he shall constantly wander about, self-controlled and not causing pain to any living brings.

6.s: ataijasāni pātrāṇi tasya syurnirvraṇāni ca teṣāmadbhiḥ smṛtaṃ śaucaṃ camasānāmivādhvare
6.d: अतैजसानि पात्राणि तस्य स्युर्निर्व्रणानि च तेषामद्भिः स्मृतं शौचं चमसानामिवाध्वरे
6.e: His vessels shall be non-metallic and free from holes; the cleansing of there has been ordained to be done by water, just like that of the vessels at a sacrifice.

6.s: alābuṃ dārupātraṃ ca mṛṇmayaṃ vaidalaṃ tathā etāṇi yatipātrāṇi manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt
6.d: अलाबुं दारुपात्रं च मृण्मयं वैदलं तथा एताणि यतिपात्राणि मनुः स्वायंभुवो ऽब्रवीत्
6.e: Manu, the son of Svayambhu, has declared that the vessels of the renunciate shall be a gourd, a vessel of wood or of earthenware, or of splits.

6.s: ekakālaṃ caredbhaikṣaṃ na prasajjeta vistare bhaikṣe prasakto hi yatirviṣayeṣvapi sajjati
6.d: एककालं चरेद्भैक्षं न प्रसज्जेत विस्तरे भैक्षे प्रसक्तो हि यतिर्विषयेष्वपि सज्जति
6.e: He shall go for alms only once, and shall not seek for a large quantity; because the renunciate who becomes addicted to collecting alms becomes attached to sensual objects also.

6.s: vidhūme sannamusale vy 'ṅgāre bhuktavajjane vṛtte śarāvasaṃpāte bhikṣāṃ nityaṃ yatiścaret
6.d: विधूमे सन्नमुसले व्य् ऽङ्गारे भुक्तवज्जने वृत्ते शरावसंपाते भिक्षां नित्यं यतिश्चरेत्
6.e: The renunciate shall go for begging alms at a time when there is no smoke issuing, when the pestle has ceased to ply, when fire embers have been extinguished, when people have eaten, and when the removal of the dishes has been finished.

6.s: alābhe na viṣadī syātlābhe caiva na harṣayet prāṇayātrikamātraḥ syātmātrāsaṅgādvinirgataḥ
6.d: अलाभे न विषदी स्यात्लाभे चैव न हर्षयेत् प्राणयात्रिकमात्रः स्यात्मात्रासङ्गाद्विनिर्गतः
6.e: He shall not be sorry at not obtaining alms; nor shall he rejoice at obtaining it; he shall have only what suffices to sustain his life, and be free from all attachment to his accessories.

6.s: abhipūjitalābhāṃstu jugupsetaiva sarvaśaḥ abhipūjitalābhaiśca yatirmukto 'pi badhyate
6.d: अभिपूजितलाभांस्तु जुगुप्सेतैव सर्वशः अभिपूजितलाभैश्च यतिर्मुक्तो ऽपि बध्यते
6.e: He shall disdain all honorific presents; by honorific presents the Renunciate, even though liberated, becomes fettered

6.s: alpānnābhyavahāreṇa rahaḥsthānāsanena ca hriyamāṇāni viṣayairindriyāṇi nivartayet
6.d: अल्पान्नाभ्यवहारेण रहःस्थानासनेन च ह्रियमाणानि विषयैरिन्द्रियाणि निवर्तयेत्
6.e: By eating little food and by standing and sitting in solitude, he shall restrain his senses, when attracted by sensual objects.

6.s: indriyāṇāṃ nirodhena rāgadveśakṣayeṇa ca ahiṃsayā ca bhūtānāmamṛtatvāya kalpate
6.d: इन्द्रियाणां निरोधेन रागद्वेशक्षयेण च अहिंसया च भूतानाममृतत्वाय कल्पते
6.e: By the restraining of the senses, by the destruction of love and hatred, and by not injuring living beings, he becomes fit for immortality.

6.s: avekṣeta gatīrnr̥̄ṇāṃ karmadoṣasamudbhavāḥ niraye caiva patanaṃ yātanāśca yamakṣaye
6.d: अवेक्षेत गतीर्न्र्̥̄णां कर्मदोषसमुद्भवाः निरये चैव पतनं यातनाश्च यमक्षये
6.e: He should reflect upon the conditions of men, arising from the defects of their deeds, their falling into hell and their sufferings in the abode of the death-god.

6.s: viprayogaṃ priyaiścaiva saṃyogaṃ ca tathā 'priyaiḥ jarayā cābhibhavanaṃ vyādhibhiścaupapīḍanam
6.d: विप्रयोगं प्रियैश्चैव संयोगं च तथा ऽप्रियैः जरया चाभिभवनं व्याधिभिश्चौपपीडनम्
6.e: On the separation of loved ones and the meeting of hated persons; on being beset with decrepitude and suffering from diseases.

6.s: dehādutkramaṇaṃ cāṣmāt punargarbhe ca saṃbhavam yonikoṭisahasreṣu sṛtīścāsyāntarātmanaḥ
6.d: देहादुत्क्रमणं चाष्मात् पुनर्गर्भे च संभवम् योनिकोटिसहस्रेषु सृतीश्चास्यान्तरात्मनः
6.e: There is for his Inner Soul departure from the body, then again birth in the womb, and transmigrations among millions of life-forms.

6.s: adharmaprabhavaṃ caiva duḥkhayogaṃ śarīriṇām dharmārthaprabhavaṃ caiva sukhasaṃyogamakṣayam
6.d: अधर्मप्रभवं चैव दुःखयोगं शरीरिणाम् धर्मार्थप्रभवं चैव सुखसंयोगमक्षयम्
6.e: On the infliction of pain upon living beings, caused by demerit; as also upon the imperishable union with happiness proceeding from the essence of merit.

6.s: sūkṣmatāṃ cānvavekṣeta yogena paramātmanaḥ deheṣu ca samutpattimuttameṣvadhameṣu ca deheṣu caivopapattim
6.d: सूक्ष्मतां चान्ववेक्षेत योगेन परमात्मनः देहेषु च समुत्पत्तिमुत्तमेष्वधमेषु च देहेषु चैवोपपत्तिम्
6.e: By meditation he shall recognise the subtile character of the Higher Self, as also the possibility of its presence in all organisms, high and low.

6.s: dūṣito 'pi careddharmaṃ yatra tatrāśrame rataḥ bhūṣito 'pi samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu na liṅgaṃ dharmakāraṇam
6.d: दूषितो ऽपि चरेद्धर्मं यत्र तत्राश्रमे रतः भूषितो ऽपि समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु न लिङ्गं धर्मकारणम्
6.e: Even though he be adorned, the man should fulfil his duty, to whichever order he may belong. He should be equal to all beings; mere external marks are not conducive to merit.

6.s: phalaṃ katakavṛkṣasya yadyapyambuprasādakam na nāmagrahaṇādeva tasya vāri prasīdati
6.d: फलं कतकवृक्षस्य यद्यप्यम्बुप्रसादकम् न नामग्रहणादेव तस्य वारि प्रसीदति
6.e: Though the fruit of the Kataka tree clarifies water, yet water does not become clear by the mere mention of its name.

6.s: saṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ jantūnāṃ rātrāvahani vā sadā śarīrasyātyaye caiva samīkṣya vasudhāṃ caret
6.d: संरक्षणार्थं जन्तूनां रात्रावहनि वा सदा शरीरस्यात्यये चैव समीक्ष्य वसुधां चरेत्
6.e: With a view to the safety of living beings, he shall always, during day and night, even during bodily illness, walk after having scanned the ground.

6.s: ahnā rātryā ca yāñjantūn hinastyajñānato yatiḥ teṣāṃ snātvā viśuddhyarthaṃ prāṇāyāmān ṣaḍācaret
6.d: अह्ना रात्र्या च याञ्जन्तून् हिनस्त्यज्ञानतो यतिः तेषां स्नात्वा विशुद्ध्यर्थं प्राणायामान् षडाचरेत्
6.e: By day and by night, if the Renunciate unintentionally injures some living creatures, he shall, for the purpose of expiating it, bathe and then perform six ‘breath-suspensions.’

6.s: prāṇāyāmā brāhmaṇasya trayo 'pi vidhivat kṛtāḥ vyāhṛtipraṇavairyuktā vijñeyaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ
6.d: प्राणायामा ब्राह्मणस्य त्रयो ऽपि विधिवत् कृताः व्याहृतिप्रणवैर्युक्ता विज्ञेयं परमं तपः
6.e: Even three ‘breath-suspensions,’ accompanied by the three ‘vyāhṛti’-syllables and the syllable ‘om’, when duly performed, should be regarded as the highest austerity for the Brāhmaṇa.

6.s: dahyante dhmāyamānānāṃ dhātūnāṃ hi yathā malāḥ tathaindriyāṇāṃ dahyante doṣāḥ prāṇasya nigrahāt
6.d: दह्यन्ते ध्मायमानानां धातूनां हि यथा मलाः तथैन्द्रियाणां दह्यन्ते दोषाः प्राणस्य निग्रहात्
6.e: Just as the impurities of metallic ores are consumed when they are blasted, even so are the taints of the senses consumed through the suspension of breath.

6.s: prāṇāyamairdaheddoṣān dhāraṇābhiśca kilbiṣam pratyāhāreṇa saṃsargān dhyānenānīśvarān guṇān
6.d: प्राणायमैर्दहेद्दोषान् धारणाभिश्च किल्बिषम् प्रत्याहारेण संसर्गान् ध्यानेनानीश्वरान् गुणान्
6.e: By means of ‘Breath-suspension’ he shall destroy the taints; and by means of ‘Concentration,’ all sin; all attachments by means of ‘Abstraction,’ and by means of ‘Contemplation,’ those attributes that are not independent.

6.s: uccāvaceṣu bhūteṣu durjñeyāmakṛtātmabhiḥ dhyānayogena saṃpaśyedgatimasyāntarātmanaḥ
6.d: उच्चावचेषु भूतेषु दुर्ज्ञेयामकृतात्मभिः ध्यानयोगेन संपश्येद्गतिमस्यान्तरात्मनः
6.e: By the practice of meditation he shall recognise the presence of this Inner Soul in all beings, high and low,—which is difficult to understand by unregenerate people.

6.s: samyagdarśanasaṃpannaḥ karmabhirna nibadhyate darśanena vihīnastu saṃsāraṃ pratipadyate
6.d: सम्यग्दर्शनसंपन्नः कर्मभिर्न निबध्यते दर्शनेन विहीनस्तु संसारं प्रतिपद्यते
6.e: Equipped with true insight, he is no longer fettered by his acts; but destitute of insight, he falls into the cycle of births and deaths.

6.s: ahiṃsayaindriyāsaṅgairvaidikaiścaiva karmabhiḥ tapasaścaraṇaiścaugraiḥ sādhayantīha tatpadam
6.d: अहिंसयैन्द्रियासङ्गैर्वैदिकैश्चैव कर्मभिः तपसश्चरणैश्चौग्रैः साधयन्तीह तत्पदम्
6.e: By abstention from injuring, by the non-attachment of the senses, by the acts prescribed in the Veda, by the rigorous practising of austerities, they attain the position of That Being.

6.s: asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanam carmāvanaddhaṃ durgandhi pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ
6.d: अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनम् चर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धि पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषयोः
6.e: He shall discard this abode of material substances, where the bones are the pillars, which is held together by the tendons, plastered with flesh and blood; covered with the skin, foul-smelling, and full of urine and ordure;—(76) beset with wrinkles and sorrow, the seat of disease, harassed, sullied with passions and perishable.

6.s: jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanamāturam rajasvalamanityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsamimaṃ tyajet
6.d: जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमातुरम् रजस्वलमनित्यं च भूतावासमिमं त्यजेत्
6.e: He shall discard this abode of material substances, where the bones are the pillars, which is held together by the tendons, plastered with flesh and blood; covered with the skin, foul-smelling, and full of urine and ordure;—(76) beset with wrinkles and sorrow, the seat of disease, harassed, sullied with passions and perishable.

6.s: nadīkūlaṃ yathā vṛkṣo vṛkṣaṃ vā śakuniryathā tathā tyajannimaṃ dehaṃ kṛcchrādgrāhādvimucyate
6.d: नदीकूलं यथा वृक्षो वृक्षं वा शकुनिर्यथा तथा त्यजन्निमं देहं कृच्छ्राद्ग्राहाद्विमुच्यते
6.e: He, who leaves this body, either as the tree leaves the bank, or as the bird leaves the tree, becomes freed from the shark of misery.—(78.)

6.s: priyeṣu sveṣu sukṛtamapriyeṣu ca duṣkṛtam visṛjya dhyānayogena brahmābhyeti sanātanam
6.d: प्रियेषु स्वेषु सुकृतमप्रियेषु च दुष्कृतम् विसृज्य ध्यानयोगेन ब्रह्माभ्येति सनातनम्
6.e: Having, by the practice of meditation, attributed what is agreeable to him, to his good acts, and what is disagreeable, to his evil acts, he reaches the eternal Brahman.

6.s: yadā bhāvena bhavati sarvabhāveṣu niḥspṛhaḥ tadā sukhamavāpnoti pretya caiha ca śāśvatam
6.d: यदा भावेन भवति सर्वभावेषु निःस्पृहः तदा सुखमवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चैह च शाश्वतम्
6.e: When, by disposition, he becomes free from longing for all things, then he obtains lasting happiness in this world, as also after death.

6.s: anena vidhinā sarvāṃstyaktvā saṅgāṃśanaiḥ śanaiḥ sarvadvandvavinirmukto brahmaṇyevāvatiṣṭhate
6.d: अनेन विधिना सर्वांस्त्यक्त्वा सङ्गांशनैः शनैः सर्वद्वन्द्वविनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मण्येवावतिष्ठते
6.e: Having, in this manner, gradually renounced all attachments, he becomes freed from all pairs of opposites, and reposes in Brahman alone.

6.s: dhyānikaṃ sarvamevaitadyadetadabhiśabditam na hyanadhyātmavit kaścit kriyāphalamupāśnute
6.d: ध्यानिकं सर्वमेवैतद्यदेतदभिशब्दितम् न ह्यनध्यात्मवित् कश्चित् क्रियाफलमुपाश्नुते
6.e: All this that has been declared here is appurtenant to Meditation; he who does not realise and cultivate the said mental attitude does not obtain the reward of the acts.

6.s: adhiyajñaṃ brahma japedādhidaivikameva ca ādhyātmikaṃ ca satataṃ vedāntābhihitaṃ ca yat
6.d: अधियज्ञं ब्रह्म जपेदाधिदैविकमेव च आध्यात्मिकं च सततं वेदान्ताभिहितं च यत्
6.e: He shall constantly recite Vedic texts bearing upon sacrifices, those dealing with deities and those dealing with the Soul, which have been called ‘Vedānta.’

6.s: idaṃ śaraṇamajñānāmidameva vijānatām idamanvicchatāṃ svargamidamānantyamicchatām
6.d: इदं शरणमज्ञानामिदमेव विजानताम् इदमन्विच्छतां स्वर्गमिदमानन्त्यमिच्छताम्
6.e: This is the refuge for the ignorant, this for the learned; this for those seeking heaven, and this also for those desiring immortality.

6.s: anena kramayogena parivrajati yo dvijaḥ sa vidhūyaiha pāpmānaṃ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati
6.d: अनेन क्रमयोगेन परिव्रजति यो द्विजः स विधूयैह पाप्मानं परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति
6.e: The twice-born person, who, by this successive process, goes forth (as a mendicant), shakes off evil and attains the Supreme Brahman.

6.s: eṣa dharmo 'nuśiṣṭo vo yatīnāṃ niyatātmanām vedasaṃnyāsikānāṃ tu karmayogaṃ nibodhata
6.d: एष धर्मो ऽनुशिष्टो वो यतीनां नियतात्मनाम् वेदसंन्यासिकानां तु कर्मयोगं निबोधत
6.e: Thus have the duties of the self-controlled Renunciates been expounded to you. Listen now to the duties of the ‘renouncers of the Veda.’

6.s: brahmacārī gṛhasthaśca vānaprastho yatistathā ete gṛhasthaprabhavāścatvāraḥ pṛthagāśramāḥ
6.d: ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थश्च वानप्रस्थो यतिस्तथा एते गृहस्थप्रभवाश्चत्वारः पृथगाश्रमाः
6.e: The student, the Householder, the Hermit and the Renunciate,—all these, several stages emanate from the Householder.—(87). But all these, when observed in due order, a ccording to the scriptures lead the Brāhmaṇa who has (thus) acted according to the law, to the highest state.

6.s: sarve 'pi kramaśastvete yathāśāstraṃ niṣevitāḥ yathauktakāriṇaṃ vipraṃ nayanti paramāṃ gatim
6.d: सर्वे ऽपि क्रमशस्त्वेते यथाशास्त्रं निषेविताः यथौक्तकारिणं विप्रं नयन्ति परमां गतिम्
6.e: The student, the Householder, the Hermit and the Renunciate,—all these, several stages emanate from the Householder.—(87). But all these, when observed in due order, a ccording to the scriptures lead the Brāhmaṇa who has (thus) acted according to the law, to the highest state.

6.s: sarveṣāmapi caiteṣāṃ vedasmṛtividhānataḥ vedaśrutividhānataḥ gṛhastha ucyate śreṣṭhaḥ sa trīnetān bibharti hi
6.d: सर्वेषामपि चैतेषां वेदस्मृतिविधानतः वेदश्रुतिविधानतः गृहस्थ उच्यते श्रेष्ठः स त्रीनेतान् बिभर्ति हि
6.e: Among all these however, in accordance with the injunction or the direct Vedic text, the Householder is declared to be the best; because he supports the other three.

6.s: yathā nadīnadāḥ sarve sāgare yānti saṃsthitim tathaivāśramiṇaḥ sarve gṛhasthe yānti saṃsthitim
6.d: यथा नदीनदाः सर्वे सागरे यान्ति संस्थितिम् तथैवाश्रमिणः सर्वे गृहस्थे यान्ति संस्थितिम्
6.e: Just as rivers and rivulets attain their resting-places in the Ocean, so do men of all other orders obtain support in the Householder.

6.s: caturbhirapi caivaitairnityamāśramibhirdvijaiḥ daśalakṣaṇako dharmaḥ sevitavyaḥ prayatnataḥ
6.d: चतुर्भिरपि चैवैतैर्नित्यमाश्रमिभिर्द्विजैः दशलक्षणको धर्मः सेवितव्यः प्रयत्नतः
6.e: By twice-born men belonging to all these four orders this ten-fold duty shall always be assiduously observed.

6.s: dhṛtiḥ kṣamā damo 'steyaṃ śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ dhīrvidyā satyamakrodho daśakaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam
6.d: धृतिः क्षमा दमो ऽस्तेयं शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः धीर्विद्या सत्यमक्रोधो दशकं धर्मलक्षणम्
6.e: (1) Steadiness (2) Forgiveness, (3) Self-control, (4) Abstention from unrighteous appropriation, (5) Purity, (6) Control of the Sense-organs, (7) Discrimination, (8) Knowledge, (9) Truthfulness, and (10) Absence of anger,—these are the ten-fold forms of duty.

6.s: daśa lakṣaṇāni dharmasya ye viprāḥ samadhīyate adhītya cānuvartante te yānti paramāṃ gatim
6.d: दश लक्षणानि धर्मस्य ये विप्राः समधीयते अधीत्य चानुवर्तन्ते ते यान्ति परमां गतिम्
6.e: Those Brāhmaṇas, who properly study the ten forms of duty, and having studied them, follow them in practice, reach the highest state.

6.s: daśalakṣaṇakaṃ dharmamanutiṣṭhan samāhitaḥ vedāntaṃ vidhivatśrutvā saṃnyasedanṛṇo dvijaḥ
6.d: दशलक्षणकं धर्ममनुतिष्ठन् समाहितः वेदान्तं विधिवत्श्रुत्वा संन्यसेदनृणो द्विजः
6.e: The twice-born person, performing, with collected mind, the ten-fold Duty, and having duly learnt the Vedānta texts, and become free from debts, should take to Renunciation.

6.s: saṃnyasya sarvakarmāṇi karmadoṣānapānudan niyato vedamabhyasya putraiśvarye sukhaṃ vaset
6.d: संन्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि कर्मदोषानपानुदन् नियतो वेदमभ्यस्य पुत्रैश्वर्ये सुखं वसेत्
6.e: Having renounced all acts, and thrown off the taint of his acts, and studied the Veda with mind self-oontrolled, he shall live at ease under the protection of his son.

6.s: evaṃ saṃnyasya karmāṇi svakāryaparamo 'spṛhaḥ saṃnyāsenāpahatyainaḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ gatim
6.d: एवं संन्यस्य कर्माणि स्वकार्यपरमो ऽस्पृहः संन्यासेनापहत्यैनः प्राप्नोति परमं गतिम्
6.e: Having thus renounced all rites, intent upon his own duty, free from longings, he destroys sin by his renunciation and attains the highest state.

6.s: eṣa vo 'bhihito dharmo brāhmaṇasya caturvidhaḥ puṇyo 'kṣayaphalaḥ pretya rājñāṃ dharmaṃ nibodhata
6.d: एष वो ऽभिहितो धर्मो ब्राह्मणस्य चतुर्विधः पुण्यो ऽक्षयफलः प्रेत्य राज्ञां धर्मं निबोधत
